This is the first Thiru-pathigam composed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal.

Now, the second Thiru-pathigam. This is a Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-pathigam, compiled as the forty-seventh Thiru-pathigam in the sixth Thiru-Murai.

Now, that Thiru-pathigam: Thiruchitrambalam. Thiruve En Selvamay Thenay Vaanor Sezhunjudaray Sezhunjudar Narsothimikka Uruve En Urave En Oonay Oonin Ullamay Ullaththin Ullay Nindra Karuve En Karpagamay Kannay Kannil Karumaniyay Maniyaadu Paavaay Kaavaay Aruvaaya Valvinai Noy Adaiyaavannam Aavaduthan Thurai Urayum Amarar Eray Maatraen Ezhuthanjum Endra Naavin Maravaen Thiruvarulgal Vanja Nenjin Etraen Pira Deyvam Enna Na My dog-like self, if I do not contemplate Thiru-Erumaan’s holy feet, and seeing the deeds you perform, I give way to suffering day after day, I cannot bear it. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! O partner of the slender-waisted maiden, O Lord of the Ganga, O Lord with matted locks, if I were to die without uttering your name, what would it matter if I were afflicted by any terrible disease? To the devotees who, melting with thought, with overflowing tears, lovingly praise your ocean-like self, do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! O Lord who bent the bow to burn the three cities, making Uma Devi fear, and who, joyfully placing his hand on the great elephant, flayed it, O Kankala, our King!

The people of this earth will not bear it day after day. O Lord who protects life, I am not pressing you. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! Having plucked fresh flowers, bathed in water, and praised and glorified your feet daily, I have cast off sorrows that cannot be cast off. What if the karma of the world comes upon me? O Lord who, becoming a kinsman, drank the poison from the roaring ocean to save the celestials, do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai!

O Lord who, taking the form of Narayana, held his head in his hand, covered himself with the skin of a dead elephant, and wandered everywhere as a Kankala hunter! Who am I to you, a destroyer of karma? You are the origin of all good and bad deeds. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! O Lord who flayed the skin O Lord whose garment is the flayed skin! O Lord of Uma Devi!

O Lord of the celestials! O Lord of Kailasa, who drank the poison from the dark ocean! It is your duty, O Great One, to forgive the faults of your devotees. Is not great compassion yours? O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai, where peacocks dance in the groves! O Beloved One who captivates the hearts of those who love you, O Lord who wanders, begging for alms from the celestials, holding a skull in your hand!

O Lord with the dancing hand! Alas, truly, I have wandered day after day, immersed in the delusion of birth, a body filled with impurities. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! O Lord who holds many white skulls in his hand, who rides a bull, and begs for alms from town to town! O Lord of the stony mountain You and all will depart. If you do not consider those who dance in the cremation ground, everyone will surely despise me.

I have abandoned the ignorant Jains and Buddhists. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! I have not walked the pure path of the renunciates, nor am I pure enough to offer garlands. All the days I have not spoken of your holy grace are days I have not been born. I know all the deeds you performed when you crushed the king of Lanka, whose city was fortified. Do not say, “Fear not,” to this servant, O Lord of the Immortals who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai!

This is the third of the four Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal for Thiru-Aavaduthurai, that is, the third of the four Thiru-Pathikams composed at this time. The Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam is the twenty-ninth Thiru-Pathikam in the fifth Thiru-Murai.

Now, that Thiru-Pathikam.

“Niraikka vaaliyal allalin nerizhai maraikkavaaliyal allali maadharaal piraikkavaala perumpunal aavaduthurai kavaaliyodaadiya sunname thavalamaadhi saayaloor chandiran pilavusoodiya pingyagan emmirai alavukandila aavaduthurai kalavu kandanal otthanal kanniye paadhi pennoru paagaththin panmarai odhi en nuzham kondavan on porul aadhi aavaduthurai meviya sodhiye sudare” — She is not able to fill, nor is she able to conceal her distress, the maiden. The great flood of Thiru-Aavaduthurai, where the Lord danced with the skull, is like the white moon. He wears the crescent moon, a fiery one, our Lord. She has not seen the measure of Thiru-Aavaduthurai. She has seen the theft, as if she were a virgin.

He who holds half a woman in his body, who recites many Vedas, who has taken my soul, the unique primal being, the light that resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai, the flame, she says. He whose throat is like a dark cloud, she is filled with pride, thinking of him, the one with the Konrai flower, Thiru-Aavaduthurai. She stands for him, and her feet are not seen. He whose throat is dark, whose light is like the fierce sun, he is like the nectar of milk. She went near him and cried, “O Lord of Thiru-Aavaduthurai, my only Lord!” He who holds the flute, the Konrai, the skull, and the maiden as part of his body. “Is he not the beautiful one of Thiru-Aavaduthurai?” she says, her bangles slipping from her hands.

She, with her soft feet like cotton, who has him as her refuge, is not afraid of anyone. This is the madness she has with the Lord of Thiru-Aavaduthurai. He who wears the crescent moon, who is both male and female, who has a full heart and purity.

The Lord of Thiru-Aavaduthurai, with its fragrant groves, my Lord, he thinks of me. He who measured the earth and Brahma, when they sought to see the truth, became a pillar of fire. O Lord of Thiru-Aavaduthurai, my Lord, the white bangles on my hand are slipping off. He who begs for alms while ghosts sing, he who destroyed the strength of the mighty Ravana. See him, the naked one, who wears bones, in Thiru-Aavaduthurai, the shameless one!

This Thiru-Pathikam is presented as the words of a mother describing the state of her daughter, who, having seen the Lord, is infatuated and has lost her self-control. This Thiru-Pathikam is set in the Akapporul (love poetry) genre. If we remember that the essence of this site is the removal of the animalistic nature of souls, and contemplate this Thiru-Pathikam, we can attain great bliss.

Next, the fourth Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal. The fourth Thiru-Pathikam, Thiru-Ner-Isai Thiru-Pathikam, is the fifty-seventh Thiru-Pathikam in the fourth Thiru-Murai.

“Manjanai maniyum aanai maragatha thirulumaanai nenjule pugundhu nindru ninai tharu nigazhvinaanai thunjumbodhaaga vandhu thunaiyanakku aagi nindru anjal endru arula vendum aavaduthuraiyulane” — You are the dark one, the jewel, the emerald cluster. You entered my heart and stood there, becoming the one who brings forth thoughts. When I am about to die, please come and be my companion, stand by me, and say, “Fear not,” O Lord who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! “Naan ugandhu unnai naalum nanuguma karuthiyeyum oon ugandhu oombum naayen ullura aivar nindrar thaan ugandhe yugandha thagavilaa thondane naan aan ugandhu eruvaane aavaduthuraiyulane” — Even though I desire to approach you daily, I am a dog-like being who cherishes the flesh, and five senses reside within me. I am an unworthy servant who loves what you love.

O Lord who rides the bull, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! “Kattame vinaigalaana kaaththivai nokki aalaai ottave otti naalum unnai ul vaikkamaatten pattavaan thalai kaiyendhi pazhi thirindhu oorgalthorum attamaa uruvinaanai aavaduthuraiyula” — My karmas are a burden. I cannot keep you in my heart daily, even if I try to embrace you. O Lord who holds a skull in his hand, who wanders from town to town, who has eight forms, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! I cannot speak of the greatness of Thillai. I cannot ascend to heaven by contemplating you with a single mind.

I am cleansing the body that has been darkened. O Lord who drank the rare poison, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! I am a wicked one, caught in the whirlpool of karma. Protect me from the five senses that come to disturb me. O Lord who joyfully holds the fragrant garlanded maiden in one part of his body, who wears the eight great serpents, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! O Lord whose throat is like dark fire, who burned the three fortresses with a single fiery arrow, who has fire in his matted locks, you remove the karmas of those who remember you.

O Lord who dances holding the six fires, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! I am not firm in my mind, I cannot perceive the holy feet of Shiva. I have no goal, no good qualities, I cannot speak of them. I have no righteous path, I cannot think of you. I am ignorant, I have forgotten. O Lord who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai!

I cannot understand the beautiful form you took with the beautiful maiden. My deeds have covered me. Grant me that I may not suffer in this great world. O Lord who drank the poison from the great banyan tree, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai! The tall one and Brahma searched on both sides, but they could not speak of the form you took, a fierce form, a pillar of fire. O Lord who resides in my heart, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai!

When the demon went to the mountain, Uma Devi feared. He lifted it with his hands above his head. You pressed him with your immeasurable toe and granted him boons. O Lord who wears the agitated great Ganga, who resides in Thiru-Aavaduthurai!

These four Thiru-Pathikams were composed by Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal. These are the Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal after reaching Thiru-Aavaduthurai and worshipping the Lord. Sivakavimani Ayya writes that the fifth Thiru-Pathikam for this site, the Thiru-Ner-Isai Thiru-Pathikam called “Mayooru Gnanam,” was composed later.

Let us resume our contemplation.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 121 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 383, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Thiru-Aavaduthurai, continues his pilgrimage to the Ponni Nadu Thiru-Thalaiyathirai.

The Lord sings as follows in his Thiru-Thalaiyathirai: “Eri punal pon mani sidharum thirai neer ponni idai maruthai sendru eythi anbinodu mari viravu karaththaarai vanangi vaiki van tamil paamaalai pala magizhchchaaththi poriyaravam punaindhaarai thiru naagechuraththu potri arunthamil maalai punaindhu poandhu serivirai nan malarcholai pazhaiyaaru eythi thiru chaththi muttraththai sendru serndhaar” — Having reached Thiru-Idai-Maruthu, where the waves of the Ponni scatter fire, gold, and jewels, and having worshipped with love the Lord who holds a deer in his hand, he stayed there and joyfully offered many garlands of rich Tamil verses. Having praised the Lord who wears a serpent in Thiru-Nageswaram and offered a garland of rare Tamil verses, he proceeded to Pazhaiyaru, a grove of fragrant flowers, and reached Thiru-Chaththi-Mutram.

Thus sings Sekkizhar Peruman. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Thiru-Aavaduthurai He goes to the holy site of Thiru-Idai-Maruthur and worships there.

After that, he reaches the holy site of Thiru-Nageswaram, sings Thiru-Pathikams there, then goes to the holy site of Pazhaiyaru, sings Thiru-Pathikams there, and then reaches the holy site of Thiru-Chaththi-Mutram. Sekkizhar Peruman sings this in one verse. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman goes to the holy site of Thiru-Idai-Maruthur. In the holy site of Thiru-Idai-Maruthur, the Lord’s holy name is Maruthavanar Mahalingeswarar. The Goddess’s holy name is Pirakat Sundara Kujambikai Perunala Mulai Ammai. The Sthala Vriksham is the Marutha tree.

In this holy site, eleven Rudras, on the night of the great dissolution when all living beings merged, came and worshipped and attained Shiva-Peru.

Furthermore, the Mahalinga Peruman resides in this holy site. The Vinayagar of this holy site resides in Thiru-Valanchuzhi, Muruga-Kadavul in Swamimalai, Chandikeswara Nayanar in Thiru-Vaipadi, Surya and other Navagrahas in Suryanar Koil, Nataraja Peruman in Thiruchitrambalam, Bhairava-Kadavul in Sirkazhi, Nandi Devar in Thiru-Aavaduthurai, Somasakandar in Thiruvarur, and Dakshinamurthy in Thiru-Alangudi and Thiru-Irumpoolai temples. The Mahalinga Peruman in Thiru-Idai-Maruthur, like a central jewel in the sanctum sanctorum, is surrounded by these subsidiary temples.

Therefore, this is a very great holy site. Shiva Peruman showed the sages in this town the greatness of Uma Devi meditating on the Lord in her heart-lotus. Shiva Peruman appeared and gave darshan to the sages in the midst of a grove of Marutha trees to bless the sage Romasa, according to the Puranic history. This holy site has twelve holy names: Shanpakaranayam, Sakthipuram, Vilvavanam, Thapovanam, Jothipuram, Sarvatheerthapuram, Selva Viruththipuram, Dharma Viruththipuram, Mukthipuram, Idaimaruthu, Veeracholapuram, and Pooloka Sivalokam. The Puranic history states that Veeracholan reached this holy site, worshipped, cleared the forests, cultivated the land, and performed many temple renovations.

Therefore, this holy site is called Veeracholapuram. The Veeracholan river flowing north of this holy site confirms this. Ancient texts such as Kanda Puranam, Linga Puranam, Brahma Kaivartha Puranam, and Sivaragasyam have glorified this holy site of Thiru-Idai-Maruthur. They speak. If we consider Manikkavasagar’s words in Thiruvasagam, “Ananda Thenirundha Pondhai” (the pot containing the honey of bliss) in reference to the Lord of Idaimaruthu, the antiquity of this site will be well understood. The great sages, by the command of Agastya Muni, began to meditate on Uma.

They obtained the knowledge of the Vedas and Agamas and the materials for Shiva worship through the grace of Namagal and Thirumagal, and began to strive for their primary goal of spiritual progress. Just as a child comes to know the father through the mother, the sages also began to meditate, seeking the grace of Shakti. Shakti is very fond of groves filled with Champaka flowers. Knowing this, the sages began to meditate in a Champaka grove here. They began to meditate there.

The Lord has the nature of quickly reaching the heart-lotus of those who remember Him with love. The Goddess also has this nature.

Therefore, the Goddess appeared and blessed the great sages. The great sages prayed to the Goddess, saying, “Mother, we desire to attain the Father.” Immediately, the Goddess, contemplating the Lord in her heart-lotus, performed Shiva Yoga in a state of silence. The great sages served the Goddess and performed penance. In this state, as the Goddess had wished in her heart, the Lord appeared as a luminous form, as Mahalinga Murthy, as Jyotir Mahalinga, and blessed the sages with His vision. All the sages, unable to behold the luminous Lord, were bewildered, but by the grace of the Goddess, they beheld Him and attained great bliss. In the state where the Lord appeared and blessed the great sages, He became Ekanayagan.

He manifested. Not only that, but in the very state in which He appeared, He Himself explained to souls the method of performing Shiva Puja and the benefits attained by those who worship. This holy site is bounded by Panapuram to the east, Thiru-Neelakudi to the south, Thiru-Bhuvanam to the west, and the Kaveri River to the north. The holy waters located in this site are as follows: Karunyamirtha Theertham, which is the most excellent of all holy waters. By bathing in it during the auspicious time of Chithirai Vishu, one can attain great merit. Next is Pana Theertham, located in Panapuram, which forms the eastern boundary of this site.

This is a holy water created by Sri Rama. Bathing in it during Vaikasi Pournami is considered special. Next is Parasara Theertham. This holy water is believed to be the Pidari Kulam located at the intersection of the north and east streets. Bathing in it during the month of Margazhi is special. The Sthala Puranam states that Parasara Muni, following the advice of Romasa Muni, bathed in this Theertham and was cleansed of the impurity of having been with Machagandhi.

Next is Soma Theertham, which is located to the east of Karunyamirtha Theertham. Bathing in it on Somavaram (Monday) is special. It was created by Chandra (the moon god) and removes the five great sins. It is currently known as Ayyanar Kulam. Next is Rudra Theertham. Next are Padma Theertham, Pandava Theerthams, Indana Theertham, Vayu Theertham, Kubera Theertham, Isana Theertham, Kanaka Theertham, Ganga Kupam, Garuda Theertham, Vasu Theertham, Surya Theertham, Maruthukkal Theertham, Narasinga Theertham, Nandi Theertham, Drona Theertham, Ragava Kupam, Sura Theertham, Muni Theertham, Kachapa Theertham, Gautama Theertham, Kalvi There are thirty-two Theerthams in this site, including Kalyana Theertham.

The other temples located around this site are Theradi Pillaiyar Koil, Viswanathar Koil, Kumarak Koil, Rishipuriswarar Koil, Melamariamman Koil, Perumal Koil, Aghoraveerabhadrar Koil, Sokkanathar Koil, Keelamariamman Koil, Ulagatchi Koil, and Atmanathar Koil. This site is a Panchalinga Sthalam. Viswanathar shines in the east, Rishipuriswarar in the west, Sokkanathar in the north, and Atmanathar in the south, with Sri Mahalinga Peruman seated as the central deity. The temple stands majestically in the center of the town. The outer circumambulatory path of this temple is called Ashwamedha Pradakshina Prakaram. Those who circumambulate this path will receive the benefit of having performed the Ashwamedha sacrifice.

The next circumambulatory path is called Kodumudi. It is called Prakaram. Those who circumambulate this Prakaram will receive the benefit of having circumambulated Thiru-Kailasa.

Next, the Prakaram located adjacent to the sanctum sanctorum is the Pranava Prakaram.

Thus, this temple shines. Other deities in the temple include Padithurai Vinayagar and Anda Vinayagar. There is a Mookambikai shrine in this site. The Goddess is in a meditative posture. Inscriptions refer to this Ambikai as Pidari Yogirundha Parameswari. The sanctum sanctorum of this temple is built in the North Indian style.

Next, the deities of Vempadi Kumarar Koil and Sokkanathar Koil are located. There are many mandapams, including Kalyana Mandapam and Natiya Mandapam. The Thevara Thiru-Pathikams sung by the Samayacharyas, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, and Sundaramurthy Swamigal, are available for this site. There are a total of eleven Thevara Thiru-Pathikams for this site. Manikkavasagar Swamigal has also sung about this site in Thiruvasagam. Pattinaththu Swamigal has composed a work called Thiru-Idai-Maruthur Mummani Kovai.

This work is in the eleventh Thiru-Murai. Bhadragiriyar has worshipped at this site. Sivakozhundhu Desikar has translated the Sthala Puranam of this site from Sanskrit into Tamil. Six daily pujas, starting from Thiru-Ananthal, are performed in this temple. During the second period, a special puja is performed exclusively for Ekanayagar. The Thai Poosam festival and the Vaikasi Vasantha festival are celebrated grandly in this temple.

In addition to these, festivals such as Thiru-Athirai Oonjal festival, Panguni Theertham, Chithirai Vishu Punyakalam, and Shivaratri festival are also celebrated grandly. This temple is under the administration of the Thiru-Kailaya Paramparai Thiru-Aavaduthurai Adheenam. Three special sites are mentioned as having the Marutha tree, also known as the Arjuna tree, as their Sthala Vriksham. The first holy site is Thiru-Paruppatham, known as Srisailam.

There, the Lord is enshrined by the name Mallikarjuneswarar, and therefore it is called Mallikarjunam. In the south, in the Pandya country, in the Tirunelveli region, there is a holy site called Thiru-Pudai-Maruthur. Here too, the Marutha tree, called the Arjuna tree, is the Sthala Vriksham. This is called Pudharjunam. Between these two sites, this site, Thiru-Idai-Maruthur, is located as Madhyarjunam. This holy site is where Varaguna Pandiyan’s Brahmagathi Dosham was removed.

Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman There are six Thiru-Pathikams sung by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, five Thiru-Pathikams sung by Appar Swamigal, and one Thiru-Pathikam by Sundaramurthy Swamigal for this site. Karuvur Devar has sung about this site in Thiru-Isaippa. As we have already seen, Pattinaththu Pillaiyar has composed the Prabandham called Thiru-Idai-Maruthur Mummani Kovai. Not only that, but Appar Swamigal and Sundaramurthy Swamigal have also mentioned Thiru-Idai-Maruthur in other Thiru-Pathikams. Manikkavasagar Swamigal has also sung about Thiru-Idai-Maruthur in six places in Thiruvasagam. In the seventy-fifth line of Keerththi Thiru-Agaval, he has sung, “Idaimaruthu athanil eenda irundhu” (residing there in Idaimaruthu).

In the one hundred and forty-fifth line of Potri Thiru-Agaval, he has sung, “Idaimaruthu uraiyum enthaay potri” (Praise to my Lord who resides in Idaimaruthu). In the Thiru-Poovalli Thiru-Pathikam of Thiru-Vasagam, the second verse, which begins with “Entha Enthai Sutram Mattumellam Ennudaiya Bandham Aruthu Ena Aandu Konda Pandi-Piran Antha Idaimaruthil Aanandha Thenirundha Pondhai Paravinam Poovalli Koyyamo,” praises the Lord of Thiru-Idaimaruthur as the abode of joyful honey. In the second verse of the Thiru-Poonnusal Thiru-Pathikam, it is sung, “Oon Thangi Nindru Urukkum Uthirakosamangai Kon Thangu Idaimaruthu Paadi.” In the ninth verse of the Thiru-Vesaravu Thiru-Pathikam, it is sung, “Arul Enakku Ingu Idaimaruthe Idam Konda Ammane.” In Thiru-Kovaiyar, in the song beginning “Kundram Kidaikkum Kadandhu Umar,” Thiru-Idaimaruthur is mentioned as “Idaimaruthu Ekambam Vanjiyam.” Parana Deva Nayanar has sung about Thiru-Idaimaruthur in the Thiru-Andhadhi of Lord Shiva. Literary works such as Maruthavana Puranam, Thiru-Idaimaruthur Ula, Thiru-Idaimaruthur Kalambagam, Thiru-Idaimaruthur Patirruppathandhadhi, and Thiru-Idaimaruthur Nondi Nadagam also elucidate the glory of this sacred sthalam. We have seen that Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, who visited this sthalam, composed five Thiru-Pathikams.

Now, let us consider those Thiru-Pathikams. The first Thiru-Pathikam is the thirty-fifth Thiru-Pathikam in the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerisai Thiru-Pathikam.

Chapter 122 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 384, Thiru-Nindratcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We have seen the first of the five Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar for the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Idaimaruthur.

Now, the second Thiru-Pathikam, compiled as the fourteenth Thiru-Pathikam in the fifth Thiru-Murai, is a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam.

Paraiyin Osaiyum Paadalin Osai Maraiyin Osaiyum Vaigum Ayalalam Iraivan Engal Piran Idaimaruthinil Uraiyum Eesanai Ulkum En Ullame Manaththul Maayanai Maasaru Sothiyai Punittruppillai Vellai Madhisoodiyai Enakku Thaayai Emman Idaimaruthanai Ninaindhuttu Oori Nirainthathu En Ullame Vandu Anainthana Vanniyum Mathamum Kondu Anaintha Sadai Mudi Kooththanai En Thisaikkum Idaimarutha Ena Vindhu Poyarum Melai Vinaigalere Thunai Ilaamaiyil Thoongiruttpeigalodu Anaiyalavadhu Emakku Aridhe Ena Inaiyila Ida Ma Maruthu Ezhu Panaiyilagama Sollum Than Pangikke Mannai Unda Maal Kanaan Malaradi Vinnai Vindhu Ayan Kanaan Viyanmudi Mannai Ma Marutha Endru En Moykuzhal Pannaiyaaya Mundhanum Payilume Mangaikkana Kodar Mana Malaiyai Gangai Kana Kodar Mudikkanniyai Nangai Meer Idaimaruthu Arinangaikke Engu Vangik Koduththar Idhazhiye In this Thiru-Pathikam, the seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth, and eleventh verses are not available to us.

The next Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for this sthalam is the fourth Thiru-Pathikam, which is the sixteenth Thiru-Pathikam in the sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathikam.

Now, that Thiru-Pathikam.

Regarding the numbers in the sixth verse, Sivakavimani notes that “Aiyirandum Aarondrum” refers to sixteen, representing the sixteen Kala Prasadha Mantras, and “Arumoonru” refers to eighteen, representing the eighteen Puranas, and “Naanmoonru” refers to twelve, representing the Moola Mantra along with the Samhita Mantras.

At the same time, regarding the difficult meaning of the seventh verse, Sivakavimani Ayya writes that this song is one of those whose meaning is not easily understood.

Chapter 123 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 385, Thiru-Nindratcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. After worshipping Thiru-Idaimaruthur, singing Thevarams, and devoutly worshipping Lord Shiva, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar stayed there, performed sacred service, and then reached the sthalam called Thiru-Nageswaram. Thiru-Nageswaram is a sacred sthalam very close to Kumbakonam. The Lord’s sacred names are Nageswarar, Naganathar, Shanbagaranyeswarar. The Goddess’s sacred names are Girikujambigai, Kundrumamulai Ammai.

The Sthala Vriksham is the Shanbaga tree. The Theerthams are Surya Theertham, Yama Theertham, Brahma Theertham, Chandra Theertham, Agni Theertham, Durga Theertham, Gautama Theertham, Parasara Theertham, Indra Theertham, Bhrigu Theertham, Kanva Theertham, Vasishtha Theertham. This sthalam is where the Naga Rajas, namely Adiseshan, Dakshan, and Karkotakan, worshipped Lord Shiva.

Hence, this sthalam is named Thiru-Nageswaram. This sthalam is renowned because the Naga Raja worshipped in the first yama at Kudanthai Keezhkottam, which is a Bilva forest, in the second yama at Thiru-Nageswaram, which is a Shanbaga forest, in the third yama at Thiru-Pambaram, which is a Vanni forest, and in the fourth yama at Nagai Karonam, which is a Punnai forest, during one Shivaratri. These four sthalams are known by the name of the Naga Raja. Enraged by Bhringi Muni, who worshipped only Lord Shiva, Goddess Parvati performed severe penance under the Shanbaga tree at this sthalam, desiring the Ardhanareeswara form of Lord Shiva. Not only Adiseshan, Dakshan, and Karkotakan, but also Gautama, Nandi, Nalan, Parasara, Bhagiratha, and others have worshipped here and attained blessings. Surya worshipped here.

Ganesha worshipped here and became the lord of the Ganas. Gautama worshipped and attained Ahalya. Nalan worshipped here and regained his lost wife. Parasara Muni worshipped and was freed from sin. The Pandavas worshipped and regained their lost wealth, and also conducted the Karthigai month festival for this Lord. Vasishtha Muni worshipped.

Indra, Brahma, and Bhagiratha also worshipped. A king named Chitrasenan conducted a festival in Vaikasi and was blessed with a good son. Shaunaka Muni performed penance for infatuation here. A muni named Narkunan lit lamps and observed fasts on Karthigai Somavaram after being bitten by a snake. Many devotees in this sthalam have been blessed and freed from diseases such as Rakshasa, Paisacha, and Vetala, and have had their dead children brought back to life. This sthalam has been sung by the three great saints: Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal.

Sekkizhar Peruman undertook sacred service here, and Thiru-Nageswarathu Peruman is Sekkizhar’s spiritual deity. Due to his affection for this sthalam, Sekkizhar Peruman built a temple with the same name in his hometown of Kundrathur, which is known as Vadathiru-Nageswaram. The sthalam’s Vinayagar is Shanbhaga Vinayagar. This temple is also known as Shanbhaga Vanam and Girikannigai Vanam. It is customary to worship at Kudanthai Keezhkottu Thiru-Nageswaram in the morning, Thiru-Nageswaram at noon, and Thiru-Pambaram in the evening, all on the same day. The idols of Sekkizhar Peruman, his mother, and his younger brother Balaravayan are present in the temple.

Here, Girikujambigai, Lakshmi, and Saraswati are seen in a single sanctum. The sanctum sanctorum of this sacred temple is built according to the Ardhanareeswara principle. The Moolavar, Naganatha Swami, has his sanctum facing south, and the sthalam’s Ambal, Piraiyani Amman, has her sanctum facing north. Both sanctums face east. Instead of separate circumambulatory paths for each sanctum, there is a single path encompassing both, reflecting the Ardhanareeswara concept. The wall on the north side of the Swami’s sanctum and the wall on the south side of the Ambal’s Ardha Mandapam are conjoined, making it impossible to circumambulate the Lord and Goddess separately.

The Lord, who manifests as Ardhanareeswara, bestows His grace here in that very principle. To the east of the Thiruchitrambalamudaiyan Mandapam, facing north, is a seated sculpture of Sekkizhar Peruman, the author of Periya Puranam. To Sekkizhar’s right is a standing sculpture of his mother, Azhagambigai. To Sekkizhar’s left is a seated sculpture of his brother, Balaravayar. These three sacred forms are arranged facing the dancing Nataraja Peruman in the Nataraja Mandapam, which faces south, with their hands clasped in worship. There are two Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for this sthalam, and Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal composed three Thiru-Pathigams, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal composed one Thiru-Pathigam.

Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal visited this sthalam and composed three Thiru-Pathigams. The first Thiru-Pathigam is the sixty-sixth Thiru-Pathigam in the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerishai Thiru-Pathigam.

Kachchai ser aravar polum karaiyani midatrar polum Pichchai kondu unbar polum per arulalar polum Ichchaiyal malargal thoovi iravodu pagalum thammai Nachchuvarkkinaiyar polum Nagaveecharavanare Veduru vedaragi visaiyanodu eythar polum Kaduru patiyar polum kadipunar gangai nangai Sedari sadaiyar polum theevinai theerkkavalla Nadari pugazhar polum Nagaveecharavanare Katrunai villathaga kadiyaran setrar polum Potrunai padar polum puliyathazh udaiyar polum Sotrunai malai kondu thozhuthezhuvar karkellam Natrunaiyavar polum Nagaveecharavanare Kombanal pagar polum kodiyudai vidaiyar polum Sembanar oruvar polum thigazh thiruneetrar polum Embiram emmai alum iraivane endru thammai Nambuvarkku anbar polum Nagaveecharavanare Kadakkari uriyar polum gananmazhu vazhar polum Padavaravaraiyar polum paridam palavum koodi Kudamudai muzhava marba kooligal pada nalum Nadana viladigal polum Nagaveecharavanare Piraiyuru sadaiyar polum pennoru pagar polum Maraiyuru mozhiyar polum nanmarai avan thannodum Muraimurai Amarar koodi mudigalal vananga nindra Naravamal kalalar polum Nagavi Saravanare Vinjagarkariyarp polum maruvinorkku eliyarp polum Kunjaraththuriyaarp polum kootrinai kumaipparp polum Vinjnyar iriyavanru velaivai vanththezhuntha Nanjani midatrar polum Nagavi Saravanare Pogamar modi kongai punartharu punitharp polum Vegamar vidaiyarp polum venpodiyadumeni Pagamaludaiyarp polum paruppatha villarp polum Nagananaudaiyar Nagavichcharavanare Kokkarai thalam veenai panisai kulagar polum Akkarai anivar polum ainththalai aravar polum Vakkarai amarvar polum matharai maiyal seyyum Nakkarai uruvar polum Nagavi Saravanare Vinmaiyal purangal moonrum venthazhal viriththar polum Thanmaiyal amarar thangal thalaivarkkum thalaivar polum Vanmaiyan malaiyeduthan valiyinai tholaiviththu ange Nanmaiyal azhippar polum Nagavichcharavanare Thiruchitrambalam. The second Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal for Thiru-Nageswaram is the fifty-second Thiru-Pathigam in the fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam.

Nallar nallathor nagam kondattuvvar Vallar valvinai theerkkum marundugal Pallil odu kaiyenthi pazhiththiri selvarpol Thiru-Nagechcharavare Navalam peruntheevinil vazhbar mevi vanthu vanangi vinaiyodu Pavamayina patru ariviththidum Devarpol Thiru-Nagechcharavare Othamarkadalil vidamundavar Adhiyar ayanodu amararkkellam Mathorkoorar mazhu valanenthiya Natharpol Thiru-Nagechcharavare Chandiranodu suriyar thamum vanthu Seer vazhipadugal seythapin Ainththalai aravin panikondu arul Maintharpol Mani Nagechcharavare Pandor nal izhvan pazhiththakkanar Konda velvi kumandai athukeda Thandama vithathavin thalai konda Chendarpol Thiru-Nagechcharavare Vambu poonguzhal mathu marugavor Kambaiyanai uriththa karaththinar Sembanar ithazhim malar senjadai Nambarpol Thiru-Nagechcharavare Manaiyenthiya kaiyinar maiyaru Gnana chothiyar adhiyar namanththan Ana anjezhuththu otha vanththanikkum Thenarpol Thiru-Nagechcharavare Kazhal kol kalinar kalanai kaynthavar Thazhal kol men santha venniru ani azhagaral Nizhal keezhara mothiya kulagarpol Kulir Nagechcharavare Vattama mathil moonrudan val aran Sutta seikaiyar agilum soozhnthavar Kutta valvinai theerththu kulirvikkum Sitrarpol Thiru-Nagechcharavare Thooraththan thonmudi thalum tholaiyave Serththinar thirupathaththoruviral Arththu vanthulagaththavar adidum Theertharpol Thiru-Nagechcharavare Thiruchitrambalam.

Now, the third Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasar Swamigal for Thiru-Nageswaram is the sixty-sixth Thiru-Pathigam in the sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathigam.

Thayaivanai vanorkkum enorkkum thalaiyavanai malaiyavanai ulagamellam Ayavanai seyavanai aniyan thannai azhalavanai nizhalavanai ariyavonna maya vanai maraiyavanai maraiyorthangal manthiranai thanthiranai valaranindra theeyavanai Thiru-Nagechcharaththuzhanai serathar nannarik serathare Uriththanai matha velam thannai minnar oli mudi emperumanai umaiyorbagam Thariththanai thariyalaraththam puram eythanai thannadainthar tham vinai noy pavamellam Hariththanai alathankeezh irun nalvarkku aram porul veedu inbam aru angam vedam Theriththanai Thiru-Nagechcharaththuzhanai serathar nannarik serathare Karanai uri porththa kadavul thannai kathaliththu ninaiyatha kayavar nenjil Varanai mathippavartham manaththuzhanai matroruvar thannoppar oppillatha Eranai imayavartham peruman thannai iyalbagi ulagelam nirainthu mikka Seeranai Thiru-Nagechcharaththuzhanai serathar nannarik serathare Thalaiyanai evvulagum thanananai thannuruvam yavarkkum ariyavonna Nilaiyanai nesarkku nesanthannai neezhvanam mugadathanai thangi nindra Malaiyanai variyaravu nanakoththu vallasurpuramoonru madiya eytha Silaiyanai Thiru-Nagechcharaththuzhanai serathar nannarik serathare Meyyanai thanpakkal virumbuvarkku virumbatha arumbavivarkku endrum Poyyanai purankattil adalanai pon pozhintha sadaiyanai podikol poothi Paiyanai paiyaravam asaiththan thannai paranththanai pavalamal varai pol menich Cheyyanai Thiru-Nagechcharaththuzhanai serathar nannarik serathare Thuranthanai aramburiya thurisarthammai thoththirangal pala solli vanor yeththa nirainthanai neer nilam thee veli katragi nirppanavum nadappanavum ayinanai Maranthanai than ninaiya vanjarthammai anjezhuththum vay navilavallorkku endrum Siranthanai Thiru-Nagechcharaththuzhanai serathar nannarik serathare Maraiyanai mal vidai onru Siraiyanai Thiru-Nagechcharaththuzhanai serathar nannarik serathare Eythanai puram moonrum imaikkum pothil iru visumbil varu punalai Thiruvar senni peythanai pirappiliyai araththil nilla piraman than siram onrai karam onrinal Koythanai kooththada vallan thannai kuriyila kodiye adiyenagas seythanai Thiru-Nagechcharaththuzhanai serathar nannarik serathare Azhiyanai annikkum an pal thannai van payirai appayirin vattam theerkkum Thuliyanai ayan malum thedik kana sudaranai thurisarath thondupattarkku Ezhiyanai yavarkkum ariyan thannai in karumbin thannullaliruntha therar Theliyanai punithan thannai Arththodi malai eduththa arakkan anja aru viralal adarththanai adainthorpam Theerththanai Thiru-Nagechcharaththuzhanai serathar nannarik serathare Thiruchitrambalam.

Thus, we have seen the three Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for Thiru-Nageswaram. Our contemplation continues.

Swamigal’s three Thiru-Pathigams for Thiru-Nageswaram.

We shall proceed with our contemplation.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 124 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 386. Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Thiru-Nageswaram and sung Thiru-Pathigams there, then proceeds to the sacred sthalam of Pazhaiyarai. This sthalam is also known as Pazhaiyarai.

It is the birthplace of Amarneethi Nayanar. We have contemplated the special features of this sthalam in the Puranam of Amarneethi Nayanar. The Thiru-Pathigam sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal at this sthalam is not available to us. The Thiru-Pathigam ‘Thalaiyellam Parikkum Saman Kaiyar’, sung at Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, is a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam, which Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar composed later when he visited and worshipped at Pazhaiyarai Vadathali. We shall see that sacred history later in the Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Having worshipped at Pazhaiyarai, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal then reached the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Sakthimuttram.

Thiru-Sakthimuttram is located very close to Thiru-Pattiswaram, near Kumbakonam. Thiru-Pattiswaram is the twenty-second sthalam among the Cauvery South Bank sthalams, and Thiru-Sakthimuttram is the twenty-third. The south street of Thiru-Sakthimuttram is the north street of Thiru-Pattiswaram. These two sthalams are thus interconnected. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar arrives at Thiru-Sakthimuttram.

Here, the Lord’s sacred name is Sivakkozhundeesar, and the Goddess’s sacred name is Periya Nayaki. The sthalam’s sacred tree is Vilvam, and its sacred water is Soola Theertham. In this sthalam, Thiru-Sakthimuttram, in this temple, Uma Devi worshipped Lord Shiva and embraced and kissed Him, which is why this sacred sthalam is known by the sacred name Thiru-Sakthi Muttram. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal praised this in his Thevara Pathigam, saying, “Mattar Kuzhali Malaimagal poojai magizhtharulum Sitta Thiru-Sakthi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe.” This sthalam is now known as Sakthi Muttram. The history of this sthalam states that the Goddess desired to worship the Lord and behold His sacred form, and a light appeared from the Shiva Lingam, at which point the Goddess embraced the Lord. The sacred marks corresponding to this event are visible on the Moolalingam Peruman in this temple.

Next to the Moolasthanam, we can behold the sacred form of the Goddess embracing and kissing the Shiva Lingam. The temple is a large structure facing east, situated amidst four sacred streets. At the entrance, Vallabhai Ganapathi is present. The Vasantha Mandapam at the temple entrance is a grand hall. There are two circumambulatory paths. The Rajagopuram has five tiers.

The outer circumambulatory path is very large. The Yagasalai is in the northeast direction, and the Pakasalai (kitchen) is in the southeast. In front of the sanctum, there is a flagstaff, Nandi, and Balipeetams. Beyond that is the front mandapam. Upon entering past the mandapam, one finds the second gopuram entrance with Vinayagar and Murugan. To the right, the Ambal temple faces south.

Beyond the second gopuram, there is a Maha Mandapam with a Nataraja Sabha. Opposite it is the Nalvar Sannidhi. At the entrance of the Swami Sannidhi, to the south is Somaskandar, and to the north is the traditional deity depicting Sakthi Muttram. Behind this traditional sculpture, there is also a scene of the Ambal performing penance standing on one leg. In the inner circumambulatory path, to the southwest are the sthalam’s Vinayagar, followed by Somaskandar, Arumugar, and Gajalakshmi. In the sanctum’s niches, to the south are Vinayagar, Natarajar, a sage, and Dakshinamurthy; to the west is Lingothbhavar; and to the north are Brahma and Durga.

In the northern circumambulatory path, there is a separate Chandeesar temple. He can be worshipped from the Swami Sannidhi itself. Next to the Natarajar Sabha is the old Ambal idol. Upon entering further, one reaches the Ardha Mandapam. Beyond that, one can worship Vinayagar and the Dvarapalakas. The Swami Sannidhi is very special.

When Appar Swamigal requested to receive Thiru-Adi Deekshai, this deity granted him grace, saying, “Come to Nallur.” The Ambal temple is in the first circumambulatory path. This is the sthalam where the Ambikai performed penance, hence this sanctum is very special. Appar Swamigal mentions the name of the Lord of this sthalam, Sivakkozhundeesar, in every verse of the Thiru-Pathigam he composed. The Thazhuva Kulantha Nathar idol in this sthalam is very beautiful. The sacred water outside the temple is known as Soola Theertham and Surya Theertham. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal comes to Thiru-Sakthi Muttram for darshan.

He worships Sivakkozhundeesar, who is enshrined in Thiru-Sakthi Muttram, and performs his characteristic sacred service of Ulavaara Thiru-Pani. He also offers garlands of Thevaram to the Lord.

At that time, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal sings the Thevara Thiru-Pathigam beginning with ‘Kovay Mudugi’. In this Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman makes a request to Sivakkozhundeesar, the Lord of this sthalam. He requests, “Before Yama comes and takes my life, please imprint the mark of your flower-like sacred feet upon my head.” In this Thiru-Pathigam, he refers to the Lord’s feet as ‘poovar thiruvadigal’ (flower-like sacred feet), feet adorned with flowers offered by Ambikai and devotees. He prays, “Please imprint the mark of those sacred feet upon my head.” ‘Poriththu vaiththal’ means to engrave it permanently, so that the mark of the sacred feet never changes. The meaning is that devotees should always remain under the shade of the Lord’s sacred feet, never going anywhere else. The meaning is that devotees should always remain under the shade of the Lord’s sacred feet, never going anywhere else.

Thus, with the request that the Lord’s sacred feet should be on his head, he prays, “Please place your sacred feet upon my head.” ‘Thadalai Karalai’ are symbolic expressions belonging to the Saivite tradition. ‘Thazh Thalai’.

Thus, he sings that Thiru-Pathigam, which is the Thiru-Pathigam ‘Kovay Mudugi’. This is the ninety-sixth Thiru-Pathigam in the fourth Thiru-Murai.

Now, that Thiru-Pathigam.

Kovay mudugi aduththal kootram kumaippathan mun Poovar adichchuvadu enmel poriththu vai pogavidil Moova muzhappazhi moodum kanday Muzhangum thalal kai Deva Thiru-Saththi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Kaynthay anangan udalam podipadak kalanai mun Paynthay uyir segap patham panivar tham palpiravi Aynthaynthu aruppay adiyerkku arulay un anbar sinthai Serththay Thiru-Saththi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Poththar kurambai pugunthu aivar nalum pugazh azhippar Matthar thayirpol marugum en sinthai marukkozivi Aththa adiyen adaikkalam kanday amarargal tham Siththa Thiru-Saththi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Nilla kurambai nilaiya karuthi innee nilaththu Onralla kuzhi veezhnthu ayarvuruvayenai vanthu andu kondaiy Viller puruvaththu umaiyal kanava vidil keduven Selva Thiru-Saththi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Karuvutru irunthu un kalale ninainthan karuppuviyil Theruvil pugunthan thigaiththu adiyenai thigaippu olivi Uruvil thigazhum umaiyal kanava vidil keduven Thiruvil polichchaththi Muttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Vemmai naman thamar mikku viravi vizhuppathan mun Immai un thazh en nenjaththu ezhuthivai eengu igazhil Ammai adiyerkku aruluthi enbathu ingu ararivar Semmai tharu Sakthimuttram uraiyum Sivakkozhundhe Vittar purangal oru nodi vevavor venganiyal Suttay en pasathth thodarbu aruththu andukol thumbi pambum Mattarkuzhali malaimagal poosai magizhtharulum Sitta Thiru-Saththi Muttram uraiyum O Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu, residing in Thiru-Sathimuttam, who, when the scornful Daksha performed his sacrifice, and the celestials implored, on that very day, you, the blue-throated one, took victory! Grant me, your praising devotee, release from my sins. O Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu, residing in Thiru-Sathimuttam, I, having attained the worthy, and overcome by sorrow, have sought refuge at your feet. What love, what benefit, do I possess other than your grace? O Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu, residing in Thiru-Sathimuttam, who is greatly desired by those in Thillai, and who is the direction of the great north!

When the chariot-borne demon, Ravana, who had taken up the burden, had his golden crown crushed and his skin torn, you pressed a single toe, causing him to wail and descend, and then you granted him grace. O Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu, residing in Thiru-Sathimuttam, you destroyed the disease of the cruel deeds I committed.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, at Thiru-Sathimuttam, petitions Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu Eesar that the sacred footprints of the Lord be imprinted upon his head. Immediately after he sang this Pathikam, Thiru-Sivakkozhundhu Eesar at Thiru-Sathimuttam graciously commands Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, saying, “Come to Nallur!” Nallur is a sacred sthalam known as Thiru-Nallur. This sacred sthalam is very close to Thiru-Sathimuttam. We know that Thiru-Nallur is the sthalam where the history of Amarneethi Nayanar, ascending the balance and reaching Kailash, occurred, as recounted in the Puranas of Amarneethi Nayanar.

The Lord graciously commands him to come to that Thiru-Nallur.

Thus, guided by divine grace, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar ...the sacred devotee, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, reverently and joyfully arrives at Thiru-Nallur. Upon arriving at Thiru-Nallur and worshipping the Peruman there, as he rises, Lord Shiva graciously declares, “We shall fulfill your desire,” and places His lotus feet upon the head of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar. Sekkizhar Swamigal sings this history as follows: “Kovai mudigi” (When the Lord, as death, comes to torment before the flowery feet are placed upon my head, as I pleaded, ‘Place them upon my head,’ and sang the Pathikam with my tongue, the Lord Himself, saying, ‘Come to Nallur,’ bestowed His grace. The devotee, Vaageesar, reverently and joyfully, following the path of great goodness, arrived at Thiru-Nallur and remained there.) When he worshipped and rose joyfully, Lord Shiva placed His lotus feet upon his head, saying, “We shall fulfill your desire.” This is what Sekkizhar Peruman states in these two sacred verses.

The Lord Shiva graciously says, “Come to Nallur,” at Thiru-Sathimuttam. The repetition of “Come” twice here signifies the abundance and certainty of His grace.

Similarly, in the sacred history of Sundaramurthi Swamigal, in the Purana of Thaduthatkonda, when Sundaramurthi Swamigal was worshipping Nataraja Peruman in Thillai, Lord Shiva called him to come to Thiruvarur.

Likewise, He graciously commanded Manikkavasagar Swamigal to come to Thillai.

Similarly, here at Thiru-Sathimuttam, Lord Shiva calls Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, who had petitioned for the sacred lotus feet of Lord Shiva to be placed upon his head, saying, “Come to Nallur!” Lord Shiva, a supreme divine flame transcending time and space, is present everywhere, shining in Thiru-Sathimuttam and Thiru-Nallur. When such a Lord Shiva graciously commanded, “Come to Nallur!”, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar came to Thiru-Nallur, worshipped the Peruman, and as he rose, the Lord graciously placed His sacred lotus feet upon the head of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, saying, “We shall fulfill your desire.” Placing the lotus feet upon the head is a form of initiation (Thiruvadi Deekshai). This is performed after Gnana Deekshai and is also known as Sambhavi Deekshai. “Sevadi Kanam Sen...” ...“Manni Thigazhume” is from Thiruvasagam. Just as the Lord, in the form of a Guru, came and bestowed grace upon Manikkavasagar Peruman, the sage of Thiru-Vathavur, similarly, the Lord, who came as a Guru, placed His sacred feet upon the head of Manikkavasagar Swamigal.

In accordance with the manner in which Sundaramurthi Swamigal was forcefully taken into service, when Sundaramurthi Swamigal was staying in the Siddhavadam Matham, the Lord Himself came and performed the Thiruvadi Deekshai for Sundaramurthi Swamigal. In this sacred verse, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal as “Mannu Thiruthondar” (the steadfast sacred devotee). “Mannum Thiru” are epithets that signify the greatness and imperishability of Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar’s devotion to Shiva and his greatness as Vaageesar. Previously, he was a Gnana Thiru-Munivar ...who performed penance as Vaageesa Munivar. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, later, came here as Thiru-Navukkarasar and served for many days by singing garlands of sacred verses.

After this, finally, becoming the very form of pure Shivanantha Gnana, he continues to perform sacred service even while seated beneath the sacred feet of Lord Shiva. Because this sacred service is blessed in all three times (past, present, and future), Sekkizhar Peruman uses the epithet “Mannu” (steadfast). And because the sacred service he performed leads to liberation, he uses the epithet “Thiru” (sacred).

Thus, Lord Shiva, in Thiru-Nallur, places His grace upon the head of Thiru-Navukkarasar. “He placed His sacred feet, which were wet, upon my head,” thus, the holy one, praising with the composed Thiru-Thandagam, and remembering His grace ...and melting with devotion, falling and rising, filled with joy, and like one who has received immense, inexhaustible wealth, his heart blossomed,“ sings Sekkizhar Peruman. “He placed His sacred feet, which were wet, upon my head,” thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar now composes the Thiru-Thandagam Pathikam and praises the Lord. Remembering the immense grace bestowed upon him by Lord Shiva, the holy one, he melts with devotion, falls to the ground, then rises, filled with contentment and inner joy, and his heart blossoms. Just as a poor person would rejoice upon receiving inexhaustible wealth, so too does his heart blossom. In this verse, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Lord Shiva as “Punithar” (the Holy One).

“Punithar” means one who is naturally free from attachments. “Punithar” also means one who purifies. One who possesses natural purity also possesses the power to purify. This is its meaning.

Thus, due to the history of Lord Shiva placing His sacred feet upon the head of Thiru-Navukkarasar in Thiru-Nallur, even today, in the Thiru-Nallur temple, the custom of placing the Lord’s sacred feet upon the heads of devotees continues.

Now, at this time, the Thiru-Pathikam sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar about the Peruman of Thiru-Nallur is the Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathikam. It is compiled as the fourteenth Thiru-Pathikam in the Sixth Thiru-Murai.

Now, that Thiru-Pathikam: Thiruchitrambalam. “He made the devotees who remember and melt with devotion to suffer (in separation), He made evil deeds disappear without remaining, He covered Himself with the skin of an enraged elephant, He placed the crescent moon, He placed the celestial beings, searching for gems and crowns...” ...He placed the flowers, blooming with honey, upon my head, those sacred feet, wet with nectar, are those of our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the golden, fragrant Konrai on His matted locks, He placed the tiger skin, He placed the water, He placed the battle-axe on His strong shoulders, He placed the earrings in His long ears, He placed the moon, He placed the part of the slender-waisted one, He placed the quiver of the god of love, He placed the sacred thread, He placed the sacred feet, full of goodness, upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the blooming Konrai flowers on His matted locks, He placed the dense garland, He made the waves crash, He placed the cool Datura flower, He placed the snake, He placed the eye on His sacred forehead, He placed the bow, He placed the daughter of the mountain, He placed the sacred feet, known throughout the land, upon my head ...He placed them, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He graciously placed the bow, He placed the part of the one who was burned, He placed the waterfall on His matted locks, He placed the mountain as a bow, He placed Kailash, the mountain of the gods, He placed the gods, He graciously taught the four sages the Dharma, He placed the ashes of the burning ground, He placed the ascetics, He graciously placed His sacred feet upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is!

He made the three cities burn in the sky, He made the deeds of those who worshipped disappear, He placed the ascetics, He burned Kama with His eye, He placed the fragrant lotus flower, He placed Kailash, He placed the fierce path and the cool water together, He made the celestials, who worshipped the directions, shine and praise, He graciously placed His sacred feet upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the seven worlds of suffering and disease, He placed life, He placed the path that life takes ...He placed the multitude of other celestials, He placed the Vedas of the celestials, He made the waning moon grow, He placed the path that does not allow anger, desire, and greed to flourish, He placed the ascetics, He placed the sacred feet of the good ascetics upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He made the opposing Vedas burn, He placed them on His jeweled crown, He made the beautiful body, filled with water, dance, He placed the eye on His forehead, He placed the abode, He made the waves of the river burn, He made the celestials worship His feet with devotion, He placed the fragrant lotus feet upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the worlds with many oceans, He placed the small jewels, He placed the form, He placed the top of the serpent, He drank the poison, He placed the eight shoulders, He placed the water and fire in the earth ...He placed the wind, He placed them in the high sky, He placed them in the minds of those who thought, He graciously placed His sacred feet, full of goodness, upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the two suns and moons in the sky, He placed the ten directions firmly on the earth, He stood and made the celestials worship His feet, He made the full and hidden meaning shine, He killed and made the cruel Yama tremble and flee, He placed His sacred feet, which are the refuge, He placed the bull, He graciously placed His sacred feet upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is! He placed the snake, the moon, and the waves in His matted locks, He placed the grace for all those who serve Him, He placed the ashes of the burning ground, He placed beauty, He made the powerful karmic disease disappear, He placed Uma on one side, He placed His sacred feet, which the celestials praise with joy, upon my head, our Lord of Nallur ...how good He is!

He placed the seven oceans with their rising waves, He placed the mountain with small jewels, He pressed a single toe upon the head of the one who lifted the mountain with his hand, causing him pain, and when he cried out, “O Lord!”, He graciously placed the sword and fame, He graciously placed His sacred feet, full of goodness, upon my head, our Lord of Nallur, how good He is!

In this Thiru-Pathikam of eleven sacred verses, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, remembering the grace of Lord Shiva in many ways, and melting with devotion, with a blossoming heart, has graciously composed this Thiru-Pathikam, saying, “By His good grace, the Lord of Nallur placed His sacred feet upon my head so that I might attain goodness.” We shall proceed with our contemplation.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 125 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 387, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Having stayed in Thiru-Nallur for a long time, he performs many heartfelt Thiru-Thondus (sacred services) with his hands. He composes many garlands of Thevaram Tamil verses for the Lord.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar performs these sacred services, focusing not on living beings and the world, but on Lord Shiva, the God of gods. While he is doing so, he visits and worships the sthalams where Lord Shiva, the God with an eye on His forehead, resides, such as Thiru-Karugavur, Thiru-Avur, Thiru-Palaithurai, and others, sings Thevaram Pathikams there, and then returns to Thiru-Nallur. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, Karuga ...Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, having visited Thiru-Karugavur, Thiru-Avur, Thiru-Palaithurai, and other places where the Lord with the eye on His forehead resides, and having worshipped there, performs abundant and ardent sacred service, and serves with a melting heart, never leaving Thiru-Nallur for a moment.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar departs from Thiru-Nallur, reaches the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Karugavur, and there praises the Lord and sings a Thiru-Pathikam. Thiru-Karugavur sthalam is located south of Thiru-Nallur, on the south bank of the Vettaru, a river that flows like a canal. This sacred sthalam is known by names such as Mullai Vanam, Madhavi Vanam, Karugavur, and Karppapuri. This sthalam is the eighteenth sthalam on the south bank of the Cauvery. The sacred name of the Lord of Thiru-Karugavur is Karppapureeswarar, Mullaivananathar, Madhavi Vaneswarar. The sacred name of the Goddess is ...Karumbanaiyal Ammai, Karpparakshambikai, Karukkakkum Nayaki.

The sacred waters are Brahma Theertham, Ksheerakundam, Sathyakoopam, Vriddha Cauvery, etc. The sthala tree is the Mullai creeper. This sthalam is named Karugavur because the Goddess here medically protected the fetus of a helpless woman. Many women who suffer from frequent miscarriages and are distressed by childlessness come to this sthalam, worship the Lord and Goddess, fulfill their vows, and attain the blessing of good children. This is a notable miraculous event of this sthalam. Among the Pancha Aranya Sthalams, which are sacred sthalams on the south bank of the Cauvery, Thiru-Karugavur (Mullai Vanam), Avalivanallur (Padiri Vanam), Arathai Perumpali (Vanni Vanam), Thiru-Irumboolai (Poolai Vanam), and Thiru-Kollamboodur (Vilva Vanam) are the five sthalams.

These are called the Pancha Aranya Sthalams. Thiru-Karugavur, also known as Mullai Vanam, is one of them. It is said that those who worship these sthalams at dawn, noon, evening, and midnight, respectively, will attain all good things. The greatness of Thiru-Karugavur is described in the Sanatkumara Samhita of the Kshetra Vaibhava Kanda in the Skanda Purana, as narrated by Sanatkumara to Narada Muni. The sthala Purana states that if one, no matter where they are, desires to go to this sthalam, named Madhavi Vanam, and takes three steps, then with the first step, all their sins will be removed. With the second step, the celestial world will become theirs.

With the third step, they are assured of attaining Shiva Sayujyam. The sthala Purana states that if one merely thinks of Thiru-Karugavur, speaks of it, resides there, or sees it, or hears of its greatness, or passes through it to other towns, all evils will be removed, they will attain various enjoyments, and finally, it is certain that they will merge with the Lord’s sacred feet. The Karppaga Vinayagar and Nandhi Devar of this sthalam are self-manifested deities. In the Somaskanda arrangement, the Lord’s shrine is on the right, the Goddess’s shrine is on the left, and Murugan’s shrine is in the middle. Brahma, Gargya, Gautama, Gujathvajan, Sangakarnan, Nithruvar, Bheemasenan, Punyathvajan, Chandra, and others have worshipped here and received blessings.

The Lord residing in this sthalam is a Swayambhu Murthy. Appar Adigal praised Him as “the eye that appears before the world as a fetus.” Thiru-Gnanasambandar, in every verse, connects the greatness of this sthalam, named Mullai Vanam, and the glory of the Lord adorned with Mullai flowers, to the Mullai. The Goddess residing in this sthalam ...protected the fetus of Vedikai, the wife of Nithruvar, from a miscarriage caused by the curse of Urthuvapatha Maharishi, and gave form to the fetus.

Hence, she is known as Sri Karpparakshaki and Karpparakshambikai. It is said that those who have lived or worshipped in this sthalam from time immemorial do not experience premature births or labor pains. It is also said that no mothers have died with their fetuses in this sthalam. The Lord’s Lingam is made of earth (Prithvi). Only civet paste is applied to it. A scar from a Mullai creeper wrapped around it is visible on the Lord’s sacred body.

Abhishekam is performed only for the Avudaiyar. Mullai flowers are offered to the Lord daily. The sthala Purana states that those who come to this sthalam, bathe in the sacred waters, and worship will attain all good things. Thiru-Gnanasambandar ...Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal each sang one Thiru-Pathikam, so there are two Thiru-Pathikams for this sthalam. The name of this sthalam is mentioned in the Thiru-Pathikam verse of Oorthogai composed by Sundarar. The temple, with a beautiful appearance, faces east and is located in the middle of the village on the south bank of the Vettaru.

There are four streets surrounding the temple. Opposite the temple is a large sacred tank called Thiru-Parkulam. A Raja Gopuram with five tiers adds beauty to the temple. Sri Sarvasiddhi Vinayagar is present at the right entrance of the temple. After passing through the Raja Gopuram entrance, one can reach the first outer prakaram. To the south of the Gopuram entrance is the Thiru-Nandavanam (sacred garden), and to the north is the Vasantha Mandapam.

After passing through the second Gopuram entrance, one can reach the first prakaram. At the entrance, there are Vinayagar, the flagstaff, twin Nandis, and Balipeedams. To the south are the sixty-three Nayanmars and the nine Thogaiyadiyars. Next to them are the Santhanacharyars and Samayacharyars. In the southwest corner is Vinayagar. To the west, between the Lord’s shrine and the Goddess’s shrine, in a Somaskanda arrangement, is the shrine of Arumuga Kadavul, and next to it is the Mahalakshmi shrine.

To the north is the Chandeesar shrine. In the Garbhagriha Koshtams, to the south are Vinayagar and Dakshinamurthy, to the west is Ardhanareeswarar, and to the north are Brahma and Durga. The sthala tree, Mullai, is in the northern prakaram. In the northeast direction are the Yagasalai and the Sabha Mandapam in the form of a chariot for horse racing. In this mandapam are the Shiva Lingams worshipped by Nithruvar, Gargya, and Sangukarnan. We circumambulate, worship Vinayagar at the sacred entrance, and enter the temple.

In the Maha Mandapam are the Navagrahas, arranged according to Agamic rules, and the Nataraja Sabha. To the right of the temple is a separate Somaskanda Mandapam. Inscriptions of the sthala Thiru-Pathikams are installed. After worshipping Karppaga Vinayagar, upon entering the Ardha Mandapam, the Panchamurthies are present. With the Dvarapalakas guarding the entrance, Sri Mullai Vana Nathar resides in the Garbhagriha and bestows grace.

The Lord shines with a tall Lingam made of earth (Prithvi) and a scar from a Mullai creeper wrapped around it. Abhishekam is performed only for the Avudaiyar. Upon worshipping and coming out, in the first prakaram, on the way to the Ambal shrine, there is a sacred water body called Sathyakoopam and the Gautameswarar temple. Opposite, facing east, the Ambal temple shines as a separate temple with its own prakaram. Karukkatha Nayaki, as the mother who binds our thoughts, bestows grace. The historical painting of the sthalam is inscribed at the entrance.

Now, the Puranic story of this sthalam ...is as follows: Brahma Devar developed the ego of “I.” As a result, the act of creation did not succeed. In this sthalam, Brahma created a sacred water body in his name, bathed in it, worshipped Mullai Vana Nathar, regained the power of creation, and attained Sathya Lokam. The sage Gargya, who caused a merchant named Swarnadharan, who had wandered in the form of a ghost for twenty-one yugas for having cheated a Brahmin of his entrusted wealth, to bathe in the Ganges and other sacred waters, and finally in the Brahma Theertham of this sthalam, thereby enabling him to attain Devalokam. This same sage performed many renovation works in this temple. The history of the sage Nithruvar is the reason why the Goddess is named Karukkatha Nayaki. The sage Nithruvar lived a married life in this sthalam with a woman named Vedikai.

When the sage had gone to another town to perform a sacrifice, Urthuvadhava The sage Nithruvar came to the ashram. Vedikai, being heavily pregnant, was unable to rise and offer alms. Urdhvapathar, angered, cursed Vedikai, the heavily pregnant woman, with the disease of Rajayatchu. Due to the power of this curse, the woman’s fetus slipped and fell. Vedikai, in a swoon of sorrow, prayed to Mullai Vananathar.

The Lord filled the fetus in the Goddess’s ambrosial pot and commanded Kamadhenu to nurture the child.

The Lord said that if Vedikai bathed in Brahmateertham for one year and worshipped Him with red lotus flowers, the curse would be lifted. Nithruvar prayed to the Goddess for the boon that those living in this sthalam would not suffer from pregnancy pains, and received it.

From then on, those who worship in this sthalam do not experience miscarriage. The Goddess is known as Karukka tha Nayaki. As we have already seen, this sthalam has one Thiru-pathigam sung by Thiru-gnanasambandhar Peruman and one Thiru-pathigam sung by Appar Swamigal, making a total of two Thevara Thiru-pathigams.

Additionally, this sthalam has sthala puranam, Pathittruppattu Andhadhi, Irattai Manimalai, Nan Manimalai, and other literary works.

Now, the Thiru-pathigam sung by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, who visited this sthalam, is compiled as the fifteenth Thiru-pathigam in the sixth Thirumurai.

Now, that Thiru-pathigam: Thiruchitrambalam. “Kurugam vairamam kooru naalang kollum kizhamaiyang kole thanam, Baruga amudhamam paalin neyyam pazhathin radhamam paattir pannam, Oru kaal umaiyaalor paaganumam ul nindra naavir kuraiyaadiyang karuvaai ulagukku munne thondrum kannang karugavoor” Enthai thane vitham mulaiyagum vere thanam vendum uruvamam virumbi nindra patham adiyarkor pangunam paal niramam paramjothi thanam thotham amararganam soozhndhu potra thondradhu en ullathin ulle nindra katham adiyerku kaanagattum kannang karugavoor enthai thane poothanam poovin nirathanamam pookuzhal vasamam manni nindra kothanam kolvalaiyal kooranagum konda samayathar devanagi ethathatharku endrum idare thunbam eevanam en nenjathu ulle nindru kaathanam kaalan adaiyavannam kannang karugavoor enthai thane iravanam elli nadamadiyam en thisai kunthevanam enuzhanam aravanam allal aruppanumam akasa moorthiyam aaneru erum kuravanam kootrai udhaithan thanam kooratha vanja kuyalarkku endrum karavanam katchikku ezhiyanumam kannang karuvoor enthai thane padaithanam paarai idanthanamum parisu ondru ariyama nindran thanam udaithanam onnar purangal moonrum ol azhalal mootti orukki nindru adaithanam soolam mazhuvor nagam asaithanam aaneru ondru oornthanamum kadaithanam kallam arivar nenjil kannang karugavoor enthai thane moolanam moorthiyam munne thanam moovatha meni mukkinanam Seelanar sernthar idargal theerkkum selvanar senjudarkor sothithanam malanam mangaiyor baganamam mandradiyam vanorthangarkellam kalanam kalanai kaynthanagum kannang karugavoor enthai thane araiser aravanam alathanam adhirai nalanam andavanor thiraiser thirumudi thingalanam theevinai nasan en sinthaiyanam uraiser ulagathar ullanumam umaiyalorbaganam velik karaiser kadal nanjai undanagum kannang karugavoor enthai thane thudiyan thodiyin muzhakkathana sollvar sollallam sothippanam padi thanam pavam aruppanamum paal neetranam paramjothi thanam kodiyan nang kootrai udhaithanagum kooratha vanjak kuyalarkku endrum kadiyanang katchikku ariyanaagum kannang karugavoor enthai thane vitturuvam kizharkindra sothianam vinnvarkkum ariyatha soozhalanam patturuvamal yanai thol keendanm pala palavum paani payindran thanam etturuvam moorthiyam en tholanam ennuchi melanam embiranam katturuvam kadiyanai kaynthanagum kannang karugavoor enthai thane poruthirundha pullurvan ullanagi ulliruthangu ulnoi kalaivan thanai seruthirundha mummathilgal moonrum veva silaiguniya theemoottum thinmaiyanam aruthirundha kaiyanam anthaar alli irundhanai oru thalaiyai theriya nokki karuthirundha kandam udaiyan polum kannang karugavoor enthai thane oruthanam onnar purangal moonrum ol azhalai maatti udane vaithu iruthanam ennan mudigal pathum isainthanam innisaigal kettan agum aruthanam anjum adakki ange akaya mandhiramum anan agum karuthanam kalanai kalal vela kannang karugavoor enthai thane Thiruchitrambalam. This is the Thiru-thandagam Thiru-pathigam bestowed by Appar Swamigal upon the Thiru-karugavoor sthalam.

We shall continue our contemplation.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 126 — Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part Three Hundred Eighty-Eight. Thirunindrachcharukkam. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Thiru-karugavoor and bestowed the Thiru-thandagam Thiru-pathigam, reaches the sthalam known as Thiru-avoor Pasupatheeswaram. Avoor is the name of this village, and Pasupatheeswaram is the name of the holy temple.

This holy place shines as a Maadakkoil (temple built on an elevated platform). It is the sthalam where the divine cow Kamadhenu worshipped, hence the name A-voor (cow’s village). This village also bears the sacred name Ashwathavanam. The vimanam (tower above the sanctum) where the Lord resides is called Manikkoodam because it has a beautiful mountain peak. It is said that Govandakkudi, near this village, is the place where Kamadhenu came to this earthly world from Thiru-kailayamalai. It is said that one of the two mountain fragments brought by Vayu Devan from Thiru-Kailayamalai settled in Nalloor and the other in this village.

The Vinayagar located in the southwest direction of this sthalam is called Niruthi Vinayagar. Murugan appears here as a spear-wielding warrior. The Lord’s name here is Pasupatheeswarar, a Swayambhu Murthy. He is the leader of Kamadhenu, the cow, and all living beings, hence He is called Pasupatheeswarar.

The Lord is also known by the sacred names Ashwatha Vananathar, Avoor Udaiyar, and Pasupatheeswara Udaiyar. There are two Amman shrines in this temple. One is the shrine of Arulmigu Mangalambikai. It is said through oral tradition that this deity was taken from the holy tank and consecrated. The other is the shrine of Pangajavalli, which is the ancient Amman shrine. Pangajavalli Pangaiya Mangai Virumbum Avoor (Avoor desired by the lotus maiden) is how this Amman is referred to in Thevaram.

The sthala tree is the Arasamaram (peepal tree). The thirthams are Brahmateertham, Kamadhenu Theertham, Chandra Pushkarani, Agni Theertham, and Poigaiyaru, a branch of the Kudamurutti river. There is a Thevara Thiru-pathigam for this sthalam, sung and worshipped by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman. There is a sthala history written by Panchanatham Pillai.

Now, the puranic story of this sthalam is as follows: Once upon a time, Sage Vasishta performed a Vajapeyam yagna. For this, he collected materials and invited many sages and Brahmins. He intended to invite Kamadhenu to provide milk for the yagna.

However, Kamadhenu was in Brahmalokam with the Devas and could not come. Vasishta became angry. The sage cursed Kamadhenu. Knowing this, Sage Narada came to Vasishta and spoke of Kamadhenu’s greatness and the sin Vasishta incurred by cursing Kamadhenu. He told the sage that his sin would be absolved if he went to Thiru-vayaaru, bathed in Surya Pushkarani, and worshipped Jappeswarar. Kamadhenu, in the form of a cow, came to this village, Ashwathavanam, worshipped, and after her curse was lifted, provided the necessary assistance to Vasishta.

Kamadhenu, having come from Brahmalokam, took the form of a cow, came to this sthalam, Ashwathavanam, bathed in Brahmateertham, offered milk to the Lord for abhishekam, removed impurities with her tongue, and worshipped in various ways. She created and worshipped a separate Lingam and Theertham. The Lord, accompanied by Mangalavalli, appeared in a divine vision on a Rishabha Vahanam on the Chithirai Amavasai day.

Thus, because Kamadhenu worshipped here, this sthalam came to be known as Avoor Pasupatheeswaram. Dasaratha has visited this sthalam, worshipped, and performed renovations.

King Dharmadhwajan’s leprosy was cured at this site.

Thus, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman visited Avoor Pasupatheeswaram, which possesses many such glories, worshipped, and bestowed Thiru-pathigams. However, due to our lack of merit, those Thiru-pathigams are not available to us now. Having worshipped Avoor Pasupatheeswaram in this manner, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar reached the sthalam called Thiru-palai-thurai and worshipped the Lord there. The holy sthalam of Thiru-palai-thurai is also nearby. It received this name because it was formerly a desert. The history of this sthalam is that Lord Shiva killed a tiger, flayed its skin, and wore it.

This sthalam is located between Kumbakonam and Thanjavur, This sthalam is the nineteenth sthalam among the Kaveri South Bank sthalams. It is located on the banks of the Kudamurutti river, with the palm tree as its sthala tree. That is also why it is called Palai-thurai. The temple faces east. In front of the temple, on the south side, there is a holy tank. The ancient temple has a five-tiered Rajagopuram, followed by an outer prakaram.

Near the gopuram entrance, there is a granary for storing paddy for the temple. This massive granary, built of brick, capable of storing eleven thousand kalams of paddy, is awe-inspiring. It indicates that at one time, this temple had such a large income.

However, today it is not in use. In the northeast corner is the yagasalai, and in the southeast corner, are the Thirumadaippalli (temple kitchen). In this sthalam, the Lord and Goddess appear in their wedding attire. The Goddess is on the right side. In the outer prakaram, there is a separate shrine for the Goddess. The Nandi and Balipitam are here.

To the north of this is the Vasantha Mandapam. Vinayagar is at the gopuram entrance. Upon entering, one finds the Mahamandapam. In the northern part of this mandapam, Lord Nataraja faces south. Opposite, on the south side, are the four Samayacharyas. In the western prakaram, there is a very beautiful stone mandapam.

There are mandapams where deities such as Vinayagar, Somaskandar, Murugan, Vasishta Lingam, and Mahalakshmi reside. In the northern prakaram, sixty-three Nayanmars are enshrined. In the garbhagriha koshtams are Nardana Vinayagar, Oordhuva Thandavar, Dakshinamurthy, and on the west, in the place of Lingodbhavar, is Ardhanareeswarar. In the northern prakaram are Brahma, Durga, and Chandeswarar. One can circumambulate and reach the Ardhamandapam. With two guards, Dvarapalakas, on either side, Palai Vananathar shines.

One can worship Him and then come to the outer prakaram and reach the Amman temple to worship. The Lord’s sacred name here is Palai Vananathar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Thavalaven Nagaiyal, meaning ‘she with white teeth’. The local people call the Amman Thavalambal. Theerthams include Vasishta Theertham, Indra Theertham, Yama Theertham, and Kaveri. The sthala tree is the Palai tree.

This holy sthalam is mentioned as one of the seven Sapthasthanams belonging to Thiru-nalloor. Thirumal, Brahma, the Ashta Dikpalakas, and others have worshipped this sthalam. The Thiru-pathigam composed by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman is not available to us, though he worshipped this sthalam and left. During their exile, the Pandavas, on the advice of Sage Dhaumya, worshipped the Lord of this sthalam, understood the intricacies of archery, went to the netherworld, married Princess Ulupi there, and returned. This is the puranic history. The sages of Tharukavanam, disregarding Lord Shiva, performed a malevolent yagna to destroy Him, creating a tiger and sending it against Lord Shiva.

The Lord flayed the skin of that tiger at this sthalam and wore it. In the Kritha Yuga, unable to bear the cruelty of Bandasuran, the Devas performed a great yagna at this sthalam. The Mother appeared and destroyed Bandasuran.

The Lord pacified the heat of the sacrificial fire created by the Devas with the waters of the Ganga. The sacrificial pit itself became a Theertham. In the Dvapara Yuga, this sthalam was known as Punnagavanam. The mountain The sage Kala, having been insulted, became a bear. Following the command of Sage Agasthya, he came to this sthalam, bathed in the Kaveri, regained his true form, celebrated the Lord’s wedding festival with joy, and then went to Madurai. Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar came to this sthalam and bestowed the Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam.

In the Thiruvasagam Keerthi Thiru Agaval, Manikkavasaga Swamigal sang, “Andharathu ezhindhu vandha azhagamar palaiyul sundaraththanmaiyodu thuthaindhu irundhu aruliyum” (Having risen in the sky, in the beautiful Palai, with beautiful nature, having been immersed and bestowed grace). There is one Thiru-kurunthogai Thiru-pathigam bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal upon this sthalam. It is a very special Thiru-pathigam. This Thiru-pathigam proves that the Thirumurais bestowed by the three (Sambandhar, Appar, Sundarar) are the Tamil Vedas. It is customary to refer to the Vedas as Thrayi, and that Thrayi The Panchaksharam shines as the central jewel in the Yajur Veda, which is in the middle of the Vedas called Thrayi. We know that the Panchaksharam shines in the middle of Sri Rudram.

Similarly, the Thevarams of the three, namely Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, and Sundaramurthy Swamigal, are called Tamil Vedas. Just as the Panchaksharam shines in the middle of the three Vedas - Rig, Yajur, and Sama - similarly, the Panchaksharam shines as the central jewel in the Thirumurais bestowed by the three great ones. The Thevarams sung by the three - Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar, and Sundaramurthy Swamigal - are compiled as seven Thirumurais, namely one, two, three, four, five, six, and seven respectively. Among them, the central jewel is the fourth, fifth, and sixth Thirumurais bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal. Among these three Thirumurais, the central jewel is the fifth Thirumurai. In this fifth Thirumurai, one hundred and one Thiru-pathigams shine.

Among these one hundred and one Thiru-pathigams bestowed by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal, the central Thiru-pathigam, shining as the fifty-first Thiru-pathigam, is the Thiru-palai-thurai Thiru-pathigam. Mostly, Appar Swamigal’s pathigams have ten verses, but this Thiru-pathigam has eleven verses.

Therefore, in the verse that shines as the central jewel among these eleven verses, that is, in the sixth verse, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal has sung the pure Panchaksharam. In the sixth verse, which shines as the central jewel, there are four lines, and in the second line, at the end, Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal has placed that pure Panchaksharam.

Therefore, this Thiru-pathigam serves to prove that the Thirumurais bestowed by the three are the Tamil Vedas.
