Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 153 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part Four Hundred and Fifteen. Thiru-Nindra Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, after worshipping the Lord at Thiru-Aakkoor Thanthondri Maadam, continue their sacred pilgrimage to the sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Sekkizhar Swamigal sings that after worshipping at Thiru-Aakkoor Thanthondri Maadam and venerating many other sacred places, they reached Thiru-Vizhimizhalai.

In the same context, in the Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman Puranam, Sekkizhar Peruman sings that Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, after worshipping at Thiru-Aakkoor Thanthondri Maadam, visited sthalams like Thiru-Miyachur and Thiru-Paambaram, and then reached Thiru-Vizhimizhalai.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman must have worshipped at Thiru-Aakkoor, then visited sthalams like Thiru-Miyachur and Thiru-Paambaram, and subsequently reached Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. The sacred places on the way from Thiru-Aakkoor to Thiru-Miyachur are not mentioned here. The Nayanmars proceeded north from Thiru-Kadhavoor to Thiru-Aakkoor.

Therefore, they must have traveled west from there. If they had taken that route, they would have worshipped at Thiru-Chembanpalli, Thiru-Vizhanagar, Thiru-Mayiladuthurai, and then proceeded south to worship at Thiru-Vazhuvoor Veerattanam before arriving at Thiru-Miyachur.

Thus, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman must have reached Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. In this pilgrimage of these two great personages, Thiru- It was customary for Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to proceed first, followed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman in a palanquin, reaching the sthalam. This can be seen in the Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman Puranam.

Thus, these two great personages arrive at the wondrous sacred sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Let us contemplate a little about the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. This sthalam, Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, is known by ten sacred names: Bhu Kailasam, Kalyana Puram, Panchakshara Puram, Dakshina Kasi, Shanmangala Sthalam, Swetha Kaananam, Akasha Nagaram, Panacharanyam, Netrappana Puram, and Thejini Vanam. This sacred sthalam, Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, is sung by all three Nayanmars: Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. It has twenty-three It possesses. The sacred sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai is the sixty-first sthalam among the Kaveri South Bank sthalams in the Chola country.

It is sung in Sendanar’s Thiruvisaippa. Arunagirinathar’s Thiruppugazh also pertains to this sthalam. This sacred sthalam is located a short distance west from Poonthottam, which is on the road from Mayiladuthurai to Thiruvarur. One can also reach Thiru-Vizhimizhalai from the cities of Thiruvarur and Kumbakonam. The sacred name of the Lord in this sthalam is Vizhi Azhagar. Netrappaneswarar and Vizhi Azhagisar are other sacred names.

The sacred name of the Goddess is Sundarakujambikai, or Azhagu Mulai Ammai. The sacred name of Vinayagar is Padikkasu Vinayagar. The Thiru-Ula Moorthy (processional deity) of this sthalam is Kalyana Sundarar. This sthalam has a total of twenty-three Thiruppathigams. exist. Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman composed fourteen Thiruppathigams, Appar Peruman eight Thiruppathigams, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal one Thiruppathigam, totaling twenty-three Thiruppathigams for this sthalam. There is one Thiruvisaippa pathigam composed by Sendanar.

In the Thirumurais, the history of Thirumal receiving the Chakra in this sthalam is extensively mentioned. There is a Sthala Puranam for Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Its author is Sri Meignana Munivar, who was a disciple of Sri Maraignana Desikar, the second Guru Moorthy of Thiru-Avaduthurai Adheenam. The total number of verses in this Puranam is six hundred and seventy-eight. This Sthala Puranam must have been composed approximately four hundred years ago. The sacred monasteries where Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal stayed and worshipped in this sthalam are located on the North Street here.

This temple contains many inscriptions. The mandapam known as Vavvalnathu or Vavval Netri in this temple is very famous. Sthapathis (temple architects) who undertake temple renovations usually have contracts for all renovations except for certain rare works in some sthalams. Among such exceptional works, the Vavvalnathu mandapam in this sthalam is one. Like the Thillai Moovayiravar and Perunthuvar, in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, Lord Shiva is also one among five hundred Brahmins. Vizhi Sivagra Yogigal, the second Guru Moorthy of Thiru-Kailaya Paramparai Suryanar Koil Adheenam, attained Shiva Paripoornam in this sthalam.

Their Guru Moorthy monasteries are also here. In connection with this sthalam, there is also a prabandham called Azhagiya Mamulai Ammai Pillai Tamil. This sacred sthalam is under the spiritual administration of the Thiru-Kailaya Paramparai Thiru-Avaduthurai Adheenam. The sacred temple faces east. The shrines of the Lord and the Goddess face east. The Goddess’s temple is to the left of the Lord’s temple.

In front of this temple shines the Vishnu Theertham. Upon passing the Rajagopuram entrance, one finds the Thiru-Kalyana Mandapam, known as the Vavvalnathi Mandapam, which adds glory to this sacred temple. No one can help but marvel at the structure of this mandapam, which is wide and constructed with lime plaster without central pillars. The Kodungai in Avudaiyar Koil, the Vavvalnathi Mandapam in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, and the Thiru-Mathil in Kadaram Kondan are considered excellent examples of architectural craftsmanship. It is said to be excellent. The Lord’s sacred wedding festival takes place in this mandapam during the month of Chithirai.

After passing the second gopuram, in the outer circumambulatory path, one can see to the east the Balipeedam where the Lord bestowed coins upon Thiru-Gnanasambandhar, and to the west the Balipeedam where coins were granted to Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal. Nearby, one can have darshan of Padikkasu Vinayagar and the sacred forms of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. After passing the third gopuram entrance, the first prakaram is found. The Vizhinathar sacred temple is built in the Maadakkoil style. In the southern prakaram are the Sthala Vinayagar, and to the west are Somaskandar, Murugan, Mahalakshmi, and other deities. In the northern prakaram, Chandeswarar is enshrined.

In the Sabha located in the northeast direction, Natarajar is enshrined. While circumambulating this prakaram, one can clearly see the Vinnizhi Vimanam, the Lord’s vimanam brought and installed by Thirumal from the divine world. This vimanam, adorned with copper plates and a golden kalasam, possesses a unique beauty and stands distinct from the vimanams of other temples. ‘Vinnizhi Vimanam udai Vinnvar Piran maruvu Vizhi Nagare’ is a Thevaram verse by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman about the vimanam of this sthalam. During the Maha Kumbabhishekam held approximately eight years ago, this vimanam was covered with Panchaloha plates. It is said that when Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman was staying and worshipping in this sthalam, he desired to see the Lord of Seerkazhi.

At that time, the Lord graciously revealed His form as seen in Seerkazhi in this sthalam. The Lord’s shrine is beautifully arranged with the Garbhagriham, Ardhamandapam, and Mahamandapam. In the sanctum sanctorum of the Vinnizhi Vimanam, the Moolalingam, Arulmigu Vizhinatheswarar is enshrined. Behind the Lord is the wedding posture of the Lord with Goddess Parvati. At the entrance are Dvarapalakas. In accordance with this being the sthalam where the Lord married Umaiyamai, there is a pillar called Arasani Kaal at the entrance of the Garbhagriham, and a pillar called Pandhal Kaal in the outer Mahamandapam.

In a separate mandapam within the Mahamandapam, the Kalyana Sundara Swamy, known as Mappillai Swamy, who is unique to this sthalam, is enshrined.

The Lord is seen as a bridegroom embracing Umaiyamai, near the Rishabam. At the Lord’s feet shines a lotus flower, which Thirumal offered by plucking one of His own eyes as a flower. Adjacent to this mandapam are Bhikshatanar, Kalasamharamurthy, and others. Near the Lord’s shrine, Thyagesar is enshrined with the Chakra weapon in hand. After worshipping Him, one can reach the Ambikai shrine through the entrance located in the northern prakaram. One can behold Arulmigu Sundara Kujambikai, who shines as a goddess whose beauty is unparalleled.

It was in this sacred sthalam that Thirumal received the Chakra he desired.

Once, when Lord Shiva was in His divine form with Uma Devi on Mount Kailash, Thirumal worshipped the Lord and made a request. He said, “My Chakra has become very weak.

“Therefore, Your Holiness should bestow upon me the Chakra with which you vanquished the demon Jalandhara.” Lord Shiva, in His compassion, blessed Mahavishnu, saying, “Go to the sthalam named Thejini Vanam, south of the Kaveri, and worship Me.” Mahavishnu took leave of the Lord and immediately came to this sacred sthalam. He worshipped the Lord and decided to create a lotus pond. He invoked the Kaveri River. The Kaveri River branched off west of Thiruvalanjuzhi, flowed as the Arisilaaru to the south of this Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, then turned north to merge with the Ksheera Nadi at the Lord’s shrine, and finally flowed east to join the sea. Vishnu created a pond here, named Padma Theertham, and cultivated red lotuses in it. He brought the Vinnilai Vimanam, supported by sixteen lions, and enshrined Lord Shiva in it.

“Daily, Mahavishnu bathed in the Theertha Pushkarani, adorned himself with Vibhuti and Rudraksha, and worshipped Lord Shiva according to scriptural injunctions with a thousand lotus flowers.

“Thus, daily, he offered a thousand lotus flowers for the thousand sacred names of Lord Shiva. He continued to perform the archana.

“One day, by the divine grace of Lord Shiva, one flower was missing from the thousand. Vishnu considered this to be the Lord’s divine will. Instead of the lotus flower, that is, since one flower was missing, he plucked his own right eye and offered it at the Lord’s sacred feet.

“At that moment, Lord Shiva, easily accessible through love, appeared before Vishnu. He bestowed upon Vishnu the Chakra weapon with which He had vanquished the demon Jalandhara.

“Afterwards, Vishnu stayed here for some time, worshipped, and created a theertham named Vishnu Theertham in his own name.

“Then he returned to his own world.

“Once before, Lord Brahma became infatuated with Tilottama, whom he had created. Lord Brahma absolved himself of that sin by worshipping Lord Shiva in this sacred sthalam. Kathyayanamuni, the foremost among sages, reached this sthalam, built an ashram on the bank of the Theertha Pushkarani, bathed daily in the Theertha Pushkarani, worshipped Azhagiya Mamulai Ammai and Vizhinathar, and performed severe penance with his wife in the Pannagasalai. He had no offspring, so he performed rare yagnas for this purpose.

“At that time, the Goddess appeared as Annapoorani, holding a vessel of food in her left hand and a ladle for serving food in her right hand, and asked the great ascetic, “What boon do you desire?” To this, Kathyayanamuni replied, “Mother, you yourself should come as my daughter.” The Goddess granted this boon to the sage. The Goddess took leave of the Supreme Lord and appeared in the form of a beautiful female child in a magnificent blue lotus flower in the Theertha Pushkarani near the Pannagasalai where the sage was performing penance. The sage’s wife, named Thumangalai, saw her, was filled with joy, took the child, embraced her to her chest, and gave her to Kathyayanamuni. They named the child Kathyayini and raised her. When Kathyayini reached marriageable age, the sage performed severe penance to Lord Shiva. Lord Shiva, moved by the sage’s penance, appeared.

“The sage prostrated at the Lord’s sacred feet and prayed, “O Lord, You Yourself should come here in the guise of a bridegroom and marry this maiden.” Lord Shiva, pleased in His heart, blessed him, saying, “We shall marry on the Magam star day in the month of Chithirai.” As the Lord had promised the sage, on the Magam star day in the month of Chithirai, He departed from Sri Kailash, accompanied by Thirumal, Brahma, Nandi, and other ganas, adorned in all ornaments, and proceeded south to reach the place where Kathyayanamuni resided in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Kathyayanamuni welcomed the Lord, worshipped Him, and made arrangements for the wedding. With grand decorations and great splendor, the wedding ceremony of Sri Kailasapathi and Kathyayini Ambikai took place.

“Afterwards, the Lord and the Goddess went in procession through the sacred streets and entered the temple.

“At that time, Kathyayanamuni had a doubt: whether the one who came as the bridegroom was indeed Lord Shiva. Knowing this, the Lord, in order to dispel the sage’s doubt, appeared there in the form of the bridegroom, radiating light, with the lotus-eye that Thirumal had offered instead of a lotus flower, and the Vilanga fruit offered by the devotee Mizhalai Kurumbar.

“At that moment, the sage fell at the sacred feet of Lord Shiva and worshipped Him. His doubt dispelled, Kathyayanamuni danced in ecstasy.

“The Lord forever resides in this sthalam. As they wished, praying that He should be graciously seated, the Peruman is seated there even today in the same bridal form for many to see.

“Therefore, it is true that those who wish for an early marriage will achieve it quickly if they come to this sthalam and worship the Peruman in that manner. This Thiru-sthalam is where the history of Shvetaketu, similar to the sacred history of Maharishi Markandeya, took place. Emperor Sibi came to this sthalam, worshipped the Peruman, performed sacred services, and brought five hundred Brahmins, who were well-versed in the Vedas and Agamas, to Thiru-vizhimizhalai. He provided them with all their needs and made them reside there.

“At that time, Lord Shiva, in the guise of a Brahmin, also received alms as one of the five hundred.

“Then, Maharishi Narada pointed out to Emperor Sibi that Lord Shiva was receiving alms as one of the five hundred Brahmins.

“At that time, Lord Shiva, the king, was greatly pleased. Afterwards, Emperor Sibi, with the help of those five hundred Brahmins, conducted daily pujas and festivals for Lord Shiva with great splendor. He provided everything necessary for the temple, received many boons, returned to his city, and lived happily. The couple Pururavas and Bhadravalli came to this sthalam, performed sacred services, received boons, and rejoiced. Kamadhenu worshipped Lord Shiva. The milk with which Kamadhenu performed abhishekam overflowed, becoming known as ‘Arasil Nadhi,’ and merged with the river at the Swami Sannidhi.

“Manu worshipped Lord Shiva at this sthalam. This sthalam was a forest of Thejini, meaning a forest of Veeli plants.

“In addition, many other trees like sandalwood, champak, and jackfruit were dense in that forest.

“At that time, there was a hunter named Mizhalai Kurumbar. He saw Lord Shiva, was filled with joy, and worshipped Him with love, offering a Vilangkani fruit daily.

“The Lord appeared before him and blessed him. From then on, he adopted an ascetic form, performed great penances, and worshipped Lord Shiva. Through the power of his penance, he attained the eight great siddhis. The form of the Vilangkani fruit accepted by the Peruman is still visible at the sacred feet of Manavala Peruman. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and Appar Swamigal received gold coins here. We will discuss this in detail.

“There are five sacred places (Panchakrosalams) associated with this sthalam. They are Vasishteswaram, which is located in the northeast direction of this sthalam, in Vadugakkudi, on the east bank of the Kirthiman River, where only a Moolingam is visible. Vasishta Theertham and Theertham are in the form of a field.

“Secondly, Indireswaram is a temple in the nearby Kadkambadi.

“Thirdly, the Lingam worshipped by Manu, now known as Manu Thapacheri, is a temple. There is also Manu Theertham.

“Fourthly, Gautameswaram is in the southeast direction of this sthalam, in Sambandan Padi, where only a Lingam is visible in the field. The Theertham is a field.

“Fifthly, Kaleswaram is in the south, on the bank of Kallikulam. Currently, it is in Vishnupuram, on the bank of Dharmakulam, and is a temple. Next is Markandeswaram, which is a temple in the first tier. Next is Subeswaram, which is a temple in Sembankudi. Next is Abhimukteswaram, which is a temple on the west, on the bank of Thamaraikulam. Tenth is Bhadravallieswaram, which is a temple in the south.

“The eleventh is Svargavadhaneeswaram, which was near the Kathyayaniyamma temple. Currently, it is in the Bhadravallisar temple. In the northern street, there are separate temples in the sacred matham where Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-navukkarasu Swamigal resided. The deities are Thiru-moolattanam, Mayuranathar, Madhyarjunewarar, Annamalaiyar, Brahmalingam, Thyagarajar, and many other Lingams.

“Now, in this sthalam, there are many Utsava Moorthies (processional deities) such as Natarajar, Somaskandar, Chandrasekarar, Chakradhanar, Bhikshadanar, Kalasamharar, Svargavadhaneeswarar, Nayanmars, and others. The Sthala Vriksham (sacred tree) is different for each Yuga. In the first Yuga, the sandalwood tree was the Sthala Vriksham. In the second Yuga, the Champak tree. In the third Yuga, the Veeli plant. In the fourth Yuga, the Jackfruit tree were the Sthala Vrikshams.

“The Theerthams (sacred waters) in this sthalam are Pushkarani Theertham, Vishnu Theertham, Brahma Theertham, Thiru-veni Sangamam, Padma Theertham, Indra Theertham, Yama Theertham, Varuna Theertham, Kubera Theertham, Gautama Theertham, Markanda Theertham, Viswamitra Theertham, Gayatri Theertham, Savitri Theertham, Saraswati Theertham, Lakshmi Theertham, Bhoomi Devi Theertham, Rudra Theertham, Kapila Theertham, Bhadravalli Theertham, Parvati Theertham, Manu Theertham, Vasishta Theertham, Abhimukta Theertham, and Samudra Theertham, totaling twenty-five Theerthams. In this sthalam, the Brahmotsavam takes place in the month of Chithirai, with the Dhvajarohanam (flag hoisting) on the Mrigasirisha star, the Thiru-kalyanam (sacred marriage) on the Magam star, and the Theertham (sacred bath) on the Chithirai star. Besides these, the Sashti Utsavam, Thiru-vathirai Utsavam, and Navaratri Utsavam are also celebrated. One-day festivals like Avani Moolam are also held. All these are the news and special features of the Thiru-vizhimizhalai Sthala Puranam. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman arrive at this sthalam.

“Let us proceed with our contemplation.”
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 154 — Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 416. Thiru-nindra Sarukkam. Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman arrive at Thiru-vizhimizhalai. The sacred devotees (Thiru-thondar) and Brahmins of Lord Shiva residing in Thiru-vizhimizhalai come to the outskirts of Thiru-vizhimizhalai and greet and worship Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman.

Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman worship the devotees who came to greet them.

Thus, the devotees of Thiru-vizhimizhalai and the two great spiritual leaders mingle with each other. Those who were already united by love now meet directly. A large gathering of Thiru-vizhimizhalai’s devotees welcome the two great spiritual leaders. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, in his Thevaram, has sung about how the devotees of Thiru-vizhimizhalai came to greet him, saying, “Known devotees went in every direction, eagerly welcoming me to Vizhimizhalai.” This conveys to us the abundance of the devotees’ love. It is for this reason that the Lord of Mizhalai placed gold coins for both Nayanmars, for the devotees of Thiru-vizhimizhalai, and protected them from suffering throughout the famine, which is a significant point.

To welcome the two great spiritual leaders arriving at Thiru-vizhimizhalai, the Brahmins living in that city decorate the main streets of the sacred city. At the entrances of their mansions, they arrange rows of auspicious lamps, large banana trees, and areca nut trees. They welcome them, holding full golden pots. Accepting their welcome, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman comes to the sacred temple of Thiru-vizhimizhalai and arrives at the entrance of the temple, which has a celestial vimanam. Having arrived thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman enters the sacred temple, circumambulates the sacred temple of Lord Shiva, who graciously resides in Thiru-vizhimizhalai, bows in the sacred courtyard, falls at the sacred feet of the Peruman, rises, and is overwhelmed with emotion. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman joins his two hands above his head and worships the Lord’s sacred feet.

Love fills the heart of Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, and it overflows. His heart melts and dissolves. Tears flow like a waterfall on his sacred body. Having worshipped the Peruman in this manner, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman sings the Thiru-thandakam, which conveys the idea that those who do not join the Lord with the red matted hair will join the path of evil. “Those who do not join the Lord with the red matted hair will join the path of evil” is the central theme of the pathigam sung by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman at Thiru-vizhimizhalai. In each verse of this pathigam, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman has used the refrain, “Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil.” Earlier, when worshipping the Lord of Thiru-nageswaram, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar stated in a negative sense, “Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-nageswaram will not join the good path.”

Now, Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar, who had previously stated in a negative sense that those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-nageswaram will not join the good path, now affirms in a positive sense that if they do not join the good path, they will indeed join the evil path. Appar Swamigal has blessed this sthalam with eight Thiru-pathigams.

At this time, he blessed the Thiru-thandakam pathigam that begins with “Poranai Irurivai Porvaiyanai,” which is the fiftieth Thiru-pathigam in the sixth Thiru-murai. Let us now contemplate that Thiru-pathigam.

“Poranai Irurivai Porvaiyanai, Puliyathale Udai Aadai Potrinanai, Paranai Mathiyanai Pagalananai, Palluyirai Neduvelliyai Paranthu Nindra Neeranai Katranai Theeyananai Ninaiyathar Purameriya Ninaitha Theiva Theranai Thiru-vizhimizhalaiyanai Serathar Theenrikke Serkinrare Savantha” “He who wears the ashes and bones from the cremation ground, with a skull and hair-rope, He who is the Pasupatha in the form of a mendicant, He who consumed all the sacrifices offered by the ancient gods, He who is Ekamban of Kanchi, He who turned red when Yama, who had approached the ocean, fell, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who taught dharma under the banyan tree, He who loved Agastya, He who stood when Brahma and Vishnu searched, He who drank the poison from the ocean, He who conquered the five senses while united with the beautiful maiden, He who resided in Meeyachur, He who went to measure the penance of the slender maiden, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who is pure, He who is the radiant coral light, He who is the mother who stands as a support for all living beings, He who gave the discus to Markandeya,” “He who is Shankara, He whose mouth recites the Chandoga Sama, He who is in the hearts of those who meditate, He who is far from those who utter the five letters with deceit, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil.

“He who is good among the fragrant ones, He who consumed the poison that came as evil, He who is immortal even if other gods perish, He who is a unique light that cannot be understood by those who know the past, present, and future, He who destroyed the three cities in the two skies, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who has a dark throat, He who has the moon on his matted hair like a lightning bolt in the sky, He who rains everywhere, He who performs the dance of a mendicant, He who holds the trident while the split ghosts roar, He who is truthful without falsehood, He who creates the life that encompasses the earth and the heavens,” “Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who is great, He who is the Lord of those who seek refuge, He who became the six different religions, He who entered all things, He who is common to all, He who is worthy of all things praised by the inhabitants of the golden world, He who is the truth that is not other than Himself, He who made the great mountain the center, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who is the son who crushed the shoulders of the king of the celestials, He who resided in Valai Kulam and Marai Kadu, He who is the flesh, He who is the life, He who went to know the state of the great penance of Arjuna one day, He who is the eye, He who resided in Kailash, He who has the Ganga in his matted hair, He who is honey to those who mingle with Him, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who is pervasive, He who is many on this side, He who is Pasupathi, He who grants liberation to devotees,”

“He who is the boon, He who is in the hearts of those who worship, He who destroyed the three cities with the arrow of fire, He who is the arrow, He who is the ascetic who placed the arrow under your feet, He who has the green head adorned with a crown of matted hair, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil. He who is the meaning, He who fearlessly cut off one of the five heads of Brahma, He who crushed the shoulders of the demon who lifted the mountain, He who listened to the music of the seven strings, He who crushed the moon, He who took the teeth of the sun, He who, at the request of the celestials for Bhagiratha, gathered the flowing waters of the Ganga like snow, Those who do not join the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai will join the path of evil.” 

“Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, having worshipped the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai, blessed this Thiru-thandakam pathigam at this time. Although both great spiritual leaders, the Samayacharyas, visited the sacred temple together, even though they visited the sacred temple together, this is the Puranam of Thiru-navukkarasu, so it describes the worship methods and actions performed by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman separately here. Sekkizhar Peruman, where necessary, brings them together and shows us their actions.

“Similarly, in the Puranam of Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, at this place, that is, where Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman visited Thiru-vizhimizhalai, Sekkizhar Peruman specifically sings about how the Brahmins greeted Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, how Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman entered the sacred temple and worshipped, and how he came out and resided in a sacred matham.

“Thus, after completing their worship, the two great personalities and the devotees resided in different sacred mathams for many days. Sambandha Peruman and Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman stayed in the sacred mathams in Thiru-vizhimizhalai for many days, performing darshan and singing sacred pathigams.

“In addition, other devotees also joined these two great personalities and worshipped the Lord. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman as ‘Meimai Arunthavargal’ (those who performed true penance). The meaning of this is that just as the Lord’s form is truth, these two great personalities, by constantly clinging to the Lord, became of the very nature of the Lord. The meaning is that they were those who performed rare Shiva pujas that bestow the state of truth.

“Therefore, their sacred words became true sacred words and acted as the Lord’s own sacred words.

“Moreover, the other devotees who had the great fortune of sitting with these two great personalities are also considered worthy devotees who attained liberation. worthy devotees.

“Thus, Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman stayed in Thiru-vizhimizhalai for a long time.

“At that time, there was a drought in Thiru-vizhimizhalai. Even the Kaveri, which always flowed without fail, changed its season of water flow. Water is essential for crops and living beings. At a time when water was needed for crops and living beings, the Kaveri did not provide water, and the season changed. The rain also decreased.

“Therefore, food items that depend on water became scarce. Consequently, all living beings that depend on food suffered. Poverty came there. It did not rain, and there was no water in the Kaveri.

“Therefore, paddy crops did not grow, and there was a shortage of food items. All living beings and people suffered. Poverty came, and there was a famine in the world.

“Consequently, the living beings of the world suffered from hunger.

“Thus, the devotees in Thiru-vizhimizhalai also suffered from hunger.

“At that time, Lord Shiva, the Lord of Thiru-vizhimizhalai, appeared in the dreams of both Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman.

“Lord Shiva appeared separately in the dreams of both, with matted red hair, holding a deer and an axe, and blessed them. He said, “Due to this change in time, this period of famine, you will not be disheartened. You will not diminish in your state. Nevertheless, to give to the devotees who worship you, I will give you a gold coin daily.” Thus, Lord Shiva appeared in the dreams of Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and spoke. “When famine and poverty come to the world, and all people suffer from the disease of hunger, they are helpless.” Therefore, Lord Shiva, who appeared in their dreams, said, “Even though you will not suffer from this hunger or famine, to give to those who worship you, I will give you a gold coin.” He blesses, saying, “We are giving.” The implication here is that wealth is acquired only for the purpose of giving to those who need it in a good way.

“Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman were of the nature of those who have renounced everything. They would view running gold and red gold equally. They were of the nature that they desired nothing but to worship with increasing love.

“Therefore, even though they did not need all these things, the Lord, intending to protect the world through them and to manifest the greatness of Lord Shiva’s servitude, appeared in their dreams and blessed them, saying, “Even though you will not suffer from the disease of hunger, take the coin we give and feed the devotees.” It is certain that if the Peruman had not appeared in their dreams and blessed them in this manner, these two great individuals would not have expected coins. “My duty is to sustain my servant, and my duty is to serve and remain.” This is the mindset of the Nayanmars.

“Therefore, it became the Lord’s duty to protect the devotees who worshipped them, as they had completely surrendered themselves to the Lord.

“Thus, to protect the devotees who worshipped Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, the Lord appeared in the dreams of these two great individuals and promised to give them a coin daily.

“Lord Shiva says, “I will give you a Padikkasu.” ‘Padi’ means a daily prescribed order.

“Therefore, Padikkasu means, “I will give you a coin daily without fail,” says Lord Shiva. To the east and west of the celestial vimanam of Thiru-vizhimizhalai, there are altars. On the altar to the east, the Lord grants one gold coin per day to Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, and on the altar to the west, to Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, as revealed by the Lord in their dreams. There are altars to the east and west of the sacred temple. The eastern altar is directly opposite the Swami Sannidhi.

“There, he grants one coin to Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman. On the western altar, he grants one coin to Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman. The western altar is directly behind the Swami Sannidhi.

“Thus, by the grace of Lord Shiva, a gold coin is received daily at the eastern and western altars. These two great individuals use those gold coins and feed the sacred devotees. They announce twice a day throughout the village, proclaiming, “All who are devotees of Lord Shiva, the primordial God, come and partake of food.” They used the coin granted by the Lord to provide food. Sekkizhar Peruman’s verse at this point is: “The gold coins received by the grace of the Lord of the dark-throated ones, the wealth that increased for many, the devotees of the Lord, all come and eat, thus proclaiming twice a day, they announced and provided food, dispelling poverty.” Sivakavimani says that this verse is of great significance and is recited during blessings during Maheswara Puja. The author notes that this sacred hymn is glorious in that it advises devotees to utilize the wealth bestowed by the Lord for the benefit of other devotees, thereby attaining good fortune. All wealthy devotees should follow this path and attain benefit, writes Sivakavimani.

“Thus, with the sacred coins granted by the Lord, Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman procured all necessary provisions for food, prepared meals, and fed all the devotees of Shiva, thereby alleviating and eradicating poverty. Let us resume our reflection.”
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 155 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 417. Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. When famine struck Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, the Lord granted a sacred coin daily to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman, one at the western and the other at the eastern pedestal. With these, they appeased the hunger of Shiva’s devotees and fed them.

Sekkizhar Peruman then sings: “The Lord of Mizhalai, from the Lord, received the sacred milk from the holy breast of the Daughter of the Himalayas, and as the great son, he received coins with ‘vasi’ (value). Due to his servitude of manual service, Vakkisar received coins without ‘vasi’.” Thus sings Sekkizhar Peruman. To these two great personages, Lord Shiva grants sacred coins daily. The sacred coin bestowed upon Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman at the eastern pedestal was a coin with ‘vasi’ (value). The sacred coin granted by Lord Shiva to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman at the western pedestal was a coin without ‘vasi’. If a coin has ‘vasi’, ‘vasi’ means a circle or mark, so exchanging that coin for food items was somewhat difficult.

Lord Shiva bestows such a coin with ‘vasi’ upon Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman. To Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, however, He grants a coin without ‘vasi’ at the western pedestal.

Therefore, with that coin, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman quickly obtained the necessary food items to feed the devotees in his sacred monastery and serves them food. Sekkizhar Peruman explains here why Lord Shiva gave coins in two different ways to the devotees. Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman is the sacred son of the Lord. Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman partook of the sacred milk from the Divine Mother. By this relationship, he is the son of Lord Shiva. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, however, serves as a devotee to the Lord, as a servant to the Lord.

Therefore, the coin he received, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, is a servant performing manual service to the Lord. Hence, the coin given to him was a coin without ‘vasi’.

The Lord did not give coins for the Nayanmars; He placed coins for the devotees who worship the Nayanmars. He placed coins to alleviate the hunger and suffering of those devotees.

Therefore, even though He placed coins for the devotees who worship the Nayanmars, He gives those coins to the devotees through the Nayanmars.

Thus, the Lord bestows coins in a manner appropriate to these two Nayanmars. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, as Vakkisar, serves the Lord in the capacity of a servant, performing vocal service and manual service. Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman, on the other hand, receives a golden cymbal from the Lord, receives a palanquin, and receives a pearl canopy.

Thus, receiving these, Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman is in a state of performing service without his sacred body experiencing any hardship. As the saying goes, “Labor brings wages,” Lord Shiva gives Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman a coin without ‘vasi’ for the manual service he performs. If Lord Shiva were to give Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman a coin with ‘vasi’, it would imply that the Lord, as a master, is extracting work without providing appropriate wages for the sacred service Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman performs.

Therefore, there is no fault even if the coin given to Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman, who is in the state of a son without physical hardship, has ‘vasi’. However, Lord Shiva thus ordains that a coin without ‘vasi’ must be granted to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, who performs sacred service with his body, hands, and voice.

Thus, He gives Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman a coin with ‘vasi’.

Therefore, Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman sang a Thiru-Pathikam, requesting, “Grant me coins without ‘vasi’,” and received coins without ‘vasi’ from Lord Shiva. That sacred history we shall see in the sacred history of Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman.

Thus, as the Lord granted sacred coins daily to these two great personages, they, in their sacred monasteries, fed the devotees.

The devotees rejoiced and found happiness always. This act of placing sacred coins for the Nayanmars is attested as internal evidence in the Thevara Thiru-Pathikams, the sacred utterances of these two great spiritual leaders. The places where Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman resided were called sacred monasteries. These sacred monasteries are now established as separate temples in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, bearing the names of these two, and worship is conducted there.

Thus, these two great personages have been performing this Shiva-service for a long time. It is mentioned here as “long time,” implying that they must have stayed in Thiru-Vizhimizhalai for at least a year, receiving sacred coins from the Lord, feeding the devotees, and alleviating the hunger caused by the famine. It is understood that during their stay and worship, these two great personages would have composed numerous Thevara Thiru-Pathikams. Among them, fourteen Thiru-Pathikams composed by Aludaiya Pillaiyar, Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman, are now available to us. Eight Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman are available to us.

Thus, for a long time, both performed this sacred service.

After some time, rain fell again, the Kaveri river overflowed, paddy crops grew abundantly, and Thiru-Vizhimizhalai and the world prospered.

Now, in this period, we saw that eight Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman are available to us. We have already reflected on the first Thiru-Pathikam.

Let us reflect on the other seven Thiru-Pathikams. The second Thiru-Pathikam, pertaining to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, is the sixty-fourth Thiru-Pathikam in the Fourth Thiru-Murai. It is a Thiru-Nerisai Thiru-Pathikam.

“Poothathin padaiyar paambin pooninar poornanoolar Seethaththil pozhindha thingal kozhundhar nanjazhundhu kandar Geethaththil pozhindha osai kelviyar velviyalar Vedaththin porular” Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare. “Kalaiyil kathirsai meni kangulil karuththa kandar Malaiyil mathiyam serntha magudaththar mathuvum paalum Alaiyil paagum pola anniththittiyarkku endrum Velaiyin amuthar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.” “Varunthina nerunal endrai vazhangina nalar arkizh Irunthu nan porulgal nalvarkku iyambinar iruvarodum Porunthinar pirinthu thampaal poyyaram avarkkandrum Virunthinar thirunthu Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.” “Nilaiyila oor moondrondra nerupparikaattambaaga Silaiyu nanathuvu naagam kondavar devar thangal Thalaiyinaal thariththa enpum thalaimayir vadamum poonda Vilaiyilaavedar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.” “Maraiyidai porular mottin malar” vazhi vasathenar Karavidai paalin neyyar karumbinil kattiyalar Piraiyidai paambu kondrai pinaiyal ser sadaiyul neerar Viragidai theeyar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.“ “Ennagaththillai allar ularallar imavaan petra Pennagaththaraiyar kaatril peruvazhi iruvaraagi Mannagaththaivar neeril nalvar theeyathanil moovar Vinnagaththoruvar Vizhi Mizhalaiyul vigithanare.” “Santhani kongaiyalor panginar samavedar Enthaiyum enthai thanthai thanthaiyumaya eesar Anthiyodu udai anthanalar an neyyal vetkum venthazhal oruvar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.” “Neetrinai niraiya poosi nitthal ayiram pookkondu Etruli orunaal ondru kuraiya kan niraiyavitta Aattralukku aazhi nalki avan konarnthu izhichchum koyil” Veetrirunthu alippar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigithanare.” “Siththi seybavarkkellaam servidam sendru kooda Paththi seybavargal paavam paraippavar irappilalar Mutthisai pavalameeni muthiroli neelakandar Vitthinil mulaiyar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.” “Tharukkina arakkan therur sarathi thadainilathu Poruppinai eduththa thozhum ponmudi patthum punnay Nerippu unda angu alari meendu ninainthu adiparava tham vazh Viruppodungoduppar Vizhimizhalaiyul vigirthanare.” 

Now, the third Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Vizhimizhalai is the ninety-fifth Thiru-Pathikam in the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Viruttha Thiru-Pathikam.

“Vaan sottachchotta nindrattum valarmathiyodaye Then sottachchotta nindrattum thirukkondrai sennivai theer maanpettai” nokki manaleer mani neer mizhalai ullir naan satta ummai marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.“ “Anthamum aathiyum aagi nindru eerandam en thisaiyum Panthamum veedum parappukkinreer pasu etrukkanthir venthazhal ompu mizhalai ullir ennai thenthisaikke unthidum pothu marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.” “Alaikkindra neer nilam kaatranal ambaramaagi nindreer Kalaikkandru serum karaththir kalaipporulaagi nindreer Vilakkinri nalkum mizhalaiyullir meyyil kaiyodu kaalkulaikkinru nummai marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.” “Theeththozhilaan thalai theeyilittu seytha velvi setreer Peythozhilattiyai petrudaiyeer pidiththu thiriyum veyth thozhilalar mizhalaiyullir vikki anjaliththum otthozhinthu um” marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.” “Thotpatta naagamum soolamum sutriyum putthimaiyan Merpatta anthanar veezhiyum ennaiyum verudaiyeer Natpatta vanthu piranthen irakka naman thamartham Kotpatttu nummai marakkinum ennai kuri konmine.” “Kandiyil patta kazhuththudaiyeer karikattilitta Pandiya parikalaththir pathiveezhik kondir Undiyar pattini noyill urakkaththil ummai avar Kondiyil pattu marakkinum ennai kuri konmine.” “Thotramkandan siramonru kondir thuyavellarithu ondru Etram kondir ezhil veezhi mizhalai irukkai kondir Seetram kondinmel sivanthatthor paasaththaal veesiya vengootram kandu ummai marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.” “Suzhipatta gangaiyum thingalum soodi sokkam payintrir” Pazhipatta paambarai pattrudaiyeer padar theepparuga Vizhipatta kaamanai vitteer mizhalaiyullir piravi chollipattu nummai marakkinum ennai kurikkonmine.“ “Pillaiyirpatta pirai mudiyir maraiyothavalleer Vellaiyirpatthatthor neetrir virineer mizhalaiyullir Nallaiyirpattaivar nakkarai pikka naman thamar thang Kollaiyil pattu marakkinum ennai kurikkolmine.” “Karukkontharakkan kaiyilayai pattriya kaiyum meyyum Nerukkendrirachcha sevadiyal kootrai neeru seytheer Veri kondrai malai mudiyir virineer mizhalaiyullir Irakkinru nummai marakkinum ennai kurikkolmine.” 

Now, the fourth Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar for Thiru-Vizhimizhalai is the twelfth Thiru-Pathikam in the Fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam.

Sambalam karainthu kaithozhuvaraiyum kaathalan Varainthu vaithozhuvaraiyum vaadalan niranthapaaridaththodavar Nitthalam virainthu povathum Vizhimizhalaiyeke.” “Etruvelkodi eesan than aathirai naatram Sooduvar nannarunthingalar neetruchchanthana vellai viravalar Vetru kolamkol Vizhimizhalaiye.” “Punaippor soolaththan porvidaiyoorthiyan vinaivel naagaththin venmazhu vazhinan Ninaiya nindravan eesanaiye enna vinaiyilar thozhum Vizhimizhalaiye.” “Maadaththaadu manaththudan vaiththavar kodaththar kurukketthiraththar palar Paadaththar pazhippar pazhippallaththor vedaththar thozhum Vizhimizhalaiye.” “Eduththa velkodi erudaiyan thamar udupparkovanam unpathu pichchaiye Keduppathavathu keezh nindra valvinai viduththu povathu Vizhimizhalaiyeke.” Kuzhalaiyazh mozhiyar isai vetkaiyal uzhalaiyakkaiyai oonum unarvileer Thalalai neermadi kollan min satrinom mizhalaiyan adi saara vinnazhvare.“ “Theeran thee thiralan sadai thangiya neeran aadiya neetran vanthar kondrai Tharan malaiyan thannarunkanniyan veeran Vizhimizhalai vigirthane.” “Eriyinar iraiyar idukattidai nariyinar pariya magizhkindrathor Periyanar tham pirappodu saathalai viriyinar thozhum Vizhimizhalaiye.” “Neenda soozh sadai melor nilamathi kaandusevadi melor kanai kazhal Venduvavar avar veethi pugunthilar meendum povathu Vizhimizhalaiyeke.” “Paalai yazhodu sevazhi pankola malai vanavar vanthu vazhipadum alaiyarazhal antha” Ahuthi velaiyar thozhum Vezhi Mizhalaiye.” “Mazhalai etru manalan thirumalai suzhala aarthethutthan mudi tholira Kazhalgol kaalin thiruviral oondralum mizhalaiyanadi vazhkana vittathe.” 

Let us continue to reflect on the other Thiru-Pathikams pertaining to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 156 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 418. Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Among the eight Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, the fifth Thiru-Pathikam begins with “En ponne em imaiyor thozhu paingazhal.” It is a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam, the thirteenth Thiru-Pathikam in the Fifth Thiru-Murai.

“En ponne imaiyor thozhu paingazhal Nanponne nalan theengarri ondrillen Semponne Thiru-Velimizhalaiyul Anbane adiyenai kurikkole.” “Kanninaal kali koora kaiyaal thozhuthu Ennumaaru ariyathu izhaippen thannai Vinnullor thozhum Vizhimizhalaiyul Annale adiyenai kurikkole.” “Nalame visumbe” nalan theemaiye Kalame karutthe karutthaal thozhum seelame Thiru-Vizhimizhalaiyul Kolame adiyenai kurikkole.“ “Mutthane muthalva mugizhum mulai Otthane oruva uruvaagiya Siththane Thiru-Vizhimizhalaiyul Atthanae adiyenai kurikkole.” “Karuvane karuvaayth thelivaarkkellaam Oruvane uyirppaay unarvaay nindra Thiruvane Thiru-Vizhimizhalaiyul Guruvane adiyenai kurikkole.” “Kaaththane pozhil ezhaaiyum kaathalaal Aaththane amararkku ayanthan thalai Serththane Thiru-Vizhimizhalaiyul Kooththane adiyenai kurikkole.” “Neethivaanavar nitthal niyamam seyth Othivaanarum unaraathathor Vedhiyaa vithithaa Thiru-Vizhiyul Aathiye adiyenai kurikkole.” Pazhagi ninnadi soodiya paalanai Kazhagin mel vaiththa kaalanai saadiya Azhagane ani Vizhimizhalaiyul Kuzhagane adiyenai kurikkole.” “Andavaanavar koodik kadaintha nanj Undavaanavane unarvondrilen Vindavaan pozhil Vizhimizhalaiyul Kondane adiyenai kurikkole.” “Orutthan ongalai thaangalutran uram Varutthinaay vanjanen manam manniya Thirutthanae Thiru-Vizhimizhalaiyul Arutthanae adiyenai kurikkole.” 

Now, the sixth Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for the sacred sthalam of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai is a Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathikam, the fifty-first Thiru-Pathikam in the Sixth Thiru-Murai.

“Kayilaya malaivullar karonaththar kanthamathanaththular kalaththiyar Mayiladu thuraiyullar” Magalaththar vakkaraiyar sakkaram maarkku eenthar vaayntha ayilvaay soolamum kapaalamum amarum thirukkaraththar aaneru eri veyilaya sothi vilangu neetrar Vizhimizhalaiye mevinare.“ “Poothiyani ponniraththar poonanoolar pongaravar sankarar venkuzhaiyor kaathar kethichcharam mevinar kedaraththar kedila vada athigai veerattaththar maathuyaram theerththu ennai uyya kondar mazhapaadimeya mazhuvaazhanar vedikudiyullar meeyachchurar Vizhimizhalaiye mevinare.” “Annamalaiye amarnthar arur ullar alappoorar anthanargal maadakkoyil unnaligaiyar umayalodum imaiyor perumanar otriyurar pennakadaththu perunthunganai maadaththar koodaththar” Peravurar vinnorgalellaam virumbiyeththa Vizhimizhalaiye mevinare.” “Venkatthar sengattangudiyar venni nannagarar vetkalaththar vedanavar pankattum vandar pazhanaththullar parayththuraiyar sirappalliyullar pandor venkottuk karungazhitrai pizhapattri uriththu urivai porththa vidalai vedam vinkattum pirainuthali anja katti Vizhimizhalaiye mevinare.” “Pudaichoozhndha poothangal vedampaada puliyur sittrambalaththai nadamaaduvar udaichoozhndha puliththozhar kalikachchi mel thazhiyullar kulirsolai ekampaththar kadaisoozhndhu palitherum kankalanar kazhumalaththar sezhimalaththar kuzhaliyooodum vidaichoozhndha velkodiyar malku selva Vizhimizhalaiye mevinare perum puliyur virumbi” The Perumpazhiyar, the Perumparra Puliyur Mulattanattar, the Irumbuthalar, the Irumbuli Yerar, the Innambarar, the Ingoymalaiyar, the sweet-worded Karumbanaiyal with Uma, the Karugavoorar, the Karuppariyalurar, the Karaveerattar, the beloved immortals, day and night, praised and worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. The Maraikattar, the Valivalattar, the Vaimur Meyar, the Valkozhi Putturar, the Magazhattar, the Karai Kattu Kandanaar, the Kapaliyar, the Karkudiyar, the Virkudiyar, the Kaanapperar, the Parai Kattu Kuzhi Vizhiya Pal Peychuzha Pazhaiyanur Alangattu Adigal, who once showed fear, the cruel Yama, fled.

They worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. The Anjai Kalaththullar, the Aiyarrullar, the Arurar. The Perurars, the Azhundur Ullar, the Thanjai Thali Kuluththar, the Thakkalurars, the Santhai Ayavanthi Thanginar Tham, the Nanjai Thamakk Amudavunda Nambar, the Nageshwaraththullar, the Naraiyurars, who rescued me from the prison of harsh words, worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. The Kondal Ullar, the Kondichcharaththinnullar, the Kovalur Veerattam Koyil Kondar, the Thandalaiyar, the Thalaiyalangattu Ullar, the Thalaichchangai Perungoyil Thanginar Tham, the Vandalodu Manarkonarum Ponni Nannir Valanjoliyar, the Vaigalin Men Madaththullar, the Venthalai Man Kai Konda Vigithavedar, worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. The Harichchandraththullar, the Ambarullar, who are rare even to Hari, Brahma, and Indra, the Purichchandraththullar, the Bogaththullar, who with the daughter of Porupparaiyan, became desirous, and the fire. The Sandhi Vetk Idaththar, the Emakkudaththar, the Padaththen Isaiyar Keethar, the Virichchangai Erik Kondu Ang Aadum Vedhar, worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

The Punkurar, the Purambayaththar, the Putturullar, the Poovanaththar, the Pulivalaththar, who, thinking of his great strength, tried to lift the mountain, whose heads and shoulders were lowered, and who, with a finger, pressed down the golden mountain-like ocean, and then graciously released it, the Vananathar with lightning-like matted locks, the rider of the bull, worshipped at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

Now, the seventh Thiru-Pathigam, the fifty-second Thiru-Pathigam of the sixth Thiru-Murai, the Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathigam, composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

Kannavan Kan Kan Kannozhiseyr Kaatchiyan Kan Kanthiruvum Paattisai. He is the one who shows the melody, He is the essence of those melodies, He is the fruit that ripens and yields taste. He is the king, He is the fire, He is the water. He is the one who comes to destroy, He is the one who resides in the sky with rain clouds, He is superior to the celestials, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one whose name is sweet like the juice of sugarcane, He is the one who resides in the minds of devotees of good conduct, He is the one who burned the three cities with His bow.

He is the one who bathed in milk, curd, and pure ghee, He is the hunter of the Pandaranga, He is the one who seeks alms, He is the one who swallowed the poison of the ocean, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one who is both gentle and fierce, He is the one who bestowed the discus upon Pushpaka, He is the one with the eye. He is the Kapali with three eyes, He is the one whose eye burned Kama’s body. He is the one who removed countless sins and enslaved me, He is the one who appeared as fire to the two. He is the one who is worshipped by the celestials, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one with the conch earring, He is the one whose form is like a golden mountain.

He is the one who tested the great penance of the goddess, He is the one adorned with the white tusk of a wild boar. He is the primordial one, He is beyond the universe, He is the one who made the five-headed serpent His ornament. He is the Vedic scholar, He is the one who showed the Vedic rituals, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one who bathed in ghee, milk, and tender coconut water, He is the one who stands as the eternal bridegroom. He is the one who holds the axe, the deer, and the spear in His hand. He is the one who kicked Yama to death.

He is the one whose sacred body is adorned with white ash, He is the one who placed the white moon on His red matted locks. He is the one who played with fierce fire, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one who, when the dark-eyed Vishnu sought the discus, plucked out His eye and offered it, and was graciously seen. He is the great Lord who holds the honey-laden Konrai, Vanni, and Datura flowers, and the celestial Ganga in His matted locks. He is the one who has the ancient-tongued goddess as His half, He is the Supreme Being, He is the one who became the Supreme Lord. He is the one who placed the white moon and the serpent on His red matted locks, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

He is the compassionate one who bestowed the discus upon the dark Vishnu, who tore apart the stone-like Salandhara. He is the one who tested the path of the victorious Arjuna, He is the hunter. He showed the battle. He is the Supreme Being, He is the Sadasiva, He is the one without equals. He is the beloved of the mountain king’s daughter, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the true ascetic, He is the one who is truthful to those who stand in true penance, He is the one who is always false to those with a mind full of desires.

He is the one who made the Buddha’s forgotten and burning ashes into fresh flowers. He is the one who saves, He is the one who makes those who contemplate on the highest path, and all the worlds, shine and be saved. He is the wise one, He is the one whom the wise desire and praise, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one who weakened the moon with His sacred foot, He is the one who, angered by Daksha, took his head. He is the one who broke Indra’s shoulders and then blessed him, He is the Lord. He is the beloved, He is the one who became all thoughts, mantras, and secret meanings.

He is the one who rose as a bright flame of white fire, whose top and bottom were unknown to Vishnu and Brahma. He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is the one who resides in the cremation ground, He is our Lord, He is the one who wore the skin of the wild elephant. He is the one who stood as one with the daughter of the great mountain king, He is the Omkara. He is the one adorned with the garland of Kongu flowers and Konrai, He is the one who hoisted the bull on His banner. He is the one whose upper garment is the skin of a striped tiger, He is the Lord of Vinnizhi Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

Now, the eighth Thiru-Pathigam, the fifty-third Thiru-Pathigam of the sixth Thiru-Murai, the Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathigam, composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar for Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

The one with the deer in His hand. He is like the giver of boons, He is like the one who bent the great mountain as a bow. He is like the one who flayed the elephant when it roared, He is like the one who holds the skull and drum. He is like the one adorned with the honey-laden Thiru-Idazhi, He is like the Lord residing in Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is like the beautiful one who rides the bull, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant.

He is like the one who, when the fierce Salandhara sought battle, tore him with the discus. He is like the Lord who once cut off Yama’s leg, He is like the one who embraced Narayana on His left side. He is like the one who has Kumaran as His son, He is like the beautiful one residing in cool Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. He is like the one who drank poison for the sake of the immortals, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant. He is like the pure one whose sacred body is adorned with water, He is like the one who blessed the great Vishnu with the discus. He is like our Lord with the beautiful banner, He is like the one whose arrow burned the three cities.

He is like the one who created the beautiful hunter. He is like the one who resides in the vast Thiru-Veezhimizhalai as the giver. He is like the beautiful one with the garlanded matted crown, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant. He is like the one who created the elephant-faced one, He is like the one who had Gayasura killed by him. He is like the one who once destroyed Daksha’s sacrifice, He is like the one who destroyed one of Brahma’s heads. He is like the one who cut off the head of the true sacrifice, He is like the one who made the vast Thiru-Veezhimizhalai His abode.

He is like the one who became the five sacrifices, He is the Lord who owns me, His servant. He is like the one who wears a loincloth, He is like the pure one who is the three lights and the flame. Thus, we have contemplated the eight Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Veezhimizhalai. We shall continue our contemplation.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 157 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 419, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We have seen the sacred deeds performed by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai.

There, we contemplated the eight Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.

Thus, these two great saints, after worshipping the Lord at Thiru-Veezhimizhalai and singing Thiru-Pathigams, developed a desire to visit other sacred places where the Lord resides. They worshipped Lord Shiva, the great jewel of Thiru-Veezhimizhalai, took leave from the Lord, and departed from there to continue their pilgrimage. These two great saints, having departed from Thiru-Veezhimizhalai, reached Thiru-Vanchiyam and worshipped the Lord there. And Lord Shiva. They visit and worship other sacred places where the Lord resides.

There, they compose Thiru-Pathigams as garlands of Tamil. The Peruman states that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman departed from Thiru-Vanchiyam, visited many sacred places, and reached Thiru-Maraikkadu, also known as Vedaranyam. They visited many sacred places in between and sang Thevaram Thiru-Pathigams.

Therefore, the many sacred places in between Thiru-Vanchiyam that these two great saints visited include Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu, Thiru-Peruvelur, Thiru-Chaththangudi, Thiru-Karaveeram, Thiru-Vilamar, Thiru-Arur, Thiru-Karayil, Thiru-Thevur, Thiru-Nellikka, Thiru-Kaichchinam, Thiru-Thengur, Thiru-Kollikkadu. Pottur, Thiru-Ven Thurai, and many other sacred places exist. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions in the Puranam of Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman that Thiru-Thandalai Nizhneri, Thiru-Kalaru, and other sacred places were also visited. Although many such places were visited, the Thiru-Pathigams sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for these places are not available to us due to our lack of merit. Among these, the Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Peruman for Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu and Thiru-Peruvelur are not available.

Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman, without elaborating on these places, generally states that they visited many places and composed garlands of Tamil, thus implicitly referring to these.

Therefore, let us briefly contemplate the Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu and Thiru-Peruvelur among these sacred places, and the special features of these places.

First, the sacred place Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu is the ninety-third sacred place on the south bank of the Kaveri. The history of this place is that Lord Shiva danced on Muyalagan, who was sent by the sage Tharuka. The Lord’s sacred name here is Nataneswarar, Adal Vallanathar. The Mother’s sacred name is Thirumadanthai Balambigai. The sacred tree is the Jackfruit tree and the Banyan tree. The sacred water is the Shankhu Theertham and the Kaduvai River.

In the Sangam period, this village was known as Thalaiyalanganam. This is the place where Lord Shiva subdued Muyalagan, who was sent by the Rishis of Tharukavanam, who, filled with arrogance, performed an Abhichara Yagna, and Lord Shiva danced on him. This is the place where he danced on him.

Therefore, the Lord is known by the sacred names Narthanapurishwarar and Adalvallanathar. In the Kritha Yuga, Sage Kapila came here, performed puja, and received the Chintamani on the Thai Amavasya day. This is the place where the Lord appeared as a Jyotirlingam to Goddess Saraswati and blessed her. It is still the unwavering belief of the people that by bathing in the tank in front of the temple and offering lamps to the Lord with determination, one can be cured of leprosy. Every year, during the last two days of the Panguni month and the first two days of the Chithirai month, at sunrise, when the sun’s rays fall on the Lord, a Surya Puja is performed. The Bhairava here is a very powerful deity who resolves intractable enmities and problems.

There are also inscriptions in this temple. On the occasion of Thai Amavasya. For two days, the Lord’s procession takes place, and the Theerthavari is performed in the Shankhu Theertham. One can reach the temple by going near Thalaiyalangadu on the Thiruvarur-Kumbakonam road. These are the special features of the sacred place Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu.

Here, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman came and composed a Thiru-Pathigam. This is a Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathigam. It is compiled as the seventy-ninth Thiru-Pathigam in the sixth Thiru-Murai.

Thondarkku Thooneriyay Ninran Thannai Soozhnarakil Vizhame Kappan Thannai Andaththukku Appalaikku Appalanai Athirai Nal Athariththa Amman Thannai Mundaththin Mulaiththozhundha Thiyayanai Muruvaththu Oruruvay Muthalay Ninra Thandaththil Thalaiyalangadan Thannai Sarathe Sala Nal Pokkinene Akkirantha. He is the one who is the Lord of the chamber, He is the one who burned the three cities of the Asuras in an instant. He is our dancer with the crown adorned with a cuckoo, He is the one with the earring in His ear, He is the pure one who entered the minds of those who waver and does not leave. He is the virtuous one, He is the one who is all the immeasurable joys, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu who remained. I have wasted many days without seeking Him.

He is the true ascetic, the Veda, the essence of the Veda, the one who wears the bright young moon, the giver. He is the one who gave me the axe, the poor one, He is the one who lifted me up from the ocean of suffering. He is the one who stands in the path unknown to false ascetics, He is the one who, with the water, stands as one half with Uma, He is the essence, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him. He is Shiva, He is Brahma, He is Vishnu, He is the bright light, He is fire, He is water. He is the wind, He is all the winds, He is the one who wanders as a cow, He is the one who stands as a wind. He is the ascetic, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him. He is the one who held the Ganga and the fierce water, He is the Lord of Kanchi, the one who broke Kama. He is the one who holds a deer in His hand, He is the Lord of Aiyaru, He is the Lord of Arur. He is the one who is compassionate to His faultless devotees, He is the Lord of Parithiniyamam, He is the Lord of Pasur.

He is Shankara, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him. He is the one who tied the poison on the serpent, He is the one whose measure is unknown even to the celestials. He is the one who makes those who seek Him rule the celestial world, He is the golden one, the one who fought the elephant. He is the one who placed the flowing water and the living serpent and the moon on the matted locks of the one with the goddess as half, He is the great ocean, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted.

I have wasted many days. He is the one who rides the bull and collects alms from every house, He is the Lord of Veerattam, He is the one with white ash. He is the one who dances in the foul-smelling cremation ground, He is the one who is before, He is the one who is after, He is the one who is that day. He is the one who delights in wearing the skin of an animal as His garment, He is the one who has Uma as His half. He is the one with matted locks, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him.

He is the sugarcane, the lump of sugar, the fruit, the honey, the calf, the middle pillar, the black one. He is the one who holds the three-pronged spear of iron, He is the one who is eight, He is the one who is ten, He is the one who protects. He is the one who wears the Konrai flowers where bees hum, He is the pure one, He is the mother, He is the one who gives all things to the world, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him. He is the sound of the ancient string, the fruit, the milk, the fruit of the milk, the fierce void, the fire, the wind. He is the one who is easy for those who rejoice at the sight, He is the cause, He is Narayana, He is the one on the lotus.

He is the one who, when contemplated. He is our Lord who resides in my heart, He is the one who cherishes the skin of the wild elephant, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him. He is the one who, when the twenty-armed Rakshasa king, without considering Kailash mountain, lifted it, and his pearl-like crowns shook and his bracelets struck, and he hastened, and He placed one sacred toe on him, and heard his song from his ten mouths, and out of compassion, bestowed upon him the name Ravana. He is the essence, He is the Lord of Thalaiyalangadu. I have wasted many days without seeking Him.

This is the Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman at Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu. Next to Thiru-Thalaiyalangadu, we have also received a Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman after visiting Thiru-Peruvelur. Thiru-Peruvelur is the ninety-second sacred place on the south bank of the Kaveri. It is currently known as Manakkal Aiyan. Pettai.

The Lord’s name is Piriyathanathar, Abhimuktheeswarar, Piriyayeeswarar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Abhinambigai, Yelavar Kuzhali. The sacred tree is the Vanni tree. The sacred water is Saravanappoigai. It is the ninety-second sacred place on the south bank of the Kaveri. In old texts, this place is referred to as Kattur Aiyampettai.

It is said that this place is called Velur because Murugan worshipped here, and Peruvelur because Peruvel, a great hunter, lived here. It is said that this is one of the Kailash peaks that fell during the competition between Vayu and Adisesha. This is the place where Vishnu, in the form of Mohini, after fulfilling the purpose of His avatar, worshipped the Lord here and regained His male form. This sacred place is a Madakoyil, built by Kochchengan Chozha Nayanar. The Moolavar (presiding deity) is a Swayambhu Murthi (self-manifested idol) with a square Avudaiyar (pedestal). One Thiru-pathikam (hymn) by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and one by Appar Swamigal are available for this Thiru-sthalam.

The Thiru-pathikam by Appar Swamigal is compiled as the sixty-sixth Thiru-pathikam in the Fourth Thiru-murai, a Thiru-nerisai Thiru-pathikam.

“Maranai nava nava marappilar manathullaanai Karaiyani kandanthannai kanalerri aadinanai Piraiyani sadaiyinanai Peruveloor peninanai Naraiyani malargal thoovi nalthorum vananguvene Nadhanai ulagamellam nambiran enavum nindra Padhanai paramayogi pala pala thiraththinallum Pedhanai thondrinanai Peruveloor peninanai Odha navudaiyanagi uraikkumaru uraikkindrene Kuravithol manandha selva
