We have extensively contemplated the connection between the Pandya kingdom and Tamil in the Puranam of Murthi Nayanar, in the sacred verses ranging from 68 to 974. Sekkizhar Peruman sang in the 974th verse, “If the Sangam that removes our sins and bestows the true meaning of the truthful Tamil texts existed in Thiru-Alavai, we can recall that message here.

“Thus, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the leader of wisdom, proceeds to the Tamil country, the Pandya kingdom, to fulfill his incarnational purpose of refuting alien religions and establishing Shaivism. While he goes there, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman remains at Thiru-Maraikkadu, worshipping the Lord and performing sacred service.

“Our contemplation continues.”””
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 163 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 425. Thiru-Nindra-Charukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. When Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, the king of Pukali, proceeded to the Pandya kingdom, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman stayed at Thiru-Maraikkadu for some time, performing sacred service. Appar Swamigal composed five Thiru-Pathikams for the sacred place of Thiru-Maraikkadu.

Among them, the Pathikam beginning “Pannin Ner Mozhiyal” was sung by Appar Swamigal to open the sacred doors. When he entered and worshipped the Lord after the doors opened, he sang the Thiru-Pathikam beginning “Odamal Kadal Pavi.” Now, the other three Thiru-Pathikams are those that we can consider to have been composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal. We will look at each of those Thiru-Pathikams one by one. The third Thiru-Pathikam is for Thiru-Marai- The third Thiru-Pathikam for Thiru-Maraikkadu is the thirty-third Thiru-Pathikam in the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Ner-Isai Thiru-Pathikam.

“Indiranodu Devar Irudigal Ethukindra Sundaramanaar Polum Thuthikkalan Sothi Polum Chandiranodum Gangai Aravaiyum Sadaiyul Vaithu Mandiramanar Polum Mamaraikkadanare Theyana Nadaragi Devarhal Devar Polum Payana Nadarukkum Paththargal Paniyammin Kayana Nadu Kandangu Adanular Kalakandar Mayana Nadar Polum Mamaraikkadanare Arumai Ivvulagu Thannai Yamenak Karuthi Nindru Verumaiyin Manaigal Vazhndu Vinaigalal Nazhivunathe Sirumathi Aravu Kondrai Thigazhdaru Sadaiyul Vaithu Marumaiyum Immaiyavar Mamaraikkadanare Kalkodu Thirugaiyetri Kalinirai Thiraichi Meyndu” Tholpaduthu Uthira Neeral Suvaredu Thiru Irandu Vasal Ezhvudai Thavamaitthang Ezhu Salokam Panni Malkoduthu Avi Vaithar Mamaraikkadanare Vinninar Vinnin Mikkar Vedangal Virumbiyodha Panninar Kinnarangal Paththargal Padiyada Kanninar Kanninulle Jothiyay Nindra Enthai Manninar Valamkondu Ethum Mamaraikkadanare Angaiyul Analum Vaithar Aruvagai Samayam Vaithar Thangaiyil Vinai Vaithar Tham Adi Parava Vaithar Thingalai Gangaiyodu Thigazhdaru Sadaiyul Vaithar Mangaiyai Bhagam Vaithar Mamaraikkadanare Geetharay Geetham Kettu Kinnaran Thannai Vaithar Vedaray Vedam Odhi Vilangiya Jothi Vaithar Etharay Nattamadi Ittamay Gangaiyodu Madhaiyor Bhagam Vaithar Mamaraikkadanare Kanathinar Valiudaiya Kadimathil Aranam Munrum Sinathinul Sinamay Nindru Theeyezha Setrarpolum Thanathinai Thavirndu Nindru Tham Adi Paravuvarkku Manathinul Masu Theerppar Mamaraikkadanare Thesanai Thesan Thannai Devarhal Potrisaippar Vasanaiseithu Nindru Vaigalum Vananguminhal Kasanai Kanalai Endrum Karuthinil Vaithavarkku Masinai Theerppar Polum Mamaraikkadanare Pinniudai Yakai Thannai Pirapparuthuyya Vendil Paniudai Thozhilgal Poondhu Paththargal Patrinale Thunivuudai Arakkanodi Eduthalum Thogai Anja Mani Mudi Paththiruthar Mamaraikkadanare Thiruchitrambalam. The fourth Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for the sacred place of Thiru-Maraikkadu. The thirty-fourth Thiru-Pathikam in the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Ner-Isai Thiru-Pathikam.

He drove his chariot high and looked with firm resolve, not knowing anyone above him, a man of great strength. He, whose matted hair spread out, making the earth and sky tremble, and whose beautiful form made people say, “Fear not!” is Thiru-Maraikkadanar. He, who, with a roar, lifted the mountain, the king of the rakshasas with matted hair, my Lord, who placed the moon on his head, adorned with the beauty of a serpent, by his will, the waves of the southern sea crash upon Thiru-Maraikkadanar. He drove a chariot of immense profit, and the rakshasa, mighty in strength, lifted the mountain, but when he pressed it down, he laughed and said, “I am Thiru-Maraikkadu.” He drove his chariot into the sky and, saying, “Who is this?” pushed the great mountain. When he pressed it down, the rakshasa, with his ten heads and mouths, cried out in agony, and he thought.

Thiru-Maraikkadanar. He, who, with irresistible strength, drove a chariot and, with what he held in his hands, said, “I will take whatever I want!” and lifted it, is capable of making him groan. He is Thiru-Maraikkadu, the beautiful one. He, who, with his glorious matted hair, trembled and did not go up, the one with the hand that seized and roared, the cruel and mighty one, tried to lift the mountain where the long-haired ascetics reside. He placed his toenail firmly on it. He is Thiru-Maraikkadanar, the ancient one.

He, who had ten mouths and twenty hands, the mighty one, the rakshasa of great strength, who committed evil with his mouth, when he cried out, he pressed his toenail on him. He is Thiru-Maraikkadanar, the ancient one, where the pearl-like waves crash. He, who, with his hands, left his side, and with an unwise mind, entered beneath the great mountain, unable to change his ways. His great wisdom was lost, and his valor was gone. The bhutas were naked. Thiru-Maraikkadanar.

He, who, with five hands and ten good heads, lost his wisdom, not knowing the long five, and lifted it, then made seven hands. He is Thiru-Maraikkadanar, the beautiful one. When he saw that he had placed the Ganga water in his matted hair, the maiden became angry. He drove his chariot with his hand and went and lifted the mountain. He cut the great nerve of his hand and sang songs. He, who granted grace with his hand, is Thiru-Maraikkadu, the beautiful one.

This Thiru-Pathikam is a special Thiru-Pathikam. Generally, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, in all his Thiru-Pathikams, in the tenth verse, sings about Ravana’s attempt to lift Mount Kailash, and how Lord Shiva punished Ravana, subdued his arrogance, and then, when he sang, granted him grace. This is a custom that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman follows in his Thiru-Pathikams, singing about that sacred history in the tenth verse of each Thiru-Pathikam.

Here, in this Thiru-Pathikam, in all ten verses, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar has sung about Ravana’s actions and the nature of Lord Shiva who granted him grace. This is the greatness of this Pathikam.

Now, the fifth Thiru-Pathikam, the twenty-third Thiru-Pathikam of the sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathikam, composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Maraikkadu.

He is the light that kindles the unextinguished flame, he is the jewel that surrounds the ancient immortals, he is the God difficult to behold, he is easy for those who contemplate him, he grants whatever those who desire him wish, he is the true path, he is the husband of those with purified minds, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. Hand. He is the one who plays the resounding Veena, he is Kapali, he is the lamp of knowledge that shines with true light, he is the seed in the hearts of true devotees, he is the one who wears the shedding serpent, he is the Supreme Being, he is the one of Thiru-Pasur, he is the one with the sharp, shining sword, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the one who formerly granted grace to the spider, he is the one who set fire to the three cities, he is the one who became earth, water, and fire, he is the one who stands as both formless and with form, he is the one with the matted hair on his head where the water flows, he is the one who is Brahma and the red-eyed Vishnu, he is the one who rides a great bull, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the one who danced in the cremation ground with thorny bushes, he is the one who conquered Yama with his foot, he is the one with the spotted deer skin, he is the one whose garment is the tiger skin, the pure one.

He is the one who wears the shining crescent moon on his head, he is the one with sacred ash, he is the father of the bridegroom of Valli, who resides in our Thiru-Sentil, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the one who became the roaring, surging water, he is the primordial one whose body is like a complete fire, he is the wealthy one who ascended and filled, he is the one who brings joy to his sweet devotees, he is the Aryan, he is the Tamilian, he is the Lord who resides in Thiru-Annamalai, he is like the rutting elephant, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the one who flayed the mighty elephant, he is the one who resides in Thiru-Agathiyanpalli, he is the one of Thiru-Kodi, he is the one of noble lineage, he is the one who made Thiru-Arur his temple, he is the desired good things, he is the one who removes the weariness of this world and the next, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the one with the poison in his throat that joins the sea, he is the Lord of the flowery Kailash mountain that touches the sky, he is the one who destroyed the sacrifices that were performed, he is the Lord whom the immortals praise, he is the one who bathed in the five products of the cow mixed with milk and ghee, he is the one of the mountain, he is the son who has a part of Vishnu, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the nectar that brings forth the mother, he is the clear honey, he is the Lord who brings forth this world, he is the one sweeter than you in my heart, he is the lamp of true knowledge, he is the one of Thiru-Venkaadu, he is the medicine for those whose minds are confused so that their karmas may depart, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the primordial one who cures the root disease, he is the one who is the three Tamils and the four Vedas, he is the one who taught dharma to the four under the tree.

He is the beginning and the end, he is the eternal youth, he is like a coral mountain, he is adorned with the Konrai flowers, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu. He is the Lord who stood as a pillar of fire, so that Brahma and Vishnu could not know him, he is the one who, with his radiant toe, pressed down the king of sorrowful Lanka, he is the one who granted great grace to those who praised him, he is the one who gave names and great armies, he is the one who cures the disease of powerful karma, he is the bridegroom who resides in Thiru-Maraikkadu.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman thus stayed in Thiru-Maraikkadu for some time and sang Thiru-Pathikams.

Now, he again wishes to go to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai and worship the Lord’s feet. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman wishes to do so because, until now, he had been on a pilgrimage with Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for a long time, and that pilgrimage extended up to Thiru-Maraikkadu. From Thiru-Maraikkadu, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman had departed for the Pandya country. Currently, only Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman remains in Thiru-Maraikkadu.

Therefore, the memory of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, where he had stayed with Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for a long time, comes to Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman. Previously, Thiru-Vizhimizhalai was the sacred place where he had stayed with Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman for a long time and received grace.

Therefore, immediately after parting from Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, he thinks of going to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai to worship.

Thus, having received the grace of Lord Shiva, who resides as a light in Thiru-Maraikkadu with love, he departs from Thiru-Maraikkadu for Thiru-Vizhimizhalai with the thought, “When will I reach Thiru-Vizhimizhalai?” On the way, he visits Thiru-Nagaikkaronam and other sacred places, sings Thiru-Pathikams, and reaches Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Sekkizhar Swamigal composes this verse, saying, “Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having received the grace of the light that resides in the groves of Thiru-Maraikkadu, departed and, thinking, ‘I will return to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, where the Lord who consumed the poison of the sea resides,’ worshipped Thiru-Nagaikkaronam and other places that exist in the world, and singing powerful Tamil songs, reached Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, the abode of the Lord.” Therefore, on his way to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, he visited Thiru-Nagaikkaronam and other sacred places. He sings Thiru-Pathikams as he goes. The other sacred places that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman visited after departing from Thiru-Maraikkadu are Thiru-Nellikka, Thiru-Nattiyathankudi, Thiru-Arur, Nannilam, and other sacred places.

However, the Thiru-Pathikams sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for these other places are not available to us now. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worshipped the Lord in Thiru-Nagaikkaronam.

At that time, we have four Thiru-Pathikams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for the sacred place of Thiru-Nagaikkaronam. Let us go on contemplating.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 164 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 426, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman reaches the sacred place of Thiru-Nagaikkaronam. This place, referred to as Thiru-Nagaikkaronam in the Thiru-Murais, is currently known as Nagapattinam. The Lord’s name here is Kayarohanesvarar, Adhipuranar. The Goddess’s name is Nilayatakshi, Karuntadankanni.

The Sthala Vriksham is the mango tree. The Theertham is Devatheertham, Pundarika Theertham. Adiseshan, Pundarika Munivar, Agathiyar, Ambigai, Murugan, Thirumal, Vasishtar, Musukundan, Arasakesari, Vichitra Kavachan, Viruragan, Pathirasenan, Bhaskaran, Mithiran, Kalakandan, Chandadharuman, etc., worshipped in this place and received the grace of the Lord. Nagapattinam. We can learn from literature and inscriptions that Nagapattinam was one of the most important ports in the Chola country. The Pattu-Pattu, one of the Sangam literatures, states that Ilanthiraiyan, who ruled Thondai Nadu, was the son of a Chola king from Nagapattinam who went to Nagalokam through a tunnel and united with a Naga maiden.

This is a place worshipped by Adiseshan, one of the eight Nagas, and hence it is called Nagai. Karonam is the name of the temple. There are three temples named Karonam in Tamil Nadu. One is Nagaikkaronam, another is Kulandaikkaronam, and the third is Kachchikkaronam. Kayarohanam itself is called Karonam. Thiru-Nagaikkaronam is the place where the Lord accepted Pundarika Munivar into his sacred body.

Pundarika. This is the place where the Lord accepted the sage Pundarika into his sacred body, along with his physical body.

Therefore, it is called Kayarohana Sthalam. Thiru M. Balasubramanian Mudaliar states that this name was given because the Lord made Pundarika Munivar ascend to the celestial world with his physical body. Thiru-Onam is the star associated with Thirumal. Thiru Muthu Manickavasagam Mudaliar, in the Tharumaiyatheena Thiru-Murai publication, states that it received the name Karonam because Thirumal, who is dark-skinned, worshipped here. Thiru-Nagaikkaronam also has other names such as Adhipuranam, Sivarajadhani, Parpatheeswaram, and Aravanagaram.

This place has received the Thevara Thiru-Pathikams of the three, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. It is the eighty-second sacred place among the sacred places on the south bank of the Kaveri in the Chola country. Adiseshan, the king of serpents, worshipped here and established his name. It is one of the Sapthavidanga Sthalams. This is also one of the sacred places where the Goddess is named after her sacred eyes, meaning that just as Madurai Meenakshi, Kanchi Kamakshi, and Kasi Visalakshi are named after the Goddess’s eyes, the Goddess of this place is known as Nagai Nilayatakshi. Like Kailash and Kasi, this place also has a Mukthi Mandapam.

It has the glory of being the birthplace of Adhipattha Nayanar.

The Lord appeared from the Moolalingam to the seven sages and gave darshan as Somaskandar. He showed the wedding form to Agasthya Munivar. To King Salisuka, the wedding temple. The Panchakrosa Yatra, which shows the wedding, and the Sapthasthana festival take place. Dasaratha worshipped here by installing Shani. The temple is located in the middle of the town, facing east.

There are two prakarams. At the entrance, there is a small gopuram adorned with stucco sculptures of the Panchamurthis. After passing through that entrance, one first sees Nagaabharana Pillaiyar in a separate shrine.

Next, there is a large Nandi made of stucco. To the north, there is a pandal darshan mandapam and a cow mandapam, and to the south, there is a mukthi mandapam and Devatheertham. After passing through the front entrance of the temple, there is a Chola gopuram with five tiers. After passing through that entrance, in the second prakaram, there is a Rajadhani mandapam in the middle. To the east, there are shrines for Vinayagar, Pazhaniyandavar, Idumban, and the temple of Adhipathar. To the south, there is a Mani Mandapam, a Nandavanam, a well, and to the west, there are temples for Vallamai Ganapathi, Kali, a mango tree, and Veerabhadra.

To the north, there are the shrine of Athmanathar, the Vasantha Mandapam, and the Yagasalai. Adjacent to the Rajadhani Mandapam are the flagstaffs for the Lord and the Goddess, and to the north, facing south, is the Goddess’s temple.

Next, there is a second gopuram entrance with three tiers. In that entrance, there are Sengazhineer Vinayagar and Arumugapperuman. We circumambulate the first prakaram after worshipping Adhikaranandi and Vinayagar. To the south of the entrance are Surya and Chandra, and to the south, in the Thiru-Maligai Pathi, are the sixty-three Nayanmars and the Samayacharyars. To the west, the deities such as Mavadi Pillaiyar, Karmukeesar, Murugapperuman, and Gajalakshmi shine. To the north, there are Shani Bhagavan, installed by Dasaratha, and the Navagrahas.

Next, there is the Natarajar Mandapam. To the east, there are Bhairavar and Chandra. In front of the Sangu Mandapam, on the pillars, there are bas-reliefs of Pundarika Munivar and King Salisuka. In the Sangu Mandapam, Lord Natarajar gave darshan. Bhikshatanar and Adhipathar’s Utsava Vigrahas are present. In the niches surrounding the Moolavar’s Vimanam, to the south is Dakshinamurthy, to the west is Lingodbhavar, and to the north are Brahma, Ardhanareeswarar, Durga, and Bhikshatanar.

The temple is divided into two parts: to the south, the Thyagesar shrine, and to the north, the Kayarohanar shrine, both facing east. Adjacent to the Sangu Mandapam is the Maha Mandapam, and next to it is the Ardha Mandapam. At the entrance of the sanctum sanctorum, the Dvarapalakas shine with Chola artistic style. Kayarohana Peruman, in the form of a Shiva Lingam, captivates our hearts as a wonderful deity. Behind, in a separate niche, Peruman appears as Somaskandar, in a form that grants grace to devotees as both male and female. In the Maha Mandapam, after worshipping Panchamukha Vinayagar, Villendhiya Murugan, Pundarika Munivar, and the processional deities, we reach the Goddess’s shrine.

The Goddess’s temple shines with unique splendor. Mother Nilayatakshi shines as a creeper whose beauty is unmatched by anyone. Nearby, there is a shrine for Adipooramman. Around this sacred place, there are other sacred Shiva temples that have been sung about, such as Sikkal, Keezhvelur, Devur, Ettukudi, Thirumarugal, and Thirusaththamangai.

Here, the Vidangar in the Thyagaraja Peruman shrine is named Sundara Vidangar. The dance of Thyagaraja here is the Tharanga Natanam.

Now, the Theerthams: the Pundarika Theertham to the west of the temple, the Deva Theertham near the Mukthi Mandapam, the Uppanaru, also called Devanadi, flowing to the west of the town, and the sea. The sea is considered the most important Theertham of this place. On the days of Adi and Thai Amavasai, and Masi Magam, and Adhipathar festival, the Lord grants Theertham in the sea. Six daily pujas are performed in this place every day. Vaikasi. The Brahmotsavam takes place.

In the month of Ani, on Krishna Ashtami, the Sapthasthana festival takes place.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal came to Thiru-Nagaikkaronam, worshipped, and sang a Pathikam, praying to the Lord to grant him all the wealth, such as pearl necklaces, diamond necklaces, musk paste, gold ingots, and horses, which are royal possessions, so that he could live a great life with two wives and worship alongside the three kings. He received all of them. The Nagaikkaronam Puranam, composed by Mahavidvan Meenakshi Sundaram Pillai, exists for this place. There is also a Sthala Varalaru written by Panchanatham Pillai. There are individual songs about Nagai sung by Kalamegha Pulavar. There are Nanmani Malai written by Karunthittaigudi Saminatha Pillai and Meykandavelar Thiruppugal sung by Azhagumuthu Pillai.

Arunagirinathar’s Thiruppugal are dedicated to Lord Muruga of this place. Nagai is also one of the Saptha Vidanga Sthalams. We know that King Muchukunda received seven Thyagesar idols and Vidanga Shiva Linga Murtis from Indra and installed and worshipped them in seven places, including Thiruvarur. Among them, Thiruvarur is the foremost and most glorious. Thiru-Nagai is one of these seven Vidanga Sthalams. The Thyagaraja Peruman here is called Sundara Vidangar, and his dance is called Paravara Tharanga Natanam.

The Vidangar of this place is made of honey-colored Gomedakam. The Thyagesar dance is also called Sukshma Panchakshara Natanam and Uravu Poli Natanam. In the Adhipattha Nayanar Puranam, Sekkizhar Peruman has sung about the glory of this city and the greatness of Adhipathar. The festival where the Lord granted grace to Adhipathar takes place annually in the month of Avani. Adiseshan, distressed by not having children, came here as advised by Vasishta Munivar and worshipped the Lord in Kudanthai in the morning, in Nageswaram at noon, in Pambaram in the evening, and in Nagai at midnight. By the grace of the Lord, a female child was born.

He was saddened to know that she had three breasts. The Lord, as an ethereal voice, blessed him, saying, “One breast will disappear when she sees her husband.” The daughter grew up and reached puberty.

King Salisuka, born in the Chola dynasty, saw her. One of the Naga maiden’s breasts disappeared. As blessed by the Lord, Salisuka married the Naga maiden. Adiseshan also worshipped the Lord with gratitude and received the boon that this town should be known by his name.

Thus, this city came to be known as Nagai. Pundarika Munivar, born as the greatly ascetic son of Karuthamar Munivar in Vedapuram on the banks of the Yamuna, and Vamadevar. As per the words of Kanvar and others, he came to Nagaikkaronam and worshipped the Lord and the Goddess, and performed penance to attain the Lord with this body and be blissful.

Lord Shiva appeared to him and, taking the sage with his body, ascended him to Thiru-Kailash. During the time of deluge, twelve suns united and caused heat in the world. The world was disturbed, and living beings suffered. Thirumal, Brahma, and the seven sages, Markandeyar, Gautamar, Vasishtar, Kashyapar, Pulastiyar, Agasthiyar, and Angirasar, came to this place and worshipped the Lord.

The Lord appeared from the Moolalingam and protected Brahma at the base of the Lingam, Thirumal in the middle, and the sages at the top.

After the deluge, everyone came out and lived by performing their respective duties. Since all the gods resided here, this city is called Sivarajadhani, and because it is very ancient, it is called. Adhipuranam.

The Lord is called Adhipuranar. Dasaratha, the king of Ayodhya, learned from astrologers that the world would suffer from lack of rain if Shani entered the Rohini star. As per the sun’s advice, he worshipped the Lord of this place, installed Shani, and saved the living beings of the world. There are many inscriptions in this place. These are the Sthala Viseshams and Puranic stories about Thiru-Nagaikkaronam. We saw that Appar Swamigal came here on his way from Thiru-Maraikkadu to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, worshipped the Lord of this place, and sang Thiru-Pathikams.

There are four Thiru-Pathikams composed by Appar Swamigal for this place. The first of them is the seventy-first Thiru-Pathikam of the fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nerishai Thiru-Pathikam.

Wife, mother, father, children. kaḷ maṟṟuḷḷa cuṟṟameṉṉum viyuḷē viḻuntaḻunti vētaṉaikku iṭamākātē kaṉaiyumā kaṭalcūḻ nākai maṇṇu kāṟōṇattaṉai niṉaiyumāvalliṟākil uyyalām neñciṉīrē vaiyaṉai vaiyammuṇṭa māl aṅkaṅtōṉ mēṟkoṇṭa ceyyaṉai ceyya pōtir ticaimukaṉ ciramoṉṟu ēntum kaiyaṉai kaṭalcūḻ nākaikkāṟōṇam kōyil koṇṭa aiyyaṉai niṉainta neñcē ammaṉām uyntavārē niṟuttaṉai nimalantaṉṉai nīḻnilam veṇṇiṉmikka viruttaṉai vētatvittai viḷai poruḷ mūlamāṉa karuttaṉai kaṭalcūḻ nākaikkāṟōṇam kōyil koṇṭa oruttaṉai uṇartalāl nām uyntavā neñciṉīrē maṇṭaṉai iṟantu koṇṭa māyaṉōṭacurarvāṉōr teṇṭirai kaṭaiya vanta tīviṭam taṉṉai uṇṭa kaṇṭaṉai kaṭalcūḷ nākaikkāṟōṇam kōyil koṇṭa aṇṭaṉai niṉainta neñcē We are saved, O mind! He whose head is adorned with abundant waters, who wears the crescent moon and the serpent, who delights in the cremation ground with the sound of the Vedas, the Lord enshrined in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, if we praise Him daily, our suffering will turn into joy. He who wears the skin of a fierce, dark-trunked elephant, who burnt Kāma, who is praised by the world, the Lord of the celestials, the golden one enshrined in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, if we remember Him, we are surely saved. He who went as a hunter with the poor woman in the fierce forest, and bestowed the sharp arrow upon Pārtha after a battle, the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, where maidens’ dances never cease, we have been blessed to see Him day and night. He who, with one arrow, burnt the three cities of the deceitful ones, those who do not enter the minds of the wicked, the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, where the learned reside and praise Him, Those who have attained Him are born, and those who are born have not yet attained Him.

The ninth verse of this decad is not available to us.

Now, the tenth verse: The Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, whose lotus feet, when pressed by one toe, did not allow the demon Rāvaṇa to stand, with His two consorts, our Lord, the red-bodied serpent, stood with His sacred feet. Surely, we are saved.

Let us press on in meditation.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 165 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Purāṇam, Part 427. Thiru-Nīṇṭa-Chāṟu-Kam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Purāṇam. We are meditating on the Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam. The second Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is the 103rd Thiru-Pathigam in the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Viruttam Thiru-Pathigam.

O Lord, who shares a form with the great mountain maiden, whose matted locks hold the Ganges, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by fragrant groves and the sea! What is this, that you ride a great white bull with a thunderous roar, while an elephant and a horse stand by? O Lord, whose eye is on the forehead, in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, where the learned reside! Your hand that held the bow, the hand of the long-eyed maiden, my good hand that wielded the great bow, your hand that destroyed the cities of your enemies, Tell me, what is it? O our Shankara, who burnt Kāma to ashes, who strung the soft flower-arrows and performed the fire sacrifice, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea, you bestow the five-letter mantra, “Namashivaya,” to those who praise your name.

You saved me from ending my life by following the path of the wicked, the bald-headed ascetics who follow the path of sin. O our Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea where the waves recede, grant that my lineage may be blessed. O Lord, whose dark eyes, red lips, and white teeth are praised by honey-tongued maidens who circumambulate and dance, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by fragrant groves and the sea, those who meditate on Him will not be separated from the divine prosperity. O Lord, the supreme light, who flayed the elephant with a trunk like a palm tree, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai, surrounded by the roaring sea, O Lord with an eye on your forehead, in Thiru-Kāṟōṇam! You removed my delusion from the ascetics and the bald-headed ones who abandoned their homes and ate no food. What more can I desire now?

O Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea and groves, rich in wealth and golden mountains! Is it not a wonder that you go begging for alms from maidens with full, soft breasts, and eat the alms you receive in the town? O our Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, where ships abound in the sea! We have a request for you, our Lord. You held the Ganges in your matted locks, and you gently hid the deceit from Umā, the maiden. You are not evil, our Lord.

The ninth verse of this decad is missing.

Now, the tenth verse: The Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, with the dark-eyed maiden, resided on the sacred mountain. He tried to lift it, but He did not do anything else, but only caused the ten heads and twenty arms to be crushed.

The third Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, the eighty-third Thiru-Pathigam in the Fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kuṟunthogai Thiru-Pathigam.

Our karma will cease when we know Him who burnt the three cities with a bow, who wears the serpent as an ornament, who is pleasant to see, the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea. When we see the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, whose matted locks are adorned with buzzing bees, whom the celestials worship and praise, our karma will vanish. When we meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the roaring sea, who wears fresh, fragrant flowers on His matted locks, all our karma will disappear.

The Lord who rides the great bull, who dances at night, When we speak of the Lord who dances, the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by stone walls, our karma will vanish. There is no suffering for those who worship the true one, who rides the bull, who holds the white axe, the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, whose throat is dark, the Lord of the celestials. Those who circumambulate the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the turbulent sea, who is the ancient one with flowing matted locks, who desires the soft maiden as a part of Himself, their karma will disappear. Those who embrace the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by great walls, who is the fierce elephant, the excellent bull, the Lord praised by the celestials, their karma will disappear. The sorrows of those who meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by fragrant groves, who is praised by maidens of endless fame as ‘Our Lord,’ will surely cease.

The Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea, the Lord whom the two could not comprehend, those who do not understand the one, When we worship the warrior who shot the three cities, evil karma will be removed.

The Lord of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea, whose foot pressed down on the demon who tried to lift the northern mountain, the fear of suffering will not approach.

Now, the fourth Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, the twenty-second Thiru-Pathigam in the Sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thāṇṭakam Thiru-Pathigam.

He who is in Pazhanam, praised by the world, who is the mountain, who is the green parrot, who is the beautiful coral mountain, who wears the moon on His glorious crown, the Lord with a thousand names, who cannot be seen by others, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by dark seas.

The Lord of the celestials, the hero, whose body is adorned with white ash, the female, He who is the male, who is the hermaphrodite, who resides in Thiru-Puli-Yūr, who is in Thiru-Aṇṇāmalai, who dances with the bull, the Lord who resides in Thiru-Ārūr, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea.

The Lord of Thiru-Maṟaikkāṭu, Shiva-Lōkaṉ, where the bees sing, He who resides in Thiru-Vāymūr, Kīḻ-Vēḷūr, Vali-Valam, and Thiru-Vūr, the supreme one who resides in Thiru-Oṭṭiyūr, the supreme one who is attached to it, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea. He who is the swan in the pond, who is in Thiru-Āchchirāmam, who made Thiru-Āṉaikkā His temple long ago, who is the form that became the three worlds, who wears small, many flowers and the white moon on His red matted locks, He who is in Thiru-Puṉṉai, surrounded by the virgin, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the sea. He who rides a good bull, who is the great ocean of wisdom, who resides in Thiru-Nallūr, who holds the axe, who speaks only of goodness, the Lord with the blue throat, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, where the plantains grow in the ponds, He can always be seen. He who is the Lord of Thiru-Pukazhi, where the bees hum, who is the Kalpaka tree of Thiru-Pūmpukār, who resides in Thiru-Puṉkūr, who desired the Ganges on His matted locks, who wears a garland of skulls and a serpent as a belt, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the turbulent sea. He who wears a garland of golden flowers and Konrai, who is the virtuous one, who smears white ash, who holds the trident, He who is in Thiru-Chirāppaḷḷi, Shiva-Lōkaṉ, who is the gem of the earth, who rides the bull, who is skilled in the Vedas, who resides in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by white waves, He can always be seen. He who holds the white skull and the white axe, who smears white ash, who flayed the fierce elephant, who is the golden one, who wears white ash, who can dance with fire in the eight directions, who resides in Thiru-Ēkampam, our Lord, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by fertile fields.

He who is in Thiru-Chōṟṟuttuṟai, who removes ancient hell through the good path, who is the archer, who resides in Thiru-Mīyachchūr, who taught the Vedas to the four Vedic scholars, who wears the serpent on His chest, who is under the Banyan tree, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by joy. O mind, do not consider as truth the lies of the ascetics who abandoned their homes, the lies of the bald-headed ones who speak of greatness, and the lies of those who wear the saffron robe. Only by clinging to the Lord who wears the elephant skin on His body can one see Him in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by the southern sea. He can always be seen. The tall one and the lotus-born one searched, but could not find His true form. He who is the serpent, who loves the serpent, who dances with the serpent, who went begging for alms with a skull, who resides in Thiru-Nīṇṭiyūr, He can always be seen in Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, surrounded by fragrant groves.

Thus, we have meditated on the four Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal for the Thiru-Sthalam of Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped Thiru-Nāgai Kāṟōṇam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having visited many shrines on his way, reaches Thiru-Vizhimizhalai. Let us go on meditating.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 166 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Purāṇam, Part 428. Thiru-Nīṇṭa-Chāṟu-Kam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Purāṇam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having returned to Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, worships the Lord of Thiru-Vizhimizhalai, performs sacred service, and sings Thiru-Pathigams.

During this time, the Nayanar’s desire to worship other shrines grew.

Therefore, he set out from Thiru-Vizhimizhalai and traveled along the banks of the Cauvery to worship the shrines. He went to worship the Thiru-Sthalams located on both banks of the Cauvery.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having set out, arrives at Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. This is the shrine where the Lord, having accepted the worship performed by the Mother in the form of a cow, bestowed His grace upon her. Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai is the place where Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman, at the request of his father, Sivapāda Hṛdayar, for performing yagnas, prayed to the Lord, who then bestowed upon him a never-ending purse containing a thousand gold coins. We will discuss this in detail in the Purāṇam of Thiru-Gnanasambandhar Peruman. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having come to this glorious Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai, worships the Lord there and sings a Thiru-Pathigam. The Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai begins with “Māyiru Gnālamellām.” There are a total of five Thiru-Pathigams composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai.

We have already seen that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman had visited Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai during his pilgrimage and had composed four Thiru-Pathigams then.

Now, this Thiru-Pathigam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar is the fifth Thiru-Pathigam composed for Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. This Thiru-Pathigam is compiled as the fifty-sixth Thiru-Pathigam in the Fourth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Nērisai Thiru-Pathigam.

The entire great world worships His lotus feet, it seems. He keeps the great Ganges in His matted locks, it seems. He bestows a thousand gold coins to the people of Kaḻumalam, surrounded by dense groves, it seems. He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. He is a part of the maiden, it seems.

He holds the deer in His hand, it seems. He is the Lord of Kuṭantai, it seems. He wears the tiger skin, it seems. He drank the poison that was churned, it seems. He burnt Kālan, it seems. He is loving to those who approach Him, it seems.

He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. He cures diseases, it seems. He is the only support, it seems. He fought and burnt the three cities of His enemies, it seems. He is loving to those who are learned, who praise Him, who mingle with Him, who measure Him, and who sing. He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai.

He holds the axe in His hand, it seems. He is a part of the great maiden, He is the Lord who holds the sharp spear, it seems. He is adorned with bones, it seems. He is loving to those who worship, weep, dance, sing, and utter many praises. He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. He is adorned with ash on His body, it seems.

He wears the sacred white thread, it seems. He rides a fierce bull, it seems. He burnt Kāma, it seems. He holds a skull, it seems. He measures the devotion of His devotees who praise Him with desire, it seems. He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai.

He bestowed the discus to Vishnu, who worshipped Him with His eye, it seems. He is the Lord of the demons, it seems. He casts the ignorant into sorrow, it seems. He is the Lord of the river bank, it seems. He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. He has the bull as His banner, it seems.

He wears the white sacred thread, it seems. He holds the axe, it seems. He wears the leaping tiger skin, it seems. He wears the elephant skin, it seems. He is the world, it seems. He removes the sufferings of those who approach Him.

He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. The ancient celestials came and worshipped Him in due order. Nandi and Mahākāla stood in the middle. He burnt the three cities of those who did not think, He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai, who wears the crescent moon on His evening sky. He who became a boar and dug the earth, Vishnu, and the lotus-born Brahma, who rides the swan, the Lord who has the sacred form to burn the wicked, He who rides the bull, He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai. He bestows grace upon Arjuna, it seems.

He has matted locks, it seems. He bestows joys to those who praise Him and removes their sufferings, it seems. He who dances and sings, who made the fierce demon cry out, He is the Lord of Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai.

Thus, having worshipped Thiru-Āvaṭutuṟai, he visits Thiru-Iṭaimarutūr, Thiru-Nāgēsuram, Thiru-Kuṭantai, Thiru-Valañchuḻi, and other shrines.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman arrives at the shrine called Thiru-Paḻaiyāṟai. He arrives at the Thiru-Kōyil of Paḻaiyāṟai Vaṭataḻi. There is a Shiva temple in Paḻaiyāṟai Vaṭataḻi. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worships that temple with folded hands.

However, the Jains had hidden that temple and converted it into their Pāḻi (Jain temple).

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman stood firm, declaring that he would see the Lord’s form, remove the Jain Pāḻi, and worship the Lord’s temple when it became visible, and only then would he proceed further. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman made a request at the sacred feet of the Lord, saying, “Destroy this power of the Jains and reveal yourselves so that we may see you.” He sat down near the temple that the Jains had converted into their Pāḻi, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman observes a fast without partaking of any food. As Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman was fasting, Lord Shiva appeared in the dream of the king of that country and revealed that the Jains had hidden the temple. He also revealed the signs of the hidden Shiva temple and the signs of His presence to the king in his dream.

Therefore, Lord Shiva instructed the king in his dream to remove the encroachment of the Jains and enable Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to worship Lord Shiva. The king, understanding this, followed the signs revealed by Lord Shiva in his dream, removed the Jain Pāḻi, discovered the temple, purified it, and consecrated it. He then bowed at the sacred feet of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and informed him. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman went there, worshipped, and sang the Thiru-Pathigam, “Can it be hidden even if the Jains hide it?” and worshipped the Lord. This act of grace is to take place here at the sacred shrine of Paḻaiyāṟai Vaṭataḻi. The sacred shrine of Paḻaiyāṟai Vaṭataḻi is a unique shrine.

Paḻaiyāṟai is to its south-southwest. Paḻaiyāṟai Mēṟṟaḻi is another shrine to the northwest of Paḻaiyāṟai. We have meditated on this history in the Purāṇam of Amar-Nīti Nayanar.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having come to Paḻaiyāṟai Vaṭataḻi, worships the Vimana, the gross form of the Shiva temple, as Lord Shiva Himself, with folded hands.

At that time, the devotees present there said that the Jains had encroached upon the Lord’s temple and They say that they have converted it into their Jain Pāḻis.

Therefore, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, from a distance, worshipped Lord Shiva and the Shiva temple. Since it was encroached upon by the Jains, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman worshipped the Lord from outside without entering.

Thus, he made a request at the sacred feet of Lord Shiva to destroy the power of these Jains who had encroached upon the temple.

Here, we must note that Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman requested to eliminate the deception of the Jains, not to eliminate or destroy the Jains themselves. Shaivism, as it is said, “Shaivism is a religion that encompasses all religions,” accepts and accommodates all other religions in a hierarchical order. It is an inner religion, an outer-inner religion, and an outer religion. Shaivism is a religion that embraces all other religions as progressive steps, and therefore, Shaivism does not spontaneously engage in conflict with any religion to destroy it. That is why Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman here states that the deception of the Jains should be destroyed, but he does not appeal to Shiva Peruman to destroy the Jains.

However, here, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman and the Buddhists in Thiru-Alavai, Madurai, caused harm and suffering, attempting to corrupt the Vedic path. To prevent this, Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman performed these sacred deeds. The Jains Here, they had concealed the Thiru-Koyil (temple), the Shiva-Alayam, and transformed it into a Jain school. Nevertheless, the Lord remained within, consenting to this. Not only that, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar was able to perceive and worship the Lord within with his mind’s eye. Even though he worshipped in this manner, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman appealed to the Lord, stating that the deception of these Jains, who had concealed the temple, must be eradicated.

This is because the people of the world would not know that the Lord was within and that the Jains had occupied it.

Therefore, for the Shaiva path to flourish undiminished in the world, and for him to be able to worship the Lord whom he had worshipped with his mind’s eye, with his physical eyes—for these two reasons, he desired that the Thiru-Koyil should be revealed, and the Lord within the Thiru-Koyil should be revealed. He prayed to the Lord, saying, “I will leave this place only after I have seen and worshipped You. I will not leave this place without seeing and worshipping You directly. I will proceed to the next Thalam only if I behold Your sacred form with my eyes. Otherwise, I will not depart from here.” Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having made this firm resolve to the Lord, achieved his desired outcome. He remained without food, fasting there.

It is a long-standing tradition and a noble path for us to fast, praying to the Lord for the fulfillment of our intentions and the completion of our desired actions.

Therefore, some believe that fasting is a new phenomenon that has emerged recently. Some people think that this method is new, but we realize through the sacred history of Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman that it is a practice that has been with us for ages. Where is the beginning, where is the seed of this fasting that we undertake until our desired action is fulfilled? It is there when young children stubbornly refuse to eat to get what they want from their parents. The fasts observed by devotees who seek boons from God, by remaining hungry, are also based on this same concept. The subtlety of this is that the compassionate Primeval Lord, unable to bear the suffering of His fasting devotees, will fulfill their requests.

Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, being such a noble soul, Understanding this, he observes a fast here. At this juncture, Shiva Peruman appears in the dream of the king of that land and reveals that the Jains have concealed our temple, and that He is within, despite their concealment. Shiva Peruman reveals all the identifying marks of the Thiru-Koyil to the king in his dream.

Therefore, Shiva Peruman instructs the king in his dream, saying, “Go and remove the occupation of the Jains, and make arrangements for Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to enter and worship the Lord.” Shiva Peruman even accepts the concealment, revealing to the king in his dream that “concealment is also our state.” The Lord commands the king in his dream to destroy and remove the Jains who are without proper conduct. The Jains, who are without proper conduct, They are those who, not adhering to the bounds of their own path, harbor evil intentions to go against and destroy other religions.

Therefore, Shiva Peruman commands, “Remove such unrighteous Jains from this land.” The king, realizing the wondrous scene he saw in his dream, awakens. He explains it to his ministers. He understood the truth revealed by the Lord in his dream, through the signs the Lord had shown.

Thus, the king goes to the place occupied by the Jains. There, a thousand Jains had gathered together. Knowing that the king had arrived, a thousand Jains gathered there. Generally, there would be a thousand Jain gurus, and each Jain school would have a thousand gurus. It is customary for Jains to gather in thousands. In Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, the Jains had deceitfully occupied the Thiru-Koyil of Lord Shiva Peruman and established a Jain school there.

In that Jain school, similarly, a thousand Jain gurus were present. As the king arrived at this place, all those thousand Jains stood together. The king had his servants remove all those Jains from the place, driving them away. He removed the Vimanam (temple tower) of the Jain school, which the Jains had falsely established, and all their encroachments.

At that time, the Thiru-Koyil and the Vimanam of the Lord became visible.

Furthermore, he renovated, cleaned, and reconstructed the Thiru-Koyil. He reinstated the worship that had ceased there according to the Agamas. He established endowments for the performance of sacred ablutions, sacred offerings, daily rituals, and festivals. Shiva Peruman had revealed to the king in his dream, “Our government will worship, and remove the Jains.” Accordingly, the king, in order for Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman to worship the Lord, removed the Jains, established the Vimanam for the Lord, and arranged for worship and offerings. Following the Lord’s command, he then went to Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, prostrated at his sacred feet, and offered special reverence. He informed Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman that the Lord had revealed Himself after the removal of the Jains.

At that time, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sang a Thiru-Pathikam (sacred hymn) with the meaning, “Even if the Jains, who pluck their hair and eat, conceal Him, can those who are unstable in their nature conceal Him?” Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman sings a sacred hymn. Even if the Jains, who pluck all their hair and eat, conceal Him, can those who are unstable in their nature, with their limited intellect, conceal my Lord? This sacred hymn is the fifty-eighth Thiru-Pathikam in the fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam dedicated to Pazhaiyarai Vadathali.

“Thalaiyellam parikkum saman kaiyal nilaiyinan maraithan maraikkonnumae alaiyināru pozhil ārai vaḍathali nilaiyinān aḍiyē ninainthu uymminē” (Even if the Jains, who pluck all their hair, conceal Him, can those who are unstable conceal Him? O you who dwell in the beautiful groves of Arai Vadathali, remember His feet and be saved!) “Mūkkinal muran rōthiya kuṇṭikai thūkkinaar kulanthūr aṟuththē thanakkākkinān aṇi ārai vaḍathali” (He who carried the water pot with his nose, he who cut off the lineage of the wicked for himself, he who is in the beautiful Arai Vadathali) “Nōkkinārkku illai ālaru nōykalē” (Those who behold Him have no suffering.) “Kuṇṭarai guṇamillaraik kūraiyil miṇṭarai thuṟantha vimalan thannai aṇṭarai pazhaiyāṟai vaḍathazhi kaṇṭarai thozhuthuvaynthaṇa kaikaḷē” (My hands, having worshipped the pure one who abandoned the wicked, the immoral, and the quarrelsome, and who is in Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, are saved.) “Muḍaiyaṟai thalaimuṇṭikkum moṭṭarai kaḍaiyaṟai kaḍinthārkaṇal veṇmazhu paḍaiyaṟai pazhaiyāṟai vaḍathali uḍaiyaṟai kuḷirnthu uḷkum en uḷḷamē” (My heart, cooled and embraced, belongs to the Lord of Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, who wields the fiery white axe, who punished those who shaved their heads and were base.) “Oḷḷarikkaṇār munna maṇ ṇiṉṟuṇum kallarai kaḍintha karuppūralai aḷḷalam puṉal ārai vaḍathali vallalai pugazhath thuyar vāḍumē” (Praising the mighty one of Arai Vadathali, who punished the stony-hearted who ate before women, my sorrow will wither.) “Nīthiyai keḍa niṉṟamaṉēyuṇañcāthiyai keḍumā ceytha caṅkaran āthiyai pazhaiyāzhai vaḍathazhiccōthiyai thozhuvār thuyarthīrumē” (Those who worship the primordial light of Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, Shankaran, who destroyed the caste that stood to destroy justice, their sorrows will cease.) “Thiraṭṭiṟaikka vaḷanthiṇikkum camaṇ piraṭṭaṟai piriththa perumān thanai aruṭṭiṟa thaniyāṟai vaḍathali the” (The Lord who separated the deceitful Jains who gathered wealth, the unique one of Arai Vadathali, the divine one) “Iruṭṭaṟai thozha thīviṉai thīrumē” (Worshipping in the dark chamber, evil deeds will cease.) “Ōthiṉa theḻuththañcuṇarā camaṉ vēthiṉai paḍuththāṉai veṅkūṟṟu uthai pāthaṉai paḻaiyārai vaḍathali nāthaṉai thozha nam viṉai nācamē” (Worshipping the Lord of Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, who caused suffering to the Jains who did not understand the five letters, and whose foot kicked the fierce Yama, our karma will be destroyed.) “Vāyirunthamiḻē pāḍi thāḷu āyirañcamaṉum aḻivākkiṉāṉ pāyirum puṉal ārai vaḍathalimēyavaṉ eṉa valviṉai vīḍumē” (Singing in sweet Tamil, he destroyed a thousand Jains. Saying that he is the one who resides in Arai Vadathali with flowing waters, strong karma will cease.) “Ceruththaṉai ceyyum cē narakaṉ uḍal eruththira viralāl iṟai ūṉṟiya aruththaṉai paḻaiyārai vaḍathali thiruththaṉai thozhuvār thirucciṟṟampalam” (Those who worship the Lord of Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, who pressed down the body of the demon who caused war with his toe, will attain Thiruchitrambalam.) Thus, after the concealed Thiru-Koyil in Pazhaiyarai Vadathali was revealed, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman went there, sang, and worshipped the Lord.

He then continued his pilgrimage to many Thalam where Shiva Peruman resides on both banks of the Kaveri, offering Tamil garlands of praise and worshipping the Lord. He continues his pilgrimage, worshipping the Thalam on both banks of the Kaveri.

Let us go on reflecting.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 167 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 429, Thiru-Nindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, having departed from Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, journeyed westward, visiting the Thalam on the northern and southern banks of the Kaveri. Sekkizhar Peruman sings, “He entered the places where the Lord of the bull resides, on both banks of the Kaveri, filled with abundant waters, worshipped, offered Tamil garlands, and then, with his fame spread everywhere, he was met by countless devotees and reached Thiru-Anaikka, the abode of the Lord with the red-eyed bull.” As we mentioned earlier, Sekkizhar Peruman states in this verse that he departed westward from Pazhaiyarai Vadathali, visited the Thalam on both sides of the Kaveri, and reached the Thalam called Thiru-Anaikka.

Thus, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman visits many Thalam from Pazhaiyarai Vadathali to Thiru-Anaikka. These Thalam include Thiru-Pattiswaram, Arai Metrali, Thiru-Valanjuzhi, Thiru-Poonthuruthi, Thiru-Kandiyur, Thiru-Sotrutthurai, Thiru-Vethikudi, Thenkudi Thittai, Thiru-Pullamangai, Thiru-Chakkarappalli, Thiru-Vaiyaaru, Thiru-Nethanam, Thiru-Alampozhil, Thiru-Perumpuliyur, Thiru-Mazhapadi, Thiru-Pazhuvur, Thiru-Kanoor, Thiru-Anbil Alanthurai, Thiru-Manthurai, Thiru-Palathurai, and so on.

However, the Pathikam (hymns) sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar for all these Thalam are not available to us. However, we have received Pathikam by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for some of these sacred Thalam. These Thalam are Thiru-Alampozhil, Thiru-Kanoor, Thiru-Anbil Alanthurai, Thiru-Vethikudi, Thiru-Kandiyur, Melai Thiru-Kattuppalli, These are the Thalam for which Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman’s Thiru-Pathikam are available.

Therefore, let us examine them one by one. The first Thalam is Thiru-Alampozhil. For this Thalam, one Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathikam sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman is available. This sacred Thalam, Thiru-Alampozhil, is located near Thiru-Poonthuruthi in Thanjavur district. It is the tenth Thalam on the southern bank of the Kaveri. It is a Thalam where the Vasus worshipped and attained blessings.

The sanctum faces west. The Lord’s sacred name is Athmanathar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Gnanaambikai. The sacred water is the Kaveri Theertham. The sacred tree is the Banyan tree. This Thiru-Koyil is known as Arulmigu Vadamooleswarar Koyil.

Opposite the temple is a sacred tank. There is a five-tiered gopuram. Upon entering, one can worship the Thala Vinayagar and Murugan, then the Durga in the northern prakaram, and In the southern prakaram, one can worship Dakshinamurthy Peruman and then reach the Lord’s sanctum.

First, there is the Maha Mandapam, where the Navagrahas are located. One can worship the Ambāl’s sanctum here. After worshipping Vinayagar and reaching the Ardha Mandapam, one can worship the Nalvar. The Lord’s sanctum faces west. Swami is enshrined here as Arulmigu Vada Mooleswarar and Athmanathar. After worshipping Swami and Gnanaambikai, one can return.

This sacred Thalam, Thiru-Alampozhil, is mentioned in Thevaram as belonging to Then Parambaikkudi. Pirambai is now known as Pirambur. This Pirambur, where Vellalars reside, is called Vellamparambur. A short distance south of Alampozhil is a place called Sambandar Medu. We will discuss this in detail in the Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman Puranam. Kashyapar, Nagar, and the Ashtavasus worshipped the Lord here and attained blessings.

These are notes about the Thiru-Alampozhil Thalam. Here is the Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, the eighty-sixth Thiru-Pathikam of the sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandagam Thiru-Pathikam.

“Karuvāki kaṇṇuthalāy niṉṟāṉ taṉṉai kamalaththōṉ thalaiyariṉtha kāpāliyai uruvārntha malaimakaḷūr pākaththāṉai uṇarvellām āṉāṉai ōcaiyāki varuvāṉai valañcozhiyam perumān taṉṉai maṟaikkāḍum āvaḍu thaṉ thuṟaiyum mēya thiruvāṉai theṉ parampaikkuḍiyiṉ mēya thiru ālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who is the embryo, who has an eye on his forehead, who is the Kapali who cut off the head of Brahma, who has the beautiful mountain daughter as a part of himself, who is all consciousness, who comes as sound, who is the Lord of Valanjuzhi, who resides in Maraikkadu and Avaduthurai.) “Uritthāṉai kaḷirathaṉ thōl pōrvaiyāka uḍaiyāṉai uḍaippuliyiṉathalēyāka thariththāṉai caḍaiyathaṉmēl kaṅkai aṅkai thaḻal uruvai viḍam amuthā uṇḍi ithallām pariththāṉai pavaḷamāl varaiyanāṉai pāmpaṉaiyāṉ thaṉakkaṉṟaṅ” (He who wore the elephant’s skin as a covering, who wore the tiger’s skin as a garment, who bore the Ganga on his matted locks, who consumed poison as nectar, who is the coral mountain, who is the one for the serpent-bedecked one.) “Kaḷi nalki ciriththāṉai theṉparampaik kuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who laughed with joy.) “Uru mūṉṟāy uṇarviṉ kaṇ oṉṟu āṉāṉai ōṅkāra meypporuḷai uḍampiṉ uḷḷāl karu īṉṟa veṅkaḷavai aṟivāṉ taṉṉai kālaṉai thaṉ kaḻal aḍiyāl kāynthu māṇikku aruḷ īṉṟa ār amuthai amararkōṉai aḷḷūri emperumān eṉpārkku eṉṟum thiruvīṉṟa theṉparampai kuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who is the three forms, who is one in consciousness, who is the true meaning of Om, who knows the fierce deceit born within the body, who kicked Yama with his sacred foot, who bestowed grace upon Markandeya, who is the rare nectar, who is the Lord of the celestials, who is our Lord in Allur, who always bestows prosperity.) “Pārmuzhuthāy vicumpāki pāthāḷamām paramparaṉai curumpamarum kuzhalāl pākaththār amuthām aṇi thillai kūththaṉ taṉṉai vāṭpōkki ammāṉai emmāṉ eṉṟu vāramathām aḍiyārkku vāramāki vañcaṉai ceyvārkku eṉṟum vañcaṉākum cīraracai theṉ parampaikkuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālam pozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who is the whole earth, the sky, and the netherworld, who is the Supreme Being, who has the honey-like tresses as a part of himself, who is the beautiful Thillai dancer, who is our Lord of Vatpokki, who is always dear to his devotees, and who is always deceitful to those who deceive, who is the glorious king.) “Varaiyārntha maḍamaṅkai paṅkaṉ taṉṉai vāṉavarkkum vāṉavaṉai maṇiyai” (He who has the mountain maiden as his half, who is the Lord of the celestials, who is a gem.) “Muṭṭai aṟaiyārntha puliththōl mēl aṟavam mārththa ammāṉai thammāṉai aḍiyārkku eṉṟum puṟaiyārntha kōvaṇaththu em puṉithaṉtaṉṉai pūnthurutthi mēyāṉai pukalūrāṉai thiraiyārntha theṉparampai kuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who is our Lord, who wore the serpent over the tiger skin, who is our pure one with the sacred loincloth, who resides in Poonthuruthi, who is the Lord of Pukalur, who is in the wave-filled Then Parambaikkudi.) “Virinthāṉai kuvinthāṉai vēthaviththai viyaṉ piṟappōḍu iṟappāki niṉṟāṉ taṉṉai aṟinthāṉai calantharaṉ thaṉ uḍalam vēṟā āḻkaḍal nañcuṇḍu imaiyōrellām uyya parinthāṉai pallasurar puṟaṅkaḷ mūṉṟum pāḻpaḍuppāṉ cilai malai nāṇēṟṟi ambu therinthāṉai theṉparampaik kuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who expanded and contracted, who is the seed of the Vedas, who stands as vast birth and death, who knew, who consumed the poison of the deep sea to save all the celestials, who destroyed the body of Salandhara, who strung the bow of the mountain and chose the arrow to destroy the three cities of the many asuras.) “Pollātha eṉ aḻukkil pukuwāṉ eṉṉai puṟam puṟamē cōthiththa puṉithaṉ taṉṉai ellārum taṉṉaiyē ikaḻa annāḷ iḍupali eṉṟu akaṇṭiriyum emperumāṉai collāthār avarthamai collāthāṉai thoḍarnthu taṉ poṉṉaḍiyē pēṇuvārai cellātha neṟi celuththa vallāṉ taṉṉai thiruvālam pozhilāṉai” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who is the pure one who entered my evil filth and tested me outwardly, who is our Lord who wandered begging for alms on that day when everyone reviled him, who does not speak of those who do not speak of him, who is capable of leading those who follow and cherish his golden feet on the path that cannot be traversed.) “Ainthalaiththa nākaṉai kiḍantha māḷōḍu ayaṉthēḍi nāḍariya ammāṉ taṉṉai panthaṇavu melviralāḷ pākaththāṉai parāyththuṟaiyum veṇkāḍum payiṉṟāṉ taṉṉai poṇthudaiya veṇthalaiyil palikoḷvāṉai pūvaṇamum puṟampayamum porunthiṉāṉai cinthiya veṇthīviṉaikaḷ thīrppāṉ taṉṉai thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who is the Lord whom Vishnu, lying on the five-headed serpent, and Brahma searched for but could not find, who has the soft-fingered maiden as his half, who frequented Paraythurai and Venkadu, who receives alms in a skull with a hole, who is in Poovanam and Purambayam, who removes the white evil deeds that are thought of.) “Kaiyil uṇḍu uḻalvārum cākkiyarum kallātha vaṉmūṭkallāthāṉai poyyilāthavarkkeṉṟum poyyilāṉai pūṇākam nāṉāka poṟuppuvillā kaiyiṉār ambeṟik kāl īrkkum kōlā kaḍunthavaththōr neḍum puṟaṅkaḷ kaṉalvāy vīḻththa ceyyiṉār theṉ parampai kuḍiyiṉmēya thiruvālampozhilāṉai cinthi neñcē” (O mind, meditate on the Lord of Thiru-Alampozhil, who resides in Then Parambaikkudi, who is not for those who wander eating with their hands, nor for the Sakyas, nor for the ignorant, who is always truthful to the truthful, who made the serpent his ornament, who held the bow without a mountain, who shot arrows with his hand, who caused the long cities of the severe ascetics to fall into the fiery mouth.) The tenth verse in this Thiru-Pathikam is not available to us.

Next, the Thiru-Pathikam for the sacred Thalam called Thiru-Kanoor. Thiru-Kanoor is the fifty-sixth Thalam among the northern bank Thalam of the Kaveri in the Chola country.

Here, when the Goddess was in Shiva-Yoga, the Lord appeared as a blazing flame and granted His vision.

Therefore, Swami is known as Semmeninathar, and the Goddess is known as Shivayoga Nayaki. Thiru-Kanoor is a very small village. The temple is located on the southern bank of the Kollidam river. It is said that at one time, the temple was covered by an earthen mound, and later, the temple kalasam (finial) was struck by boys playing with cows, leading to the discovery of the temple. In recent times, new renovation works have been carried out, and the temple looks beautiful. The sanctum faces east, and there is a three-tiered Raja Gopuram.

Inside, the Ambāl’s sanctum faces south. There is one prakaram, a sacred kitchen, a well, and Nandavanams (flower gardens). In the western prakaram, there are temples for Vinayagar and Murugan, and in the northern prakaram, There are temples for Durga and Chandeesar. After passing the Nandi and Balipeetam, upon entering the Swami temple, there are shrines for the Nalvar, Bhairavar, Sastha, and others. Swami is known as Arulmigu Arumbeswarar. In Thevaram, he is referred to as Kanoor Mulai.

We have received one Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for this Thalam. The sacred trees are Vanni, Vilvam, and Sugarcane. The Kollidam is the sacred water. The Vimanam is a single-tiered, round-shaped Vimanam. The Ambāl’s idol is said to be a Salagrama idol. The Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam composed by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for this sacred Thalam is the seventy-sixth Thiru-Pathikam of the fifth Thiru-Murai.

“Thiruvin nāthaṉum cemmalar mēlurai oruvaṉāy ulakaththiṉ uyirkkellām karuvaṉāki muḷaiththavaṉ kāṉūril paramaṉāy parañca” (The Lord of prosperity, the unique one residing on the red lotus, who became the embryo for all living beings in the world, who sprouted in Kanoor, who is the Supreme Being, the Supreme Light.) “Suḍar kāṇamiṉē” (Behold the light!) “Peṇḍir makkaḷ perunthuṇai naṉṉithi uṇḍiṉṟē eṉṟu ukavaṉmiṉ ēḻaikāḷ kaṇḍu koṇmiṉ nīr kāṇūr muḷaiyiṉai puṇḍarīkap pothumpil othukkiyē” (O ignorant ones, do not rejoice saying, “Wives, children, great help, wealth, food are here.” Behold the sprout of Kanoor, hidden in the lotus pond.) “Thāyaththār thamar naṉṉithi eṉṉum immāyaththē kiḍanthiṭṭu mayaṅkiḍēl kāyaththēyuḷaṉ kāṇūr muḷaiyiṉai vāyaththāl vaṇaṅkīr viṉai māyavē” (Do not be deluded by this illusion called relatives, kinsmen, and good wealth. The sprout of Kanoor is within the body. Worship it with your mouth for karma to vanish.) “Kuṟiyil niṉṟuṇḍu kūṟaiyilā camaṉ neṟiyai viṭṭu niṟai kaḻal paṟṟiṉēṉ aṟiyaluṟṟirēl kāṇūr muḷaiyavaṉ ceṟivu ceythiṭṭu iruppathu eṉ cinthayē” (I have abandoned the path of the Jains who eat without clothes and have grasped the full feet. If you wish to know, the sprout of Kanoor is firmly established in my mind.) “Poththal maṇcuvar pollā kuṟampaiyai meythaṉeṉṟu viyaṅkiḍēl ēḻaikāḷ ciththar paththarkaḷ cēr thiru kāṇūril aththaṉ pātham aḍaithal karumamē” (O ignorant ones, do not marvel at this leaky mud wall, this evil hut, thinking it is real.

It is indeed a duty to attain the feet of the Lord in Thiru-Kanoor, where Siddhas and devotees gather.) “Kalvi ñāṉa kalaiporuḷāy avaṉ celvamalku thiru kāṇūr īcaṉai elliyum pakal” (The Lord of Thiru-Kanoor, who is the essence of education, knowledge, and arts, who is full of wealth, day and night.) “Icaivāṉava colliḍīr nuṇ thuyaraṅkaḷ thīravē” (Speak of him who is agreeable, so that subtle sorrows may cease.) “Nīrum pāṟum neruppum aṟukkaṇuṅ kāru māṟuthaṅ kāṇōr muḷaiththavaṉ cērvum oṉṟaṟiyāthu thicai thicai ōrvum oṉṟila rōḍi thirivarē” (They wander in all directions, not knowing the union of water, earth, fire, and air, nor the sprout that appeared, nor any thought.) “Ōmaththōḍaya mālaṟiyāvaṉam vīmappēroḻiyāy viḻupporuḷ kāmaṟkāynthavaṉ kāṇōr muḷaiththavaṉ cēmaththāl iruppu āvathu eṉ cinthayē” (My mind is a safe abode for the sprout that appeared in Kanoor, who is the noble substance, the great light, unknown to Brahma and Vishnu, who burnt Kama.) The ninth verse in this Thiru-Pathikam is not available.

Now, the tenth verse: “Vaṉṉi koṉṟai erukku aṇinthāṉ malai uṉṉiyē ceṉṟeḍuththavaṉ oṉ thiral taṉṉai vīḻa taṉi viral vaiththavaṉ kaṇṇimā mathil kāṇōr karuththaṉē” (He who adorned himself with Vanni, Konrai, and Erukku, who placed his single toe to make the one who went to lift the mountain fall, he is the Lord of Kanoor with the beautiful great walls.) 

Now, the next Thalam is Thiru-Anbil Alan Thurai. This sacred Thalam is the fifty-seventh Thalam on the northern bank of the Kaveri. It is known as Anbil. Lower Anbil, Anbil, Ambil, Anbil Alan. The Lord’s sacred names are Sathiyavakeeswarar, Brahmapureeswarar, and Alanthuraiyar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Soundaryanayaki.

The sthala tree is the Banyan, and the sacred water is Chandra Pushkarani. The village is Anbil, and the temple is Alanthurai. The Vinayagar here is known as Sevisaaitha Vinayagar (the listening Vinayagar). He is called so because he listened attentively to the sacred hymns of Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, sung from the south bank of the Kollidam river. Parantaka Chola settled 108 Agnihotris in this sthalam. Because he blessed their Jaimini Sama Veda recitation, this Vinayagar is also known as Samagana Ketta Vinayagar (the Vinayagar who heard the Sama Veda).

Later, he adopted the name Sevisaaitha Vinayagar, having listened to the songs of Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman’s sacred hymn: one. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal’s sacred hymn: one.

Thus, there are two sacred hymns for this sthalam. Beside the Dvarapalakas, there is a sculpture of Brahma worshipping. The Moolavar (presiding deity) is a Shiva Lingam, a Swayambhu Murthy (self-manifested idol) with a square pedestal. The sacred hymn by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal for this sthalam is the 80th hymn of the Fifth Thirumurai, a Thirukkurunthogai hymn.

“Vaananjer mathi soodiya mainthanai nee nenje keduvai ninaikkirkilai aananjaadiyai anbil alanthurai kon en selvanai kooridagittriye kaaranaththar karuththar kapaaliyar vaaranaththuri poorththa manaalanar aaranapporul anbil alanthurai naaranarkku ariyaan oru nambiye anbinna nanjamainthuda naadiya enbin aanaiyuriththuk kalainthavan anbilanai ammaanai allooriy anbinnaal ninainthaar arinthaargale.”
Gloss: “Oh heart, you will perish if you do not remember the Lord who wears the moon, who danced with the elephant, the king of Anbil Alanthurai, my Lord. He is the cause, the thought, the skull-bearer, the groom who wears the elephant hide. He is the essence of the Vedas, unknown even to Narayana in Anbil Alanthurai, a trustworthy one. Those who remembered with love the Lord who removed the poison with love and wore the elephant hide, they understood.” “Sankaiyullathum saavathum meyyumai panganaar adipaaviyen naan uyya angann enthai anbil alanthurai sengkannaaradi seravum vallane kokkiragar kulirmathi senniyar mikkarakkar purameri seythavar akkarainar anbil alanthurai nakkuruvarum nammai arivare vellamulla virisadai nanthiyai kallamulla manaththavar kaankilaar allalaar vayal anbil alanthurai ullavaaru ariyaar silar oomare piravi maaya pinakkil aluthinum uravellam sinthiththu unni ugavaathe aravan embiraan anbil alanthurai maravaathe tholuthu eththi vanangume nunangu noolaiyan maalum iruvarum pinangiyengum thirinthu eyththung kaankila anangan embiraan anbil alanthurai vanangum numvinai maaintharum vanname poyyellam uraikkum saman saakkiya kaiyan.”
Gloss: “I, a sinner at the feet of the Lord who shares His body with the Truth, can I reach the red-eyed feet of my Lord in Anbil Alanthurai to be saved?

“The Lord with the cool moon on His head, who destroyed the cities of the mighty Rakshasas, the Lord of Anbil Alanthurai, will also know us. Those with deceitful hearts cannot see Nandi with the flowing matted locks. Some in Anbil Alanthurai, with its fertile fields, are mute, not knowing the truth. Even if entangled in the illusory bonds of birth, do not think of all relations and rejoice. Worship and praise our Lord, the righteous one, in Anbil Alanthurai, without forgetting. The subtle-threaded Brahma and Vishnu, though they wandered everywhere in conflict and grew weary, could not see the formless Lord in Anbil Alanthurai.

“Worship Him, and your karma will be destroyed. The deceitful Jain and Buddhist who speak all falsehoods.” “Maarurai kelaathu eluminno aiyan embiraan anbil alanthurai meiyan sevadi etruvaar meyyare ilangai venthan irupathu thol itru malanga maamalai mel viral vaiththavan alangal embiraan anbil alanthurai valangolvaarai vaanor valangolvare Thiruchitrambalam thodarnthu sinthippom Thiruchitrambalam.”
Gloss: “Rise up, do not listen to opposing words! Those who accept the true sacred feet of our Lord in Anbil Alanthurai are indeed true.

“The Lord who placed His finger on the great mountain, causing the twenty shoulders of the king of Lanka to wither and fall, our garlanded Lord in Anbil Alanthurai. Those who circumambulate Him will be circumambulated by the celestials.

“We shall continue our meditation.”
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 168 — Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 430. We are contemplating the sacred hymns available to us from the sthalams visited by Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman on his way to Thiru-anaikka. In that sequence, the next sacred sthalam is Thiru-vedikudi. It is located in Thanjavur district, near Thiru-kandiyur, on the way from Thanjavur to Thiru-vaiyaru. This sthalam is called Vedikudi because Brahma worshipped here.

It is also called Vedikudi because the Vedas worshipped here.

The Lord is known as Vedapureeswarar. He also bears the sacred name Aara Amudhunathar. The Goddess shines with the sacred name Mangaiyarkarasi. Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman each sang one sacred hymn, making a total of two Thevara sacred hymns for this sacred sthalam. Thiru-vaiyaru, Aiyaru. This is the fourth of the seven sthalams in the Sapthasthana festival that takes place in the month of Chithirai.

At the Lord’s shrine, Vinayagar, who listens attentively to the Vedas expounded by the Lord with His four sacred faces, is known as Veda Vinayagar. The sacred water, Veda Theertham, is located opposite the temple. The sthala tree, the Vilva tree, is in the northern prakaram. The temple faces east. Opposite the temple, across the street, is the Veda Theertham. At one time, the current structure had two prakarams, but now there is only one.

The Goddess’s temple is in the second outer prakaram. Adjacent to the Nandi and Balipitam, the Goddess’s temple faces south. Next to the Goddess’s temple is the Vasantha Mandapam. After worshipping these, one can enter the temple. Passing through the small Rajagopuram with three tiers, one enters the temple to find the Maha Mandapam. The Natarajar Sabai is located here.

As one circumambulates the temple, 108 Shiva Lingams are consecrated in rows in the Thiru-maligai sections. In the Garbhagriha Koshtams, Dakshinamurthy is to the south, Ardhanareeswarar to the west, and Brahma to the north. In the western prakaram, one can worship Durga, Vinayagar, Murugan, and Mahalakshmi before reaching the Lord’s shrine. At the entrance to the Snapana Mandapam, Vinayagar and Murugan are visible. Entering the Ardha Mandapam, we are at the shrine. At the shrine, we can behold Vinayagar as Sevisaaitha Vinayagar, with his left leg raised.

It is believed that Vinayagar is listening to the Vedas, which the Lord expounds in this sthalam.

The Lord has a large form. Utsava Murthies (processional deities) are in the Ardha Mandapam, near the Natarajar shrine. The ancient and beautiful idol of the Goddess is located here. The sacred hymn by Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal for this sthalam is the 90th hymn of the Fourth Thirumurai, a Thiruviruttha sacred hymn.

“Kaiyathu kaalari naagam kanalvidu soolamathu veyyathu velai nanjunda virisadai vinnnavarkon seyyinil neela manang kamalun thiruvedikkudi ayyanai aara amuthinai naam adainthaaduthume kaiththala maan mari enthia kaiyan kanal malu van poyththalai enthi narpoodhiy aninthu palithirivaan seylaikal paainthu ukalu thiruvedikkudi aththanai aara amuthinai naam adainthu aaduthume munpin muthalvan munivan em melai vinai kaliththaan anbin nilaiyil avunar puram podiyaana seyyum semponai nanmalar melavan ser thiruvedikkudi anbanai nammai udaiyanai.”
Gloss: “With a snake in His hand, a fiery trident, He who consumed the terrible ocean poison, the Lord of the celestials with matted locks, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where blue lotuses bloom in the fields, that inexhaustible nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. He who holds a deer in His hand, with a fiery axe, who wanders for alms carrying a skull and adorned with sacred ash, whose deeds are leaping, that Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, that inexhaustible nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. The first and last, the sage, who removed our past karma, the golden one who destroys the cities of demons with love, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where Brahma on the good lotus resides, our loving Lord, our master.” “Naam adainthu aaduthume baktharkal naalum maravaar piraviyai ondru aruthaan muththarkal munnam pani seythu paaridam munnuyarththaan koththana kondrai manang kamalum thiruvedikkudi aththanai aara amuthinai naam adainthu aaduthume aananainthu erum kuri gunamaar arivaar avar ka maananainthu aadum mathiyum punalum sadaimudiyan thenanainthaadiya vandupayil thiruvedikkudi aananainthaadum maluvanai naam adainthu aaduthume ennum eluththum kuriyum aripavar thaam oliya pannin isai moli paadiyavaanavar thaam panivaar thinnen vinaikalai theerkkum piraan thiruvedikkudi nanna ariya amuthinai naam adainthu aaduthume oorntha vidai ukanthu eriya selvanai naam ariyom aarntha madamolli mangaiyor paa.”
Gloss: “Let us reach and dance in praise of Him. Devotees never forget Him daily, who cuts off rebirth, who was worshipped by the liberated ones before, who uplifted the earth.

“That Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where clusters of Konrai flowers spread fragrance, that inexhaustible nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. Those who know the nature of the bull He rides, they know Him. He with the moon and water in His matted locks, who dances with the deer. That Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where bees hum, that axe-wielding Lord who dances with the bull, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. Those who know numbers, letters, and symbols, they speak. The celestials who sang songs of musical language, they worship Him.

“That Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, who removes strong karmas, that rare nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. We do not know the wealthy one who gladly rides the bull. A modest maiden on one side.” “Aagam makilnthu udaiyan serntha punal sadai selvappiraan thiruvedikkudi saarntha vayal ani than amuthai adainthu aaduthume eriyum maluvinan enniyum matroruvan thalaiyul thiriyum paliyinan theyamum naadum ellam udaiyan viriyum polil ani seru thikal thiruvedikkudi ariya amuthinai anbarkalodu adainthu aaduthume maiyani kandan maraiviri naavan mathiththukandha meyyani neetran vilumiyavenmalu vaalpadaiyan seyya kamalam manang kamalum thiruvedikkudi ayyanai aara amuthinai naam adainthu aaduthume varuththanai vaalarakkanmudi tholodu patthiruttha poruththanai poyya arulani poothappadaiyudaiya thiruththanai thevarapiraan thiruvedikkudaiyaru ththanai aara amuthinai naam adainthu aaduthume Thiruchitrambalam.”
Gloss: “The wealthy Lord with matted locks, who delights in His body and has water in His hair, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, adorned with fields, that nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him. He with the fiery axe, who wanders for alms with another’s skull, who owns all lands and nations, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where beautiful groves spread, that rare nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him with devotees. He with the dark throat, whose tongue expounds the Vedas, who delights in sacred ash on His body, who wields the excellent white axe, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, where red lotuses spread fragrance, that inexhaustible nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him.

“He who crushed the ten heads of the powerful Rakshasa, the truthful bestower of grace, who has an army of Bhootas, the Lord of Thiru-vedikudi, the Lord of the Devas, that inexhaustible nectar, let us reach and dance in praise of Him.

“” The next sacred sthalam is Thiru-kandiyur. This is one of the Ashta Veeratta Sthalams. The Lord’s sacred names are Brahmasirakandeeswarar, Veeratteswarar, Brahmanathar, and Adhivillvanathar. The Goddess’s sacred name is Mangalanayaki. The sthala tree is the Vilvam.

“The sacred waters are Kapala Theertham, Nandi Theertham, Daksha Theertham, Brahma Theertham, and the Kudamurutti River.
