This place was named Kandana Puram or Kandiyur because the Lord severed one of Brahma’s five heads with His trident. After severing Brahma’s head, the Lord blessed him when he pleaded. Sadathapa Muni used to visit and worship during Pradosham. One time, when he came to Kandiyur, he could not reach the temple in time.

“At that moment, the Lord granted him the Darshan of Kalathi in this very sthalam.

“Furthermore, for Sadathapa Muni, the Vilva tree was brought from Kailash by the Lord and planted in this sthalam.

“Therefore, this place is also known as Adhivillvaranyam. This sthalam is said to remove the sin of Brahmagathi. Just as it is one of the Ashta Veeratta Sthalams, it is also one of the Sapthasthana Sthalams of Thiru-vaiyaru. During the Sapthasthana festival, the Lord comes here, rests for a while, and then proceeds. Since Sadathapa Muni was the elder brother of Silatha Muni, there is a tradition here that when the Lord rests, he is given a packed meal (kattuchoru) as an elder father-in-law. It is customary to send the Lord off with a packed meal of curd rice and puliyodarai.

“In the Navagraha shrine, Surya is seen with his two consorts. The Moolavar here is a Swayambhu Murthy, and the pedestal is somewhat tall. Brahma Deva is depicted holding a Japamala and praying to the Lord with both hands. There is a separate shrine for Brahma. The Vadugakolam (form of Bhairava) taken by the Lord to sever Brahma’s head is depicted as a small stone sculpture by the door of the entrance to Brahma’s shrine. Two Thevara sacred hymns are available for this sthalam.

“One is by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman, and one is by Appar Swamigal. Among them, the Thevaram sung by Appar Swamigal is the 93rd hymn of the Fourth Thirumurai, a Thiruviruttha sacred hymn.

““Vaanavar thaanavar vaikal malarkonarnthittu irainji thaanavar maal biraman ariyaatha thagaimaiyinaan aanavan aathipuraanan andru odiya panriyeytha kaanavani kandiyoor andavaanar tholukinrathe vaanamathiyamum vaalaravum punalodu sadai thaanamathuvana vaiththulal vaan thalal pol oruvan kaanamariyondru kaiyudaiya.”
Gloss: “The celestials and demons, bringing flowers daily, worshipped Him. He whose nature is unknown to Vishnu and Brahma, the ancient primordial one, who shot the boar that fled that day. The celestials worship the Lord of Kandiyur. He who wanders with the moon and the fierce snake and water in His matted locks, like a fiery one, holding a deer in one hand.” “Yaan kandiyoor iruntha oonamil vedamudaiyaanai naam adi olukuvathe pandangkaruththathor kaiyudaiyaan padaiththaan thalaiyai undangu aruththum oorodu naadavaiththaan ariyum kandangkaruththamidarudaiyaan kandiyoor iruntha thondarpiraanai kandeer andavaana tholukinrathe mudiyin mutraathathondrillai ellamudan thaanudaiyan kodiyum mutravidaiyeriyor kootrorupaaludaiyan kadiyamutravinai noy kalaivaan kandiyoor iruntha adiyumutraar thondar illai kandeer andavaanavare patriyoraanaiyuriththapiraan pavalaththiral pol mutrum aninthathor neerudaiyan munname koduththa katrangudaiyavan thaan ariyaan kandiyoor iruntha kutramilvedamudaiyaanai yaam andar kooruvathe porpanai yaanaiyuriththapira.”
Gloss: “Let us follow the feet of the Lord of Kandiyur, who possesses the flawless Vedas.

“He who holds a skull in His hand, who severed the head of Brahma and consumed it, and who knows all towns and nations. Behold the Lord of the devotees in Kandiyur, who has a dark throat, worshipped by the celestials. There is nothing incomplete in His crown; He possesses everything. He who rides the bull with a flag, who has a part of Yama. He who removes severe karma diseases, the Lord in Kandiyur. Behold, there are no devotees who have not reached His feet, O celestials.

“The Lord who flayed the elephant, who is adorned with sacred ash like a coral heap, who gave the stone before, He does not know. We, the celestials, speak of the flawless Lord of Kandiyur, who possesses the Vedas.

“The Lord who flayed the elephant in battle.” “Porivaay aravan serppathu vaanaththiraikadal sool ulagam ithanai kaappathu kaaranamaaga kondaana kandiyoor iruntha koorppudai ol vaalmaluvanai yaam andar kooruvathe attathu kaalanai aaynthatu vedam aaru angam andru suttathu kaamanai kannathanaale thodarnthu eriya kattavai moondrum eriththa piraan kandiyoor iruntha kutta mun vedappadaiyanai yaamandar kooruvathe attum oli neer ani mathiyum malaraana vellam ittu pothiyum sadaimudiyan indai maalai angai kattum aravathu thaanudaiyan kandiyoor iruntha kottum paraiyudai kooththanai yaamandar kooruvathe maainthana theevinai mangina noykal marukivila theynthanapaavam serukilla nammai setra nangai kaainthapiraan kandiyoor embiraan angam aarinaiyum aayntha piraan allano.”
Gloss: “The Lord with the fiery mouth, who protects this world surrounded by the wavy ocean, the Lord in Kandiyur with the sharp, bright axe, we, the celestials, speak of Him. He who kicked Yama, who studied the Vedas and the six Angas, who burned Kama with His eye, who burned the three cities that followed, the Lord in Kandiyur, who has the ancient Vedic army, we, the celestials, speak of Him. He with matted locks adorned with the moon and flowers, who binds the garland of flowers in His hand, who has the snake, the Lord in Kandiyur, the dancer with drum and cymbal, we, the celestials, speak of Him. Evil deeds perished, diseases vanished, sins diminished, our pride disappeared. Is He not the Lord of Kandiyur, our Lord, who burned the woman who angered us, who studied the six Angas?”

“Adiyenai aatkondavane mandi malaiyai eduththu maththaakki avvaasukiyai thandi amarar kadaintha kadal vidam kandaruli undapiraan nanjoliththa piraan anjiyodi nannakkanda piraanallano kandiyooranda vaanavane Thiruchitrambalam ini aduththa thiruththalam melai thirukkaattu palli iraivan uraiyum thirukkoilkalai palli endru kuriththirukkinranar nammudiya munnavarkal iththakaiya palli endra peyaruudaiya thalangal palavatrai thoguththu uraikkinraar thirunavukkarasasamikal poruppalli varaiyilla puram moondru eythu pulanthaliya salanthiranai pilanthaan porchakkara palli thirukkaattu palli kallar kamal kolliyarai palli kalavanjjaaral sirappalli sivappalli semban palli selunanippalli thavappalli seeraar parappalli endrendru.”
Gloss: “He who enslaved me, who took the Mandara mountain as a churning rod, and with Vasuki, the celestials churned the ocean, and He consumed the poison that appeared. Is He not the Lord who removed the poison, the Lord who saw the celestials flee in fear and then approached them, the Lord of Kandiyur, O celestial?

“Now, the next sacred sthalam is Melai Thiru-kattu Palli. Our ancestors referred to temples where the Lord resides as ‘Palli’. Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal compiles and describes many such sthalams with the name ‘Palli’: ‘Poruppalli, Varaiyilla, Puram Moondru Eythu, Pulanthaliya, Salanthiranai Pilanthaan, Porchakkara Palli, Thiru-kattu Palli, Kallar Kamal, Kolliyarai Palli, Kalavanjjaaral, Sirappalli, Sivappalli, Semban Palli, Selunanippalli, Thavappalli, Seeraar Parappalli,’ and so on.” “Pagarkor ellam paralokaththai inithaaga paalippaare endru paadukinraar aththakaiya palli endru valangappadum thalangalil sola vala naattil kaattu palli endra peyaruudaiya paadal petra thalangal irandu irukkinrana kaaviriyin vadakarai thiruvengkaattukku arugil ulla thalam keelaith thirukkaattu palli endrum inge melai thirukkaattu palli endra thalam ondrum irukkinrathu thiruvaiyaarukku arugile irukkinra thalam intha melai thirukkaattu palli endra thalam iththalaththirku thirugnana sambandha peruman paadiya thiruppathikam ondrum appar swamikal paadiya thiruppathikam ondrum aaga irandu thiruppathikangal irukkinrana swamiyin peyar arulmigu theeyaadi appar vadamoliyil agneeswarar ambikai peyar alakamar nayaki vadamoliyil soundarya nayaki theertham agni theertham matrum kaaviri sthalavirukkam vanni vilvam palangkaalaththil kottai koththalangalodu koodiya periya nagaramaaga.”
Gloss: “He sings that all who utter these names will joyfully attain the heavenly abode. Among such sthalams known as ‘Palli’ in the Chola country, there are two sthalams named ‘Kattu Palli’ that have received hymns. One is Keelai Thiru-kattu Palli, located on the north bank of the Kaveri, near Thiru-venkadu, and the other is Melai Thiru-kattu Palli, located here.

“This Melai Thiru-kattu Palli is near Thiru-vaiyaru. For this sthalam, there is one sacred hymn sung by Thiru-gnanasambandha Peruman and one sacred hymn sung by Appar Swamigal, making a total of two sacred hymns. The Lord’s name is Arulmigu Theeyaadi Appar, and in Sanskrit, Agneeswarar. The Goddess’s name is Alagamar Nayaki, and in Sanskrit, Soundarya Nayaki. The sacred waters are Agni Theertham and Kaveri. The sthala trees are Vanni and Vilvam.

“In ancient times, this town was a large city with forts and ramparts.” This temple is located in the center of the village, facing east. Upon entering through the Rajagopuram with seven tiers, Vinayagar is visible. After worshipping the flagstaff, Balipitam, and Nandi, one proceeds to the Lord’s shrine, which faces east, and the Goddess’s shrine, which is in the first prakaram, facing south. Opposite the Amman shrine, facing north, shines Narthana Vinayagar. Passing through the second gopuram and reaching the inner mandapam, to the right is the Natarajar Sabhamandapam.

“On the lower platform of the mandapam are the idols of Bhairavar and the Samayacharyas. Passing through the front mandapam, one can reach the Lord’s shrine. The place where the Lord is enshrined is very low. In the Mahamandapam are the Utsava Vigrahas (processional deities). In the inner prakaram are Valampuri Vinayagar, Thirumal, Lakshmi, Dakshinamurthy, Lingodbhavar, Murugan, Durga, and Chandeswarar. Thirumal, Brahma, Surya, Agni.

“Bhageerathan and the elder queen of Uraiyur Chola worshipped the Lord here and received His grace.

“Once, Indra and other Devas came to this sthalam and worshipped the Lord and Goddess.

“At that time, Agni Deva, who was like the face of the Devas, worshipped the Lord of this sthalam with many pujas to absolve himself of the sins incurred by destroying all things in the world.

“The Lord appeared to Agni Bhagavan and blessed him, saying, “Create a sacred water in your name, bathe in it, and continue to worship Me.” Agni Deva worshipped accordingly.

“The Lord granted His divine vision and blessed Agni Deva. The temple worshipped by Agni is named Agneeswaram. Those who bathe in Agni Theertham and worship on Karthigai Sunday, Masimagam, Panguni Uthiram, and Vaikasi Visakam will receive all blessings.

“The King gave the Chrysanthemum flowers, brought by a servant from the Uraiyur Nandavanam belonging to Lord Shiva, to his wives. The elder queen offered those flowers to Lord Shiva and worshipped Him, while the younger one adorned herself with them and rejoiced. When Uraiyur was destroyed by a sandstorm, only Thiru-kattu Palli, where the elder queen who worshipped Lord Shiva resided, survived without being destroyed, it is said here. The Panguni Uthiram festival is celebrated grandly. On Panguni Uthiram, the Lord grants sacred water in the Kaveri. There is one Thirukkurunthogai sacred hymn by Appar Swamigal for this sthalam.

“It is the 84th hymn of the Fifth Thirumurai.

““Maattuppalli makilnthurai veerarkellam kettuppalli kandeer keduvithu ottuppalli vittu odal uraa munam kaattuppalliyulaan kalal sermine maattai thedi makilnthu neer nummule naattu poyyellam pesidu naanileer koottai.”
Gloss: “To all the heroes who reside joyfully in Maattuppalli, behold the school of hearing, this is destruction. Before the school of running away and fleeing, reach the feet of the Lord in Kattu Palli. You shameless ones, who search for wealth and speak all falsehoods among yourselves, before the body leaves the soul.” “Vittu uyir povathan munname kaattuppalliyulaan kalal sermine thenai ventra sollaalu selvamum oonai vittu uyir povathan munname kaanavedar karuthungaattuppalli gnananaayakanai sendru nannnume aruththa mummanaiyalodu makkalum poruththamillai pollaathathu pokkidum karuththan kannuthal annal kaattuppalli thiruththan sevadiyai sendru sermine sutramum thunaiyum manai vaalkkaiyum atra pothanaiyaar avar endrendre katravarkal karuthum kaattuppalli petram erum piraan adi sermine adumbum kondraiyum vanniyum maththamum thudumbal seyda thoomani chothiyaan kadamban thaathai karuthum kaattuppalli udambinaarkkor uruthunaiyaagume meyyin maasudaiyaar udal mooduvaar poyyai meyyendru pukkudan.”
Gloss: “Before life leaves the body, reach the feet of the Lord in Kattu Palli. The wealth of the woman whose words conquered honey, before life leaves the body, the Lord of knowledge in Kattu Palli, whom the hunters seek, go and reach Him.

“There is no compatibility with the three wives and children who have been cut off.

“The Lord with the eye on His forehead, who removes evil thoughts, the righteous one in Kattu Palli, go and reach His sacred feet. When relatives, companions, and married life are gone, who are they?

“The Lord who rides the bull in Kattu Palli, whom the learned consider, reach His feet. The pure jewel-like light who wears Adumbu, Konrai, Vanni, and Maththam, the father of Kadamban, the Lord in Kattu Palli, will be a strong support for those with bodies. Those with impurities in their bodies, who cover themselves, do not enter and fall into falsehood, thinking it is truth.” “Veelanmin kaiyin maanudaiyan kaattuppalli em aiyan thannadiye adainthu uymine velai ventra kannaarai virumbi neer seelam kettuth thikaiyan min pedaikaal kaalaiye tholung kaattuppalliyurai neelakandanai nitthal ninamminne indrullaar naalai illai enum porul ondrum oraath tholitarum oomarkal andru vaanavarkkaaga vidamunda kandanar kaattuppalli kandu uymine ennilaa arakkan malai enthida enni neenmudi patthum eruththavan kannullaar karuthungaattuppalliyai nannuvaar avar tham vinai naasame Thiruchitrambalam thodarnthu sinthippom Thiruchitrambalam.”
Gloss: “Do not fall! Reach the feet of our Lord in Kattu Palli, who holds a deer in His hand, and be saved. You foolish ones, who desire women whose eyes conquered the ocean, do not lose your virtue and be bewildered.

“Worship the blue-throated Lord residing in Kattu Palli every morning and remember Him daily. You mute ones, who do not understand the meaning that those who are here today will not be tomorrow, behold the Lord with the throat who consumed poison for the celestials that day in Kattu Palli and be saved. Those who thought of lifting the countless Rakshasa’s mountain, and whose ten long crowns were crushed, those with eyes who seek Kattu Palli, their karma will be destroyed.

“Let us meditate further.”
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 169 — Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 431. Thirunindracharukkam. The Puranam of Thiru-navukkarasu Nayanar. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, who had been visiting the sthalams on both banks of the Kaveri, arrived at the sacred sthalam of Thiru-anaikka. Thiru-anaikka is a very famous sthalam known to everyone.

It is a sthalam located on an island between the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers, near Trichy. It is a sthalam on the north bank of the Kaveri. Thiru-navukkarasu Peruman, who came to this sacred sthalam, composed three sacred hymns. Before looking at those hymns, let us briefly contemplate the history and mythological accounts of Thiru-anaikka sthalam. The sthalam is Thiru-anaikka. The deity is Sri Jambukeswarar.

The Goddess is Sri Akilandeswari. The sacred waters are Brahma Theertham, Chandra Theertham, Jambu Theertham, Rama Theertham, and Srimath Theertham. The nine sacred bathing places (Thirthams) such as Agni Thirtham, Surya Thirtham, Indra Thirtham, and Agasthiya Thirtham, the processional deity Sri Somasakandar, the sthala-tree (sacred tree) Naval Maram, and the five circumambulatory paths (Pancha Prakaram) are the special features of this holy place. This sacred sthalam, known as Thiru-Aanaikka, also bears various other sacred names such as Thiru-Aanaikkaval, Gajaranyam, Jambukeswaram, Jambuveeswaram, Ven Naval Vanam, Jambuvana, Gnana Kshethram, Gnana Sthalam, Gnana Bhoomi, Kavai, Thanthi Pukaa Vaayil, Amutheeswaram, Thanthivanam, and Ibavanam. It is called Thiru-Aanaikka and Thiru-Aanaikkaval because the Peruman bestowed grace upon an elephant. It is known as Gajaranyam, Ibavanam, and Thanthivanam, meaning ‘forest where elephants resided’.

Since the Peruman is seated here beneath a white Naval tree, it is called Jambukeswaram, Jambuveeswaram, Ven Naval Vanam, and Jambu. It is also called Poovanam. Because the Ambikai received spiritual instruction (Gnana Upadesam) from the Lord, it is known as Gnana Kshethram, Gnana Sthalam, and Gnana Bhoomi. Due to its beautiful groves, it is called Kavai. It is named Thanthi Pukaa Vaayil because it was built in such a way that elephants could not enter. Since the deity, formed from the ambrosial water, is enshrined here, it is called Amutheeswaram.

This sthalam is one of the Panchabhootha Sthalams (five elemental shrines) representing water, hence it is also known as Appu Sthalam. This sthalam is beautifully situated amidst groves. The Swami Sannidhi faces west, and the Amman Sannidhi faces east. There are two prakarams in the Amman temple. This sacred temple has five prakarams from the inside to the outer street. During the Pancha Prakaram festival, the processional deities appear in all five prakarams.

The fourth and fifth prakarams contain houses. In the fourth prakaram, during festival seasons, processional deities are taken out, and chariot processions (Therottam) take place. Among the many walls surrounding this sthalam, the fourth wall is the largest; it is called Thiruneetru Mathil (sacred ash wall). Inside the temple, there are many thirthams, sannidhis, multi-tiered mandapams, large mandapams, and coconut groves. The Gajaranya Kshethra Mahatmyam states that Sri Ranganathar resides in Srirangam solely to worship the Peruman of this sthalam. Confirming this history, it is customary for the Perumal to come out from a grove here once a year, stay overnight, and return with special decorations that night, just as he would appear.

In later times, due to religious disputes between the two factions, this custom appears to have ceased.

The Lord enshrined in this sthalam is named Jambukeswarar. Other sacred names include Jambunathar, Jambunayagar, Vennavaleesar, Jambulingam, Appulingam, Amutalingam, Amutheeswarar, Brahmalingam, Brahmeesar, Gajaranyanathar, Pachathathapeswarar, Aadhi Perunjelvar, and Sangareswarar. Appar Swamigal praises the Peruman as ‘Sezhuneerthiral’ (abundance of rich water). In inscriptions, the names Thiru-Aanaikka Udaiyar, Thiru-Aanaikkavudaiya Nayanar, and Mahadevapattar are attributed to the Swami. The Goddess is known by the sacred names Akilandeswari, Akilanda Nayaki, and Akilandavalli, which mean ‘Mistress of all worlds’. To the north of this sthalam is the Kollidam River, and to the south is the Thirumanjana Kaveri.

Water for ablutions is brought from both the Kollidam and Thirumanjana Kaveri rivers. Not only this, but there are also nine Thirthams belonging to the temple. They are as follows: Brahma Thirtham, which is located in the south of the fourth prakaram, to the south of the road. Indra Thirtham, which is located in the southwest of the third prakaram, next to the Kasi Viswanathar Sannidhi.

Thirdly, Jambu Thirtham, which is located to the east of the third prakaram, near the old Jambukeswarar temple.

Fourthly, Rama Thirtham, which is the temple tank outside the fifth prakaram, to the west of the Sannidhi. The Theppa Thiruvizha (float festival) takes place in the month of Thai on Punarpoosam.

Fifthly, Srimath Thirtham, which is a small spring near the Moolalingam.

Sixthly, Agni Thirtham, which is a large well located in the third prakaram, in the southeast, next to the Vasantha Mandapam.

Seventhly, Agathiya Thirtham, which is a Sannidhi in the first prakaram of the Amman temple. It is a small well located opposite the Sannidhi, next to the Palliyarai (bedchamber).

Eighthly, Soma Thirtham, which is said to be the Chandra Pushkarani in Srirangam.

Ninthly, Surya Thirtham, which is the temple tank located in the fourth prakaram, in the southwest corner, opposite the Aayiram Kaal Mandapam (thousand-pillared hall). Surrounding it is a two-tiered mandapam with approximately one hundred pillars. The Theppa Thiruvizha takes place here in the month of Aadi on Pooram Nakshathiram.

Next, the glories of the sthalam: This sthalam possesses special significance in terms of Moorthy (deity), Sthalam (place), and Thirtham (sacred water). Among the Panchabhootha Sthalams, this is the Appu Sthalam (water element shrine). Among the Aaru Aadhara Sthalams (six energy centers), this is the Swathishtana Thirthalam. It is a temple where the Ambikai formed the deity from water. Even today, water can be seen seeping from the Moolalingam. It is a temple where an elephant and a spider competed to worship.

This sacred temple is foremost among the Maadak Kovils (elevated temples) built to prevent elephants from entering.

The Lord himself, appearing as a Siddhar, came and gave sacred ash as wages. It possesses the excellent wall known as Thiruneetru Mathil, which was built with sacred ash. When a Chola king was bathing in the Kaveri River, a pearl necklace he wore fell into the Kaveri. This necklace came to rest on the Lord’s neck through a sacred water pot (Thirumanjana Kudam). In front of the Swami Sannidhi, there is a balcony with nine openings. By worshipping the Lord through these openings, one receives the benefits of bathing in all nine Thirthams.

The Brahmotsavam is particularly suited to this sthalam. It is a Mandalotsavam (forty-day festival) conducted by Brahma. It features the excellent festival called Panchaprakaram. The Thirukkalyana Mahotsavam (sacred marriage festival) that occurs in other temples does not take place here. Daily cow worship (Go Pooja) is performed. The Swami receives daily Annabhishekam (rice anointing).

Besides the flagstaff in the Sannidhi, there are eight flagstaffs surrounding the third prakaram. Unlike other sacred temples, here on the sixth day of the festival, a grand procession (Perottam) takes place. On Margazhi Thiruvathirai, Nataraja Moorthy proceeds with the sixty-three Nayanmars. During the Uchchikala Pooja (midday worship), the Amman temple priest, dressed as a woman, worships the Lord. In the third prakaram, there is a Sannidhi for Jyeshtadevi. Kalamega Pulavar is renowned for having received the grace of the Ambikai.

The Naval tree is the sthala-vriksham (sacred tree). It contains many inscriptions. It is distinguished by having hymns sung by the Samayak Kuravargal (four great Shaivite saints). The temples surrounding this sacred temple are: The Rajarajeswarar Temple, which is located on the north street in the fourth prakaram. The Moolalingam in this temple has five faces and is known as Panchamukalingam. Next is the Neelavinteeswarar Temple, which is located to the west of the temple, to the west of Rama Thirtham, and was consecrated by Rama.

It is named thus because it was worshipped by Rama, who is Vishnu with a blue complexion. Next is the Sangareswarar Temple, which is in the third prakaram, at Jambu Thirtham. Besides these, within the main temple itself, apart from the Swami Sannidhi and Amman Sannidhis, there are also sub-temples such as the Mummoorthy Temple, Kasi Viswanathar Temple, Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple, Balathandayuthapani Temple, Saneeswarar Temple, and Vinayagar Temple. Inside the temple, there are many mandapams adorned with sculptures, including the Oonjal Mandapam, Noorrukaal Mandapam (hundred-pillared hall), Aayiram Kaal Mandapam (thousand-pillared hall), Vasantha Mandapam, Navarathri Mandapam, Dhwajastambha Mandapam, Somasakandar Mandapam, Natarajar Mandapam, and Mummoorthy Mandapam. There are two mandapams with one hundred and eight pillars. In the Aayiram Kaal Mandapam, the central mandapam is designed like a chariot, with many sculptures, chariot wheels, and horses.

Among these mandapams, the Somasakandar Mandapam stands out, showcasing ancient sculptural artistry. It is said to have been built by Rama. The stone corbels within it are crafted with bands, resembling wooden work. In this sthalam, the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagriham) of the Moolalingam is built small to prevent elephants from entering. The vimanas (towers) of the Moolamoorthies are constructed entirely of stone. The large Dhwajastambha Mandapam (flagstaff hall) in front of the Swami Sannidhi is prominent.

It is built upon four large pillars, with eight lions supporting each pillar. There is an ancient text called ‘Thiru-Aanaikka Thiruppani Maalai’. Through this, it is known that the walls, gopurams, and mandapams of this temple were renovated from time to time by the Cholas, Pandyas, Nayak kings, and other devotees. The names of kings such as Kochchengan Chozhan, Vijayabalan, Thiruneetru Chozhan, Vikrama Chozhan, Sundara Pandiyan, Kulasekara Pandiyan, Varaguna Pandiyan, Thirumalai Nayakkar, and various devotees are mentioned in this book. Those who worshipped the Lord in this sthalam include Brahma, Vishnu, Dikpalakas, Ashta Vasus, Jambu Muni, Ambikai, the spider, the elephant, Rama, Parachara, Chola Kochchengan Chozhan, Gautama, Kubera, Agathiyar, Surya, Chandra, Indra, Agni, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, Arunagirinathar, Aiyadigal Kadavar Kon, Kachiyappa Munivar, Kalamega Pulavar, and Mahavidwan Meenakshi Sundaram Pillai. In this temple, ablutions and worship (Abhisheka Aradhanai) are performed daily during the four periods: morning, midday, evening, and night.

There is no Abhishekam at Ardha Jamam (midnight). During the Uchchikala Pooja (midday worship), the Amman temple priest, dressed as a woman, circumambulates the Swami temple with attendants and performs worship. It is believed that the Ambikai herself performs the worship. Daily at midday, a cow is brought and worshipped in front of the Sannidhi as a custom. Festivals in this sthalam are conducted according to the Sakalagama Sangiraham. The Brahmotsavam begins annually in the month of Maasi and continues for forty days until Panguni.

During these days, festivals are held for all deities, including Vinayagar, Subramaniyar, Nalvar, Somasakandar, and Chandikeswarar. On the first day, earth is collected. Festivals for Vinayagar and Subramaniyar last five days, for Nalvar three days, for Kalyana Sundarar three days, for Chandrasekarar six days, for Somasakandar ten days, for Pallakku Chokkar three days, a silent festival for three days, for Chandikeswarar one day, Panchaprakaram one day, Vidayatri Utsavam one day, and Mandalabhishekam one day, totaling forty days of festivities. In the month of Maasi, the flag-hoisting (Kodiyetram) occurs on Mirugasirisa Nakshathiram, the chariot procession (Therottam) on Panguni Revathi, the sacred bath (Thirtham) on Rohini, and in the month of Panguni, Panchaprakaram takes place on Chithirai. The Panchaprakaram festival is celebrated with great grandeur. On that day, the Peruman, adorned in female attire, and the Ambikai, in male attire, parade through the five streets, granting their divine vision.

To witness this sacred sight, one would need a thousand eyes. Before the Brahmotsavam, a five-day festival for Pidari Amman takes place.

Additionally, in Vaikasi, the Vasanthotsavam (spring festival) is held for ten days in the Vasantha Mandapam. On Aani Pournami, the Swami receives Mupazha Abhishekam (anointing with three fruits), and on Aani Thirumanjanam, Natarajar proceeds in procession. In Aadi, on Karthigai day, the flag is hoisted, and the ten-day Aadi Pooram festival takes place. On Pooram, the last day, the Theppa Vizha (float festival) is held in the Surya Thirtham, which is an inner tank. In Aavani Moolam, the legend of carrying earth for Puttu (sweet dish) is enacted. In Purattasi, the Navarathri festival is celebrated for ten days in the Navarathri Mandapam within the Amman Sannidhi.

In Aippasi Kanda Sashti, the Soorasamharam Utsavam (festival of slaying the demon Soora) takes place, and in the month of Karthigai, on every Somavaram (Monday), Sangabhishekam (conch anointing) and on Periya Karthigai, Sudalai Deepam (cemetery lamp) takes place. In Margazhi, on Thiruvathirai day, Natarajar from the second prakaram proceeds with the sixty-three Nayanmars. The Moola Natarajar in the first prakaram does not proceed. In the month of Thai, a forty-day festival takes place, and on the last day, the Theppa Thiruvizha (float festival) is held in Rama Thirtham. On Thai Poosam, the Swami goes to the Kollidam riverbank and on Maasi Magam to the Kaveri riverbank, performs Thirtham (sacred bath), and returns at night. On Chithirai Vishu Punyakalam (auspicious time), at night, the Rishabha Vahana Purappadu (procession on bull mount) and the reading of the new Panchangam take place.

On Pournami, Marukkozhundus Moolam Abhishekam. On Vaikasi Pournami, Eka Vasantham. Before this, on the tenth day, the Vasanthotsavam begins. On Pournami Vaikasi Pournami, Annabhishekam. On Vaikasi Visaka Nakshathiram, Paal Maangai Abhishekam (milk and mango anointing). On Aani Uthira Nakshathiram, Aani Thirumanjanam.

The next day, Natarajar proceeds in procession. On Pournami, Muppal Abhishekam. On Aadi Dakshinayana Punyakalam, Thirthavari in the daytime, and Rishabha Vahana Purappadu at night. On Aadi Bharani Nakshathiram, Aadi Pooram Utsava Dhwaja Arohanam (flag hoisting). On the first day, Aadi Pooram Nakshathiram Thirtham. On the twelfth day, Thiruvadi Pooram Theppakulam Theppotsavam (float festival).

On Aadi Amavasai, Rishabha Vahanam Purappadu at night. On Pournami, Pattu Pavithram. On Aavani Moola Nakshathiram, Aavani Moolam Swami Pittu Man Sumandha Utsavam (festival of the Lord carrying earth for Puttu). On Aavani Pournami, Thilabhishekam. On Purattasi Krishna Chathurthi, Navarathri Utsava Aarambam (beginning of Navarathri festival). On Saraswathi Vijayadasami, Ambu Eythal (shooting arrow) and Paalabhishekam.

On Aippasi Deepavali, Abhishekam. On Aippasi Pournami, Vibhuthi Abhishekam. Skanda Sashti Utsavam. On Karthigai Pournami, Kiruthappadam. On Margazhi Dhanurmasa Pooja Aarambam. On Thiruvathirai, Arudra Darisanam.

On the first day of Margazhi, Thiruppavai Manikkavasagar Utsavam. On Margazhi Pournami, Aryabhishekam. On Margazhi Maha Vyapatha Dinam, Udaya Vyapthi Pavadai. In the month of Thai, Uttarayana Punyakalam, Makar Sankranti, Thirtham in the morning, Rishabha Vahanam at night. On Thai Amavasai, Rishabha Vahanam at night. On Thai Sathayam Nakshathiram, Thai Theppotsavam.

On Thai Poosam, Thirthavari in Kollidam, Rishabha Vahanam at night. On the last Tuesday of Thai month, Pidariyar Utsavam, first Kaappu. On Thai Pournami, Madhu Abhishekam. In the month of Maasi, Maha Shivaratri Abhisheka Aradhanai, Rishabha Vahanam. On Maasi Pournami, Kiruthappadam. In Panguni, as we have already seen, the Mandala Brahmotsavam.

In this festival, Thervadaichan Rishabha Vahanam, Rathotsavam, Panchaprakara Mahotsavam, etc., are celebrated grandly. Panguni Pournami Kandabhishekam will take place. These are all the special features of the Thiru-Aanaikka sthalam. The Thiru-Aanaikka Thirthalam is a sacred place with a very rich mythological history. Many saints have worshipped the Lord here.

We will continue to reflect on all those mythological histories.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 170 — Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 432. Thirunindrachcharukkam, Thirunavukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. We are contemplating the special features of the Thiru-Aanaikka sthalam. Let us briefly reflect on the mythological history of Thiru-Aanaikka.

First, the mythological history of the elephant and the spider’s worship. On Mount Kailash, there are many Gananathas. Among them are two, Maliyavan and Pushpadanthan. Both were preeminent in their devotion to Shiva. They competed with each other in Shiva devotion, each believing himself to be superior. Due to this rivalry in Shiva devotion, they became envious of each other and harbored enmity.

One day, Maliyavan cursed Pushpadanthan to become an elephant. Pushpadanthan, in turn, cursed Maliyavan to become a spider. Both appealed to the Peruman. The Peruman, in His divine grace, instructed them to go to the Gnana Sthalam in the Chola country, worship Him there, and thus be freed from their curses.

Accordingly, the two Gananathas were born as an elephant and a spider in the Thiru-Aanaikka sthalam. Born here as an elephant and a spider, they desired to worship the Peruman residing here and attain liberation. The elephant bathed in many Thirthams.

Then, filling its trunk with water and gathering many flowers, it entered the Sannidhi of the Peruman. It removed the dry leaves and other debris lying there, performed sacred ablution (Thiru Abhishekam) on the Peruman’s sacred head with the water brought in its trunk, and then lovingly offered the many flowers it had gathered to the Peruman, worshipped Him, and returned to its dwelling. While the elephant was thus worshipping, the spider resided in a Naval tree. From the tree’s hollow, it wove a canopy with its silk threads to prevent dust and leaves from falling on Lord Shiva, and thus worshipped Him. The next morning, the elephant, as usual, bathed, gathered flowers, and came to the Sannidhi. It became enraged upon seeing the canopy woven with threads above the Peruman’s head.

Believing the presence of threads there to be an offense, it destroyed the silk canopy made by the spider, purified the spot, bathed again, and again worshipped the Peruman.

Thus, the spider and the elephant worshipped the Peruman alternately. The spider would weave a silk canopy, and the next day the elephant would destroy it. This continued until one day the spider hid on one side of the tree to discover how its silk canopy was being destroyed. The elephant arrived as usual, destroyed the silk canopy made by the spider, and worshipped as before. The hidden spider, seeing its silk canopy destroyed by the elephant, became enraged. It entered the elephant’s trunk, swiftly climbed up, reached the elephant’s skull, and bit it.

The elephant trumpeted like thunder, fell down, rolled here and there, suffered various torments, and died. As the elephant died, the spider, having entered it, also died, unable to find a way out.

At that moment, both, freed from their enmity, appeared in divine form. The Peruman, granting them His vision, said, “Because you worshipped Us with love, you have attained a glory worthy of being worshipped by the Devas. The one who was freed from the elephant form will shine as a Gananatha in Our world as before. This sthalam will be known by the name of him who worshipped in the form of an elephant. You, freed from the spider form, will be born as a king in the Chola dynasty, perform many righteous deeds, and attain liberation.” Thus, Lord Shiva bestowed His grace upon the elephant and the spider and disappeared.

Therefore, this sthalam came to be known as Thiru-Aanaikka because grace was bestowed upon an elephant. The Gananatha who was freed from the elephant form returned to Kailash. The Gananatha who was freed from the spider form was born as the son of Subadeva and Kamalavathi in the Chola dynasty and ruled for a long time with the name Kochchengan Chozhan, due to his red eyes. He built many sacred temples for Lord Shiva to reside in. Thirumangai Azhwar sang about Kochchengan Chozha Nayanar: “He built seventy beautiful elevated temples for the eight-shouldered Lord and ruled the world, the Chola who flourished in the sacred lineage.” Kochchengan Chozha Nayanar was the one who built seventy elevated temples that elephants could not enter. This is the story of the elephant and the spider’s worship in this sthalam.

Secondly, the history of Jambu Muni’s penance. In this sthalam, which was once a Jambu Vanam (forest of Naval trees) filled with Naval trees, a sage once performed severe penance, controlling his senses.

One day, a white Naval fruit fell from a Naval tree before the sage. It was very luminous and had a sweet taste. The sage picked up the fruit and was astonished by its greatness. Thinking that he should not eat it himself but offer it to the Lord, he went to Mount Kailash and offered the precious fruit he had brought to the Peruman. The fruit, having been eaten, began to sprout within the sage’s stomach and grew into a large tree, causing the sage’s head to burst. The sage, now in the form of a tree, performed an ecstatic dance and praised the Peruman.

He requested that this fruit, now grown into a tree, with its mother tree on the sage’s head, should reside in the shade of that mother tree. The Peruman, bestowing His grace upon the sage, instructed him to return to the place where the fruit had originally fallen, promising to come there Himself. The sage, who had taken the form of a tree, desired to reach this sacred place of knowledge and set out from Kailash, walking. Many were astonished to see the tree walking.

Thus, he came to the very spot where the fruit had fallen, to that Jambu Vanam, and performed severe penance for a long time. The Peruman, moved by his penance, resided in the shade of the Naval tree as the sage desired. This glorious Naval tree serves as the sthala-vriksham. Since the Peruman is enshrined beneath the Naval, or Jambu, tree, He is known as Jambunathar.

Next, thirdly, the history of Panchaprakaram, Brahma Devan, his At a time when Brahma was very proud of his creative work, he created a woman of exquisite beauty. Upon seeing her, Brahma, driven by fate, conceived an evil desire for her, like a Chataka bird seeing a cloud.

Consequently, the power of his creative work diminished. Those he created deviated from the path of righteousness and followed evil ways. They met untimely and unnatural deaths. Witnessing this, Brahma realized his mistake and trembled with fear. Seeking atonement for his sin, he came to Thiru-Anaikka, a sacred place of wisdom, and began severe penance. Peruman, understanding this, and wishing to purify Brahma’s mind, came here with the Goddess.

At that time, Shiva disguised as the Goddess and the Goddess disguised as Shiva, appeared before Brahma. Brahma, seeing Shiva standing before him in the form of a woman, fell like a uprooted tree. He prostrated at Shiva’s sacred feet and praised Him in many ways. He prayed that his sin, committed out of ignorance, be forgiven and that he be granted the grace to resume his creative work. Shiva, seeing Brahma’s mature state, bestowed His grace and disappeared with the Goddess. Brahma bathed in the Thirtham he had created and circumambulated the five prakarams (corridors), worshipping Peruman.

He grandly conducted a Mandala Brahmotsavam for forty days for Peruman Jambukeswara. On the thirty-seventh day, Peruman, just as He had appeared to Brahma, manifested with the Lord in the form of a woman and the Goddess in the form of a man, and conducted the Panchaprakara Utsavam. This festival continues to be celebrated annually to this day.

Fourthly, the history of the Goddess receiving instruction.

One day, Uma Devi worshipped Paramasivan, the Lord of Kailash, and raised a question about a doubtful matter. Peruman addressed Uma Devi, saying, “Go to a sacred place of wisdom on earth and perform penance. We will come there and instruct you.” Uma Devi was deeply saddened, unwilling to part from Paramasivan. Peruman comforted the Goddess, gave her assurance, and sent her to the sacred place of wisdom. The Goddess took leave, praising Peruman, and, as per His command, arrived at Thiru-Anaikka with the Bhootha Ganas (celestial attendants) and her companions. The sages performing penance there saw the Goddess and worshipped her.

The Goddess desired to bathe in the various Thirthams here and worship Peruman. The Goddess’s attendants gathered all the necessary items for the worship. The Goddess, wishing to understand the nature of Mukti, which bestows bliss, decided to consecrate a Shiva Lingam made of sweet-tasting water.

Therefore, meditating on the sacred feet of the Lord, she gathered the Thirtham itself and consecrated it as a luminous Lingam. Due to this, this Lingam came to be known as Appu Lingam (Water Lingam). As the devotion of the Goddess grew, the Thirtham overflowed from that spot. It was named Srimath Thirtham. The Goddess performed Abhishekam to Peruman according to tradition, performed Shiva Puja, and offered praises.

One day, during this daily Shiva Puja, Peruman appeared to the Goddess on His Rishabam (bull mount). The Goddess, with her spiritual eye, beheld the Lord whom she could not perceive with her physical eyes. The Goddess, not for herself but for the sake of other beings, sought and received many boons from Shiva.

Afterwards, the Goddess requested Peruman to clarify the doubt she had initially asked on Kailash. Peruman addressed Uma Devi, saying, “You asked about the truth of Yoga. I will tell you now, listen. All worlds operate by Our grace.

“Therefore, just as a dance instructor first demonstrates the dance himself, We must first train the world.

“Thus, to enable the souls in the world to experience enjoyment, We embraced you and became a Bhogi (one who enjoys), and to enable them to attain true knowledge through Yoga and achieve salvation, We became a Yogi.” Peruman thus instructed the Goddess. The Goddess was greatly delighted. We can recall here Karuvur Devar’s eleventh verse in the Thiru-Pathigam of Gangaikonda Cholapuram in the Ninth Thiru-Murai, where he sings, “He who performs Yoga while with the maiden.” We can also recall here Appar Peruman’s third verse in the fiftieth Thiru-Pathigam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai, where he sings, “He who conquered the five senses while united with the beautiful maiden.” After hearing this instruction, the Goddess again asked Peruman, “I wish to understand Mala (impurity), Jiva (soul), Maya (illusion), Karma (action), true knowledge, and Mukti (liberation). Please instruct me on these.” Peruman clearly instructed her on their natures. To signify that the Goddess received instruction, the Swami Sannidhi (Lord’s shrine) faces west and the Amman Sannidhi (Goddess’s shrine) faces east in this temple.

“Therefore, such an arrangement is called an Upadesa Sthalam (place of instruction). Kachiappa Munivar, in his Thiru-Anaikka Puranam, has dedicated a chapter called ‘Gnana Upadesa Padalam’ (Chapter on the Instruction of Wisdom). In this chapter, Kachiappa Munivar has extensively described the nuances of Saiva Siddhanta that Peruman instructed to the Goddess. In the book titled Thiru-Anaikka Puranam.

“Now, fifthly, the history of Rama’s worship. When Rama returned after completing the destruction of Ravana and others, and rescuing Sita, the shadows of Ravana and Kumbhakarna followed Rama, threatening him. Rama, intending to dispel them, consecrated a Shiva Lingam at Rameswaram and worshipped it. Only Ravana’s shadow disappeared. Rama saw that Kumbhakarna’s shadow continued to follow him. As Rama was contemplating how to remove it, upon reaching the boundary of Jambukeswaram, Kumbhakarna’s shadow vanished like darkness before the sun.

“Rama was greatly pleased, bathed in several Thirthams, went to the Sannidhi, and worshipped Shiva, the Lord, and Akhilanda Nayaki. Afterwards, Rama met the sages there and recounted how the shadow had come, and how it had disappeared at the boundary of this sacred place. They told Rama, “In this sacred place, which is excellent in its Moorthy (deity), Sthalam (place), and Thirtham (sacred water), evils like ghosts, shadows, and diseases will not approach. If you cross the boundary of this place, that shadow will follow you again.

“Therefore, to ensure it never follows you, consecrate a Shiva Lingam here, worship it, and dispel it.” The sages advised Rama. Rama commanded Angathan to bring a Shiva Lingam. Angathan brought an emerald Lingam. Rama created a Thirtham to the west of the Lord’s Sannidhi, built a temple nearby, and, according to tradition, consecrated the new Lingam there. He worshipped and praised Peruman and the Goddess with a melting heart. Peruman appeared to Rama with the Goddess.

“Rama worshipped Shiva and the Goddess, then returned to Ayodhya and ruled the kingdom. The deity consecrated by Rama is known as Neelavinteeswarar. The Thirtham created by Rama is known as Rama Thirtham here.

“Now, sixthly, the history of Peruman wearing a pearl necklace. In Uraiyur, the capital of the Chola country watered by the Kaveri, a Chola king ruled. He was very devoted to Shiva and His devotees. He regularly performed the daily and occasional pujas in the temples where Shiva resided, without fail.

“At that time, winter ended and summer began, and the heat intensified. The Chola king who ruled Uraiyur then sent many items to Peruman residing in Thiru-Anaikka, the sacred place of wisdom, to alleviate the heat, and set out with his wife to have Darshan. Seeing the pearl necklace on his wife’s chest, the king, due to his devotion to Shiva, wished to adorn Peruman with that beautiful pearl necklace.

“At that time, as the king and his wife were bathing in the Kaveri, the pearl necklace worn by his wife slipped into the river. The king was greatly distressed that the pearl necklace, which he had intended to offer to the Lord, had slipped into the river. He praised Peruman in his thoughts.

“Then, crossing the Kaveri, he came to Thiru-Anaikka and had Darshan of Peruman.

“At that time, the temple priests performed Thirumanjanam (sacred bath) for Peruman with the Thirtham brought from the Kaveri.

“Then, by the grace of Shiva, the pearl necklace that had fallen into the Kaveri entered the Thirumanjana pot and, during the Abhishekam, fell onto Peruman’s sacred head along with the Thirtham. Everyone was astonished. The king also saw it and was amazed. He praised Peruman, saying, “O Lord, the leader who resides in Jambumoolam! How great is Your grace upon me! You, who removed the troublesome river, and adorned Your sacred head with the celestial river, causing wonder!” The fame of that king endures in the world even today.

“Sundaramurthy Swamigal has sung about this history in his Thevaram, in the song beginning “Tharamakiya Ponni.” Now, next, seventhly, the history of the sacred ash wall. Many days ago, when Kochchengan Cholan and other kings were performing renovation work on temples, by the grace of Peruman, a voice would always be heard from the sky, saying, “Perform all other works except the great wall.” Whenever they performed renovation work, this voice would be heard.

“One day, while renovation work was in progress, Peruman came as an ascetic, wearing saffron robes, with matted hair, rudraksha beads, and sacred ash. He began to build the sacred ash wall with carpenters and other laborers. He gave sacred ash as wages to the laborers. That sacred ash transformed into gold according to their work. The Siddhar who came as an ascetic performed many wonders and miracles. Such is the glory of that sacred ash wall.

“This sacred place possesses many such historical and Puranic narratives. There are seven Thiru-Pathigams sung by the Thevara Moovar (three great Shaivite saints) for this sacred place. There are three Pathigams by Thiru-Gnanasambandha Peruman, three Pathigams by Appar Swamigal, and one Thiru-Pathigam by Sundaramurthy Swamigal, making a total of seven Thiru-Pathigams for this Sthalam. This Sthalam has been sung by the Moovar. The Thiru-Anaikka Puranam, composed by Sri Kachiappa Munivar, consists of twenty-one chapters. There is another Puranam called Thanthivana Puranam.

“Its author is said to be Kamalai Sri Gnanaprakasar. All these are details, special features, and historical accounts about Thiru-Anaikka Sthalam. May Arul Valar Sambu Moolathu Amuthalingesar live long! May Akilanda Valli live long! May the essence of the Vedas and Agamas flourish! May the glorious sacred city of Thiru-Anaikka live long!

“May all lands live long, O Mother! May the righteous Kaveri live long! May Akilanda Ammai live long! May all the abundant clusters of the earth live long! May the Lord of the world, who renounces attachment, live long in His true glory! May the sacred feet of the excellent Sambunathan live long!

“Thus, praising and extolling Jambukeswara and Akilandeswari Ammai, and praising the sacred feet of the Lord of Anaikkaval, we shall now contemplate the three Thiru-Pathigams bestowed upon this Sthalam by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman.”
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 171 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 433, Thirunindrachcharukkam, Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar came to Thiru-Anaikka Sthalam, worshipped the Lord there, and sang Thiru-Pathigams. Appar Swamigal sang a total of three Pathigams for Thiru-Anaikka Sthalam. The first Thiru-Pathigam is the Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathigam from the Fifth Thiru-Murai, the thirty-first Thiru-Pathigam from the Fifth Thiru-Murai.

“The Lord of the forest, cool and fragrant, some southerners do not drink the honey. They do not approach our Lord in Anaikka, but carry their bodies and wander like fools.” “O Lord of Anaikka, who stands near, without any flaw, for those who remove their crooked thoughts, make them righteous, and melt with devotion, knowing the path, holding onto the essence of the town.” “Without sorrow, without suffering, if you desire bliss, praise Him day and night. To those who contemplate, ‘My golden Lord is the Ruler,’ the Lord of Anaikka will be a friend.” “O Lord of Anaikka, who says ‘Ah!’ to all who praise His sacred feet with their tongues, without ceasing, and whose sins are removed by those who worship with their hands, saying ‘Protect me!’” “Worship without deceit, always. Avoid harsh words to attain liberation. To all whose hearts cool down, melting and melting, the Lord of Anaikka says, ‘Fear not!’” “Do not speak atheism, thinking the body is real.

“The five elements come like armies. To all who take refuge in Him without any hindrance, the Lord of Anaikka is a refuge.” “Before the nine gates of the flowing body are consumed by vultures, worship His sacred feet, offer pure flowers with your hands, and to those who weep, the Lord of Anaikka is a friend.” “O people of the world, who cannot comprehend when it rolls! Do not let evil deeds approach you firmly. To all who remove darkness and say, ‘He is the Lord,’ the Lord of Anaikka bestows grace.” “O my foolish heart, remember with love! The family and relatives that are destined for destruction, leave attachment and desire the supreme bliss of the Lord of Anaikka.” “The Lord of Anaikka, who is the beginning, who, when the king of Lanka, surrounded by the vast ocean, sang songs and played the Kinnaram, accepted his feet and bestowed grace.” The second Thiru-Pathigam is the sixty-second Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathigam, from the Sixth Thiru-Murai.

““What mother, what father, what relatives, what wealth is mine? Who are the good ones? No one will come to help when one dies. They will light the fire with small firewood and depart. O Lord of Thiru-Anaikka, the wealthy one, with the form of an ascetic, residing in the long Ponni river!

“If I attain Your golden feet, what else can I, Your servant, do with this body?” “You are the body, the life, the consciousness within it, and all else. You came into me without my knowing anything, and showed me both good and evil. O Lord with the honeyed Konrai flower, residing in Nindriyur, Shiva residing in Thiru-Anaikka! You are knowledge. If I attain Your golden feet, what else can I, Your servant, do with this body?” “You are incomparable. You live in harmony with this world.

“You stand with those who are not one with others. You are the one who protects me, who wanders, eating meager food, forgetting my true nature, and makes me subtle consciousness everywhere, and rules me, O beautiful Lord of Anaikka! You are the body, the life, the consciousness within it, and all else. You came into me without my knowing anything, and showed me both good and evil. O Lord with the honeyed Konrai flower, residing in Nindriyur, Shiva residing in Thiru-Anaikka! You are knowledge.

“If I attain Your golden feet, what else can I, Your servant, do with this body?” “You are incomparable. You live in harmony with this world. You stand with those who are not one with others. You are the one who protects me, who wanders, eating meager food, forgetting my true nature, and makes me subtle consciousness everywhere, and rules me, O beautiful Lord of Anaikka! O Father of the celestials, O Lord of Anaikka! If I attain Your golden feet, what else can I, Your servant, do with this body?” “You are in the hearts of those who remember You, O deceitful thief!

“You have the full moon in Your matted hair. You destroyed the three cities of those who opposed You. O Primeval One, who wore the skin of the elephant! O Lord with the blue throat, who rides the roaring bull! O Lord of Kailash mountain! I have reached Your ocean.

“O Lord who rules all worlds, O Lord of Anaikka! If I attain Your golden feet, what else can I, Your servant, do with this body?” “O Lord, who saved me, a servant, from being caught in the whirlpool of suffering in the ocean of this illusory birth, by helping my mind, which is like a wild elephant, with compassion, and placing love in me, O Invisible One! O Brahmin, who wore the skin of the fierce, intoxicated elephant! O Lord residing in Thiru-Anaikka! If I attain Your golden feet, what else can I, Your servant, do with this body?” “O Lord of Uraiyur, whose fame is enduring, O Lord of Kachi Ekambam, O Lord of Karona! You are supreme among those who worship You by scattering fragrant flowers.

“You wear snakes as ornaments. O Honey residing in Thiru-Anaikka, where the Ponni river with its waves and sacred waters overflows! O Lord of the celestials! If I attain Your golden feet, what else can I, Your servant, do with this body?” “O Lord with the dark, jewel-like throat, who is half of the Mother! O Lord with hands holding a deer, a great battle-axe, and fire! O Kankala, who destroyed Yama’s body!

“You are the past and the future. O Red One, whose sacred body is unknown! O pinnacle of the race of gods! O Lord residing in Thiru-Anaikka! If I attain Your golden feet, what else can I, Your servant, do with this body?” “O Lord with the young, surrounding army, O Lord with eight shoulders! You are the nature of those who bow down, saying, ‘There is none but You everywhere.’ O Lord with the bow, who holds the great mountain of fire in His hand!

“O Fire-dancer residing in Thiru-Anaikka! May my heart not wander, afflicted by small ailments. If I attain Your sacred feet, what else can I, Your servant, do with this body?” “O Lord with the red matted hair adorned with celestial waters! O path of the Vedas! O Lord who consumed the poison from the fiery ocean! O Lord of countless glories!

“If I, Your servant, can always remember You with my tongue, saying ‘My Lord,’ and behold You with my eyes, and always bathe in the abundant waters of Thiru-Anaikka, surrounded by beautiful groves, O Lord! If I attain Your golden feet, what else can I, Your servant, do with this body?” “O Lord with the bull adorned with a banner! You dance while the goblins sing and dance. O Youth who holds the beautiful maiden! O Lord of Thiru-Anaikka, O Lord of Mahakalathi! If I, Your servant, can come and serve Your feet, which crushed the mighty shoulders and heads of the king of Lanka, surrounded by the ocean, what else can I, Your servant, do with this body?” 

“The third Thiru-Pathigam sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman for Thiru-Anaikka Sthalam is the sixty-third Thiru-Pathigam, Thiru-Thandaka Thiru-Pathigam, from the Sixth Thiru-Murai.

““I bathed in the abundant waters of Thiru-Anaikka, the Lord who wore the skin of the elephant, the one with an unaging mind, who made the mind and speech His own, who rode the bull, who is difficult to approach, who is the Father, my Lord, my Master, the one residing in Thiru-Anaikka, surrounded by the Kaveri with its fiery waves, the honey, the milk, the abundant waters.” “I bathed in the abundant waters of Thiru-Anaikka, the medicine, the one in the hearts of those who chant His name, the one with the crescent moon in His matted hair, the one who joyfully resides in my heart, the immortal, the unborn, the Lord of the Himalayas, the one who wore the skin of the fierce, intoxicated elephant, making Uma afraid, the one with the mighty battle-axe, the one who wandered from village to village seeking alms, the one residing in Thiru-Anaikka, the abundant waters. I bathed in the abundant waters of Thiru-Anaikka, the one with the unblemished white moon, the one who consumed the poison of the ocean and bestowed nectar upon the celestials, the one who is a relative and a support to all living beings, the inner meaning of Omkara, the one who created all worlds, the one who performs the act of creation, the one who destroyed the three cities of those who did not praise Him as the Lord, the one residing in Thiru-Anaikka, the abundant waters.” “I bathed in the abundant waters of Thiru-Anaikka, my Lord with the dark, jewel-like throat, the one with the white earring in His ear, the one with the garland of fragrant Konrai flowers, the one with the tiger skin as clothing, the one who is the great knowledge, beyond all else, the one with the jewel-adorned chest, the one with the matted hair, the one who is the chariot of the four divine Vedas, the one residing in Thiru-Anaikka, the abundant waters.” “I bathed in the abundant waters of Thiru-Anaikka, the truthful one without any falsehood, the virtuous one, the one who shot arrows at those who were not good, the one who is supreme in penance, the Lord who rides the bull, the one with the left hand, the one with the Kankala form, the one with the banner of the skull, the one with a body like fire, the red one, the one residing in Thiru-Anaikka, the abundant waters.” “I bathed in the abundant waters of Thiru-Anaikka, the one with the deer, the one with the battle-axe in His hand, the one who is a cluster of diamonds, the mountain of rubies, the one at the crown of my head, the one with the matted hair, the one who is stable with the ashes of the cremation ground, the one who strung the bow with the serpent as the string, the one who bent the Meru mountain as a bow to destroy the cities of those who did not remember Him, the one residing in Thiru-Anaikka, the abundant waters.” “I bathed in the abundant waters of Thiru-Anaikka, the primordial one, the sound of the fiery jewel, the one beyond the comprehension of the celestials, the supreme light, the meaning of the pure Vedas, the Brahmin who wore the ancient texts of flowers where bees gather, the one who taught righteousness, the one who cut off one of the five heads of Brahma, the one residing in Thiru-Anaikka, the abundant waters, with joy. I bathed in the abundant waters of Thiru-Anaikka, the one who rules the golden world for those who remember, praise, and extol the Lord of Kachi Ekambam without forgetting, the one with the army of Bhootha Ganas, the one who delights in dancing in the cremation ground, the one who desires alms, the one who shines like a coral cluster within my heart, the one residing in Thiru-Anaikka, the abundant waters.” “I bathed in the abundant waters of Thiru-Anaikka, the desired one, beyond the four Vedas, the one who protects from poverty and severe diseases, the one who is music, the one with countless virtues, the one who resides in Idai Maruthu and Eengoy, the one who rides the bull, the one who is the eight directions of the vast ocean, earth, sky, abundant fire, water, and wind, the one residing in Thiru-Anaikka, the abundant waters.” “He who looked at Kama and reduced his body to ashes, the one who was beyond the comprehension of Brahma and Vishnu in ancient times, the one who was like a blazing fire, the Lord of the celestials, the one who roared without fear.” Having destroyed the might of the Lankan king who lifted the mountain, and having relieved his distress then and there, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, praising and worshipping the Lord at Thiru-Anaikka, composes three Thiru-Pathikams. Sekkizhar Peruman then states: “Having worshipped the anklets that blessed the spider, and having sung many garlands of eloquent words, he bowed to the Lord of Thiru-Erumbiyur, whose matted locks shine.

“After singing, he worshipped the radiant Thiru-Chirappalli mountain, Thiru-Karkudi, and the prosperous Thiru-Paraythurai.” Thus, having worshipped the Lord of Thiru-Anaikka, who blessed the spider, and having sung Thiru-Pathikams, he then reached the sacred site of Thiru-Erumbiyur. After singing to the Lord there, he proceeded to Thiru-Chira- palli mountain and sang to Thayu-Mana Swamy there.

“Then, he proceeded to Thiru-Karkudi, also known as Uyyakkondan Malai, and sang a Thiru-Pathikam there. Afterwards, he reached the sacred site of Thiru-Paraythurai. All the places mentioned now are located near and within Thiru-Chirappalli. Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman visits all these places, praises the Lord, and sings Thiru-Pathikams.

“Let us continue our reflection.”
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 172 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 434. Thiru-Nindra Sarukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at Thiru-Anaikka, proceeds to the site known as Thiru-Erumbiyur, also called Thiru-Erumbur. This site, Thiru-Erumbur, is very close to Thiru-Chirappalli.

This sacred site, mentioned as Thiru-Erumbiyur in the Thevaram hymns, is located on the road from Thiru-Chirappalli to Thanjavur. It is near Thiru-Chirappalli and is a hill temple. According to legend, it is called Manikkoodam and Rathnakkoodam.

Furthermore, this site is also known by the names Thiru-Erumbipuram, Erumbeesam, Brahmapuram, Lakshmipuram, Madhuvanapuram, Rathnakkoodapuram, Manikkoodapuram, and Kumarapuram. These names are attributed to the worship of Brahma, Lakshmi, and Murugan. It is called Thiru-Erumbiyur in Tamil and Pipileeswaram in Sanskrit. Thiru-Erumbiyur is the place where the Devas worshipped the Lord in the form of ants. We saw that Thiru-Anaikka is the place where the elephant worshipped, and a spider also worshipped there.

Here, ants worshipped the Peruman. The temple faces east, situated on a hill. There are 115 steps from the bottom to the top. At the base, there is a circumambulatory path where chariot processions and festivals take place. On the hill, there are two circumambulatory paths: one inside the temple and another outside. Inside the inner circumambulatory path are shrines for Vinayagar and others, and in the outer circumambulatory path is the Amman temple.

The Vinayagar of this site is named Balachandra Vinayagar. The Moolamoorthy is known by the names Erumbeesar, Erumbeeswarar, Madhuvaneswarar, Manikkoodachala-pathi, Pipilikes- eeswarar, Manikkanaathar, and others. In inscriptions, names such as Thiru-Malai Azhwar, Thiru-Erumbur Azhwar, Thiru-Erumbiyurudaiya Nayanar, Thenkailayathu Mahadevar, and Adiththa Pattaragar are found. The names Pillaiyar Kshethra Baladevan and Pillaiyar Bhagavathi were given to some deities. Thiru-Navukkarasar refers to the Lord as a ruby on the mountain and a radiant flame in his Thiru-Thandagam. The Amman is known by names such as Narunguzhal Nayagi, Soundarya Nayagi, Madhuvanaveeswari, and Rathnambaal.

Now, regarding the sacred waters in the temple: Brahma Theertham, which is the temple tank in front of the temple, was established in the name of Brahma Devan. Since the sins of those who bathe in it are destroyed, it is called Pavanaasa Theertham. The float festival takes place in the month of Vaikasi, on the third day after the full moon. Next is Padma Theertham, which is located in the north-east direction of the temple, named after Lakshmi. The third is Madhu Theertham, named after the Devas. The fourth is Kumara Theertham, located north of the temple, named after Kumara Kadavul.

Additionally, there are Surya Pushkarani, Chandra Pushkarani, Kalyana Theertham, and other sacred waters. This site is praised as Then Kailayam and is said to be a fragment of Mount Meru. This temple, situated on a hill, is located amidst the fertile fields of the Marutham land. The Moolavar is a Swayambu Moorthy. Brahma, Thirumagal, Rathi, Indra, and other Devas, Agni, Murugan, Agasthiyar, Naimicha Munivar, and others have worshipped Lord Shiva at this site and received blessings. When Indra worshipped the Lord in the form of an ant, the Lord inclined His head and accepted it.

This is a unique glory of this site. The line “Kulichakkaiyan Erumbana Ahhrinaiyin Urukkodu” (He who took the form of an ant, a tiny creature) emphasizes this. It is also said that Karan worshipped here in the form of an ant. There are many inscriptions in this temple. Thiru-Kurunthogai and Thiru-Thandagam, hymns sung by Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar, are dedicated to this site. There is also a Purana called Thiru-Erumbiyur Puranam.

This temple is glorious in terms of Moorthy (deity), Thalam (place), and Theertham (sacred water). Inside the inner circumambulatory path of this temple, next to the kitchen, there is a tunnel, but no details about it are known. In the North Street, there is a monastery of a great saint named Sri Kattai Kali Swamigal. The surrounding temples for this temple are Kailasanathar Temple to the north, Vinayagar Temple at the base, and Arasu Kaaththamman Temple as the village deity temple.

After the festival for this Amman, the festival in the hill temple takes place. Abhishekam and Aradhanai are performed daily for the Lord and other deities in this temple during the four periods of morning, noon, evening, and night. Abhishekam is performed for the Moolalingam without water touching it. Annually, a grand ten-day festival takes place in the month of Vaikasi. The festival begins on the Punarpoosam star during the waxing moon and concludes with Theerthavari on the Visakam star, followed by palanquin festivals and float festivals on subsequent days.

Once upon a time, there was a demon named Tharukasuran. He waged war against Indra and captured Devaloka. Indra went to Brahma to complain, and Brahma told him to go to Thiru-Erumbiyur, the Southern Kailash on earth, and worship the Lord.

Accordingly, Indra and other Devas, fearing Tharukasuran, took the form of ants and reached this site. They worshipped the Lord and expressed their grievances.

The Lord appeared with Uma Devi, granted them darshan, and promised to alleviate their sorrows, commanding the Devas to stay at this place for some time. Accordingly, Indra, along with the host of Devas, came and worshipped Erumbiyur Eesan here with black water lilies. This was the Lord’s command.

Therefore, Indra, in the form of an ant, worshipped the Lord daily with a thousand black water lilies. The Lord, inclining His sacred head, accepted that worship. The Purana of this site states, “Even the great Indra, in the form of an ant, surrounded and praised Erumbeesam.” To make this known to the people of the world, the Lord even today grants darshan with His sacred head inclined. Agasthiyar, the sage of the Kumbha, married Lopamudra and embarked on a pilgrimage, visiting many sacred sites. He came to this Rathna Koodam, Thiru-Erumbiyur, on the southern bank of the Kaveri, bathed in the Kumara Theertham there, and worshipped Rathnachalanathar and Rathnambaal according to Agamic rites.

One day, the Lord appeared with His consort and blessed him.

At that time, Agasthiyar requested the Lord to impart spiritual knowledge to him.

The Lord blessed the sage, saying that Murugapperuman would impart the knowledge. Agasthiyar then worshipped Murugapperuman. Murugapperuman, with His consorts, appeared on His peacock vehicle, granted darshan, and imparted spiritual knowledge to Agasthiyar.

Thus, Murugapperuman taught Agasthiyar the three realities of Pathi, Pasu, and Pasam.

Here, Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman comes to this glorious sacred site of Thiru-Erumbiyur, also known as Thiru-Erumbur, and composes two Thiru-Pathikams. The first Thiru-Pathikam is the 74th Thiru-Pathikam of the Fifth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Kurunthogai Thiru-Pathikam.

“Virumbiyooruvidel madanenjame karumbinooral kandaay kalanthaarkkavan irumbinooral araathathor vendalai erumbiyoor malaiyaan engal eesane.” (O foolish heart, do not desire to wander; see the sweetness of sugarcane for those who mingle with Him. He is our Lord, the Lord of Erumbiyur mountain, with a skull that is not a mere iron skull.) “Pirangu senjadai pinagan penuseer karangu bootha ganamudai kannuthal” “Narunguzhal madavaalodu naadorum Erumbiyoor malaiyaan engal eesane.” (Our Lord, the Lord of Erumbiyur mountain, with fragrant locks, is with the young woman daily.) “Marunthuvaanavar thaanavarkku insuvai purintha punjadai punniyan kannuthal porunthu poonmulai mangai nallaalodum Erumbiyoor malaiyaan engal eesane.” (Our Lord, the Lord of Erumbiyur mountain, is the virtuous one with matted locks, who gave sweet taste to the Devas and Asuras, and is with the good maiden with adorned breasts.) “Nirangol kandathu ninmalan em mirai marangol ver kanni vaanuthal paagamay arampurintharul seytha em angnan Erumbiyoor malaiyaan engal eesane.” (Our Lord, the Lord of Erumbiyur mountain, is our pure Lord with a dark throat, who, with the beautiful-browed maiden as a part, performed dharma and bestowed grace.) “Narumpo nanmalar kondraiyum naagamum thurumbu senjadai thoomathi vaiththuvaan urumpon maalvarai pedaiyodu oorthorum Erumbiyoor malaiyaan engal eesane.” (Our Lord, the Lord of Erumbiyur mountain, with fragrant golden flowers, konrai, and snakes, with pure moon in His matted locks, wanders through towns with the golden mountain-like maiden.) “Karumbiyooruvana ainthula kaayaththil thirumbiyooruvana matrum palavula kurumbiyooruvathor kootagaththu inai Erumbiyoor aran seytha iyarkkaiye maranthu,” “Matrathu peridar naadorum thirumbi nee ninaiyel madanenjame puranjai kolak kurambaiyil ittu ena Erumbiyoor aran seytha iyarkkaiye inbamum pirappum irappum pinnodu thunbamum udane vaiththa sothiyaan anbane arane endru aratruvaarkku inbanagum Erumbiyoor eesane kanniraintha ganapavala thiral vinniraintha virisudar sothiyaan un nirainthu uruvaay uyiraay avan enniraintha Erumbiyoor eesane nirangol maal varai oon eduththalum narunguzhal madavaal nadukkai thida marangol vaalarakkan vali vaattinaan Erumbiyoor malai em mirai kaanmine.” (O foolish heart, do not daily remember other great sorrows; the nature that Erumbiyur’s Lord created, placing joy, birth, death, and sorrow together in this beautiful body, is the radiant one. He is the beloved Lord of Erumbiyur, who is sweet to those who cry out, ‘Beloved, Lord!’ He is the radiant light, full of coral clusters, filling the sky with spreading light.

He is the Lord of Erumbiyur, who fills your being, becoming your form and life. See our Lord, the Lord of Erumbiyur mountain, who, when the great mountain was lifted, and the fragrant-haired maiden trembled, crushed the strength of the mighty demon.) 

Now, the next Thiru-Pathikam by Thiru-Navukkarasu Peruman, the 91st Thiru-Pathikam of the Sixth Thiru-Murai, a Thiru-Thandaga Thiru-Pathikam.

“Panniya senthamizh ariyēn kaviyēn maattēn ennōdu panniraintha kalaigalāy thannai unthan thiraththu ariyā poriyilēnai than thiramum ariviththu neriyum kaatti annaiyaiyum aththanaiyum pōla anpāy adainthēnai thodarnthu ennai ālāk konda then Erumbiyūr malaimēl mānikkaththai sezhunjudarai senradaiya petrēn nānē.” (I do not know refined Tamil, nor am I a poet. I am an ignorant one who does not know your nature, though you are the arts that fill me. You made me know your nature, showed me the path, and like a mother and father, you lovingly embraced me, followed me, and made me your own. I have attained the ruby on the Southern Erumbiyur mountain, the radiant flame.) “Pazhungin nizhalul pathiththa sōthiyānai pasupathiyai pāsupatha vēdaththānai vizhinthazhuntha salantharanai vīttinānai vēthiyanai viņṇavanai mēvi vaiyam aḷanthavanai nānmukanai allal thīrkkum arumarunthai āmārariṇthu en uḷḷan theḷinthu Erumbiyūr malaimēl mānikkaththai sezhunjudarai senradaiya petrēn nānē.” (I have attained the ruby on the Erumbiyur mountain, the radiant flame, having understood and clarified in my heart that He is the light enshrined in the shadow of the fruit, the Pasupathi, the one in Pasupatha guise, who destroyed Salandharan who rose up, the Vethiyan, the celestial one, who measured the earth, the four-faced one, the rare medicine that removes suffering.) “Karuvai en than manaththiruntha karuththai gnāna kadunjudarai padinthu kidanthu amarar ēththum” “Uruvai aṇḍaththu oru muthalai ōtha vēli ulaki niṟai thoḻil iruthi naḍuvāy ninṟa maṟuvai venṟa kuḻal maḍavāḻ pākam vaiththa mayāṉaththu māsilā maṇiyai vāsaththiruverumbiyūr malaimēl māṇikkaththai seḻuñcuḍarai cenraḍaiya peṟṟēn nāṉē.” (I have attained the ruby on the fragrant Thiru-Erumbiyur mountain, the radiant flame, having worshipped the form that is the primal source of the universe, the one who stands in the middle of the ocean-girt world, the blemishless jewel in the cremation ground, who has the maiden with fragrant locks, who conquered blemish, as a part.) “Pakaḻi poḻinthu aḍalarakkar puṟaṅkaḷ mūṉṟum pāḻpaḍuththa parañcuḍarai paṟinthu taṉṉai pukaḻum anparkku iṉpamarum amuthai tēṉai puṇṇiyaṉai puvaṉiyathu muḻuthum pōka umiḻum ampoṟkuṉṟaththai muttiṉ tūṇai umaiyavaḷ tam perumāṉai imaiyōr ēttum tikaḻ erumbiyūr malaimēl māṇikkaththai seḻuñcuḍarai cenraḍaiya peṟṟēn nāṉē.” (I have attained the ruby on the shining Erumbiyur mountain, the radiant flame, having worshipped the supreme light who destroyed the three cities of the mighty Rakshasas with arrows, the nectar and honey that brings joy to devotees who praise Him, the virtuous one, the golden mountain that emits the entire world, the pillar of pearls, the Lord of Uma, praised by the celestials.) “Pāriḍaththudan pāḍappaṉiṟu naṭṭam payilvāṉai ayilvāy sūlam ēnti nēriḍum pōr mikavalla nimalaṉ taṉṉai nirmalaṉai ammalar koṇḍu ayaṉum mālum”

“Pāriḍanthum mēl uyarnthum kāṇāvaṇṇam paranthāṉai nimirnthu muṉi kaṇamēttum sīr Erumbiyūr malaimēl māṇikkaththai seḻuñcuḍarai cenraḍaiya peṟṟēn nāṉē.” (I have attained the ruby on the glorious Erumbiyur mountain, the radiant flame, having worshipped Him who dances with the Bhoothaganas, who holds the sharp trident, the pure one, the stainless one, who is very skilled in battle, whom Brahma and Vishnu could not see by digging down and rising up, who spread out, and whom the hosts of sages praise.) “Kārmukilāy poḻivāṉai poḻintha muṉnīr karappāṉai kaḍiya naḍai viḍaiyoṉṟu ēṟi ūrpalaṉum tirivāṉai ūradāka oṟṟiyūr uḍaiyaṉāy muṟṟum āṇḍu pēr eḻuththu oṉṟu uḍaiyāṉai nīḻnilavum an thīyum nīrum maṟṟai neṟiyilaṅku miku kālum ākāsamum vāṉilavu tārakaiyum maṇṇum viṇṇum maṇṇuyirum eṉṉuyirum tāṉāṉ sempoṉ āṇi eṉṟum añcaṉa mā malaiyē eṉṟum ampaḷa thiraḷ eṉṟum aṟinthōr ēttum seḻñerumbiyūr malaimēl māṇikkaththai seḻuñcoḍarai cenraḍaiya peṟṟēn nāṉē.” (I have attained the ruby on the glorious Erumbiyur mountain, the radiant flame, having worshipped Him who pours down like a dark cloud, who hides the ancient waters, who rides a swift bull and wanders through many towns, who owns Ottiyur as His town, who rules completely, who has a great name, who is the moon, fire, water, the mighty wind, sky, stars in the sky, earth, heaven, all earthly beings, and my own life, whom the knowing ones praise as a pure golden pillar, a great collyrium mountain, and a coral cluster.) “Aṟantariyā ūththaivāy aṟivil sinthai ārampa kuṇḍarōḍu ayarththu nāḷum maṟanthum” “Aṟanthiruvaḍikaḷ ninaiyamāṭṭā mathiyiliyēn vāḻvellām vāḻā maṇmēl piṟantha nāḷ nāḷalla vāḻā vīsaṉ pēr pithaṟṟi sīraḍimai thiṟaththul anpu seṟinthu Erumbiyūr malaimēl māṇikkaththai seḻiñcuḍarai cenraḍaiya peṟṟēn nāṉē.” (I, a foolish one with a foul mouth and ignorant mind, who daily forgets and cannot remember the sacred feet of dharma, my life is not a life; the day I was born on earth is not a day. I have attained the ruby on the Erumbiyur mountain, the radiant flame, having uttered the name of the Lord and filled with love for the path of sacred servitude.) “Aṟivilaṅku maṇaththāṉai aṟivārkaṉṟi aṟiyāthārtham thiṟattoṉṟu aṟiyāthāṉai poṟiyilaṅku vāḻaṟavum puṉainthupūṇḍa poṉṉiyaṉai poṟuthiraivāy nañcamuṇḍa kuṟiyilaṅkumiḍaṟṟai maḍaṟṟēn koṉṟaic caḍaiyāṉai maḍaitōṟum kamalamenpūccedi Erumbiyūr malaimēl māṇikkaththai seḻuñcuḍarai cenraḍaiya peṟṟēn nāṉē.” (I have attained the ruby on the Erumbiyur mountain, the radiant flame, having worshipped Him who has a shining mind, who is known only by the knowing and unknown by the ignorant, the golden one adorned with shining snakes, who swallowed poison from the ocean, whose throat has a shining mark, who has matted locks with konrai flowers, and whose lotus-like flower plants are in every channel.) “Arunthavaththiṉ peruvaliyāl aṟivathaṉṟi aḍal arakkaṉ thaḍavaraiyai eḍuththāṉ thiṇṭōḷ muṟinthu neṟinthu aḻinthu pāthāḷam muṟṟu muṉkai narampiṉai eḍuththukki” “Kītham pāḍa irunthavaṉai ēḻulakum ākkinaṉai emmāṉai kaimāviṉ urivaip pōrththa thirunthu eḻumpiyūr malaimēl māṇikkaththai seḻuñcoḍarai cenraḍaiya peṟṟē nāṉē.” (I have attained the ruby on the sacred Erumbiyur mountain, the radiant flame, having worshipped Him who was there to sing the song, who created the seven worlds, our Lord, who is covered with the hide of an elephant, after the mighty demon who lifted the great mountain had his strong shoulders broken, crushed, and destroyed, reaching the netherworld, and took out the nerve of his forearm.) 

We shall continue with our reflection.
Thiruchitrambalam.


Chapter 173 — Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar

Thiruchitrambalam.
Periya Puranam, Part 435. Thiru-Nindra Sarukkam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Nayanar Puranam. Thiru-Navukkarasu Swamigal, having worshipped at the sacred site of Thiru-Erumbiyur, proceeds to the temple of Thayu-Mana Swamigal, also known as Thiru-Chirappalli Mathrubhuteswarar.

There, he worships the Lord and sings Thiru-Pathikams. The Lord, Thayu-Mana Swamy, who is centrally enshrined on the hill in Thiru-Chirappalli, is famously known as Thiru-Chi Malai-Kottai. It is said that there is no one who does not know the Uchi Vinayagar (Ganesha at the summit) of this temple, as he is very famous. The Thiru-Pathikam sung by Thiru-Gnana Sambandha Peruman, beginning with “Nandrudaiyanai Theeyathilanai,” is dedicated to this site. A Thiru-Pathikam by Appar Swamigal is also dedicated here.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, in the twelfth Thiru-Pathikam, the general Thiru-Pathikam, mentions this site as a Vaippu-Thalam (a place mentioned in hymns) with the lines “Thengoorum Thiruchitrambalamum Chirappalli Paangur.” Manikkavasaga Peruman sang “Chirappalli Meviya Sivane Potri” in the Thiru-Vasagam Potri Thiru-Agaval. This site has many names such as Thiru-Chiramalai, Thiru-Chirapuram, Thiru-Chiragiri, Muththalaimalai, and Brahmagiri. The word ‘Palli’ means temple. This name Thiru-Chirappalli came about because a demon named Thirisiran ruled here, worshipped the Lord, and received blessings. Scholars also say that the name Thirisirapuram came about because this mountain has three peaks, namely the Swami, Amman, and Uchi-Pillaiyar. Since it is named after Brahma, it is called Brahmagiri, and because it appears like a bull when viewed from a distance, it is called Rishabachalam.

Due to its connection with Mount Kailash, it is specially referred to as Thenkailayam (Southern Kailash).
